# `d-SEAMS` {#d-seams}

**Author**

[d-SEAMS core team](https://dseams.info)

Load a LAMMPS frame and print nop, frame, and box.

CHILL+ four-neighbour star: cubic, hexagonal, interfacial, clathrate, interClathrate, or water.

Cage membership: HC is ice Ih, DDC is ice Ic, else water.

## Overview {#overview}

d-SEAMS 2.14 reads a molecular-dynamics trajectory and names the ice in it.
The name is Deferred Structural Elucidation Analysis for Molecular
Simulations. Release 2.14.0 of this repository is the C++ engine
`libyodaLib`, the C API `libseams` (`include/seams.h`), the header-only
C++ API `include/seams.hpp` (it links `libseams`), the C ABI
`libseams_lang` (`bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h`, used by the Python, R, and
Julia fronts), the `seams` command, and the LAMMPS, GROMACS, OpenMM,
PLUMED, and in-situ drivers. `gmx-seams` reads the trajectory `gmx mdrun` wrote.
The standalone PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in
[PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).
`seams --version` prints `2.14.0`.

See the [PLUMED](engines/plumed.md) page for the plugin.

CHILL+ labels an oxygen from its four-neighbour star: cubic, hexagonal,
interfacial, clathrate, interClathrate, or water. Cage membership is a
separate score. A molecule in a hexagonal cage (HC) is ice Ih. A molecule
in a double-diamond cage (DDC) is ice Ic. A molecule in neither is water.
Primitive rings and Steinhardt $q_l$ are computed in the same engine.
[CHILL+ versus cages](explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md) records
where the two scores disagree.

A source build from this tree, when the compilers are already on `PATH`,
is `meson setup build && meson compile -C build`.
pixi is `pixi run setup && pixi run build`.
[Install](getting-started/install.md) has each method.

The ice Ih frame shipped in this tree is `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`,
128 molecules of LAMMPS type 1.

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
```

`seams read` prints `nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073`.
`seams chill-plus` prints `nop 128 hexagonal 128`.
[The quick start](getting-started/quickstart.md) classifies an eight-atom cubic
cell from C and from Python.
[From a trajectory to the ice front](user/howto/from-trajectory.md)
adds the ring census on this frame and the ice front on
`input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj`.

Each other language is its own repository.
[Use a language binding](user/howto/bindings.md) names the package
and the library each one links.

- Python: `pydseamslib` (`import dseams`, `import pydseams`),
  with `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'` from
  [PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib)
- Lua and Fennel: `require("dseams")`, clone
  [yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct) and run `luarocks make` in the checkout
- R: `remotes::install_github("d-SEAMS/dseams-r")` from [dseams-r](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-r)
- Julia: `Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl")` from
  [Dseams.jl](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl)
- Rust: `cargo add dseams@2.14.0` from [dseams-rs](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-rs)
- Fortran: fpm Git dependency `dseams` from [dseams-fortran](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran)

[The 2.14.0 notes](reference/release-2.14.md) are the changes
since 2.13.0.
[Migrate from 1.x](user/howto/migrate-1x.md) maps `yodaStruct -c`
onto `seams`.

## Suite stack {#suite-stack}

`libyodaLib` reads a LAMMPS dump or an XYZ file. chemfiles
(`.pdb`, `.gro`, `.dcd`) and the `.con` reader are compiled in when
those libraries are found. The cutoff neighbour list is linkcell when
that library is built, and vesin otherwise. `seams --features` prints
which backends this binary has. The `seams` command, `libseams`, and
`libseams_lang` each link `libyodaLib`. `include/seams.hpp` links
`libseams`. Python and Julia link both libraries. R links
`libseams_lang`. Lua, Rust, and Fortran link `libseams`.

The user guide groups the tutorials and the how-tos by
task. The explanation pages are the background for those tasks.

Release notes and how to cite d-SEAMS.

The C++ header reference is
[*api-cpp*](https://docs.dseams.info/api-cpp/).

The numbers for OVITO, freud, ClavisCage TRACE, SQQ, and PLUMED are on
[Head-to-head](user/comparisons.md).
The sitting medians are on
[the sitting tables](explanation/performance.md).

# Getting started {#getting-started}

Install the engine, then classify one frame.

The install page builds `seams` 2.14.0 from a source checkout or with
pixi. The quickstart then classifies an eight-molecule cubic cell from
C and from Python, and reads the bundled TIP4P frame
`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` (250 oxygens, LAMMPS type 2). The
videos page is the recording of that run.

[Install the engine](install.md)[Quickstart](quickstart.md)[Videos](../videos/index.md)


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/getting-started/install.md -->

# Install the engine {#install-the-engine}

Release 2.14.0 provides the `seams` command, `libyodaLib`, `libseams`
(`include/seams.h`), and `libseams_lang` (`bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h`).
Build it from source or with [pixi](https://pixi.sh). Language
bindings live in their own repositories; the last section gives their
install commands.

## From source {#from-source}

You need a C++20 compiler, CMake, Python 3, Meson 1.3 or newer, Ninja,
pkg-config, and cargo with rustc 1.88 or newer. Eigen 3.4 must be
visible as the `eigen3` pkg-config module. conda-forge can supply
Meson, Ninja, pkg-config, and that Eigen:

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge meson ninja pkg-config 'eigen=3.4.*'
```

An unpinned `eigen` package on that channel currently resolves to
5.0.1. This release builds with Eigen 3.4. If pkg-config does not
find `eigen3`, Meson fetches the Eigen 3.4.0 wrap in the repository.

A default setup fetches vesin, gpulite, linkcell, minimage,
readcon-core, and readcon-db when those libraries are not already
installed. linkcell, minimage, and the two readcon projects need the
Rust toolchain above. When chemfiles is not already installed, setup
builds it with CMake. LAMMPS dump and XYZ files still read through the
native parsers when chemfiles is left out.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/d-SEAMS/seams-core
cd seams-core
git checkout v2.14.0
meson setup build --prefix="$HOME/.local" --libdir=lib -Dwith_tests=false
meson compile -C build
meson install -C build
```

`--prefix` is set at setup. `meson install` writes that prefix.
`--libdir=lib` places the shared libraries in `$PREFIX/lib`. Put
`$HOME/.local/bin` on `PATH`. The install writes `seams.pc`,
`seams-core.pc`, `seams-lang.pc`, and
`lib/cmake/seams/seams-config.cmake`. Point `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` at
`$HOME/.local/lib/pkgconfig` before compiling another program against
those files.

`-Dwith_tests=true` is the Meson default and builds the Catch2 suite.
`-Dwith_readcon=disabled` skips readcon-core and readcon-db.
`--wrap-mode=nodownload` makes setup fail instead of fetching a
subproject. Highway (`libhwy` 1.3 or newer) is optional. A setup that
does not find it leaves Highway off. The pixi environment below
provides it.

## pixi {#id1}

From a checkout of `v2.14.0`:

```bash
pixi run setup
pixi run build
./bbdir/seams --help
./bbdir/seams --features
```

The default environment includes Highway and chemfiles. Environments
`ira`, `sphericart`, `nauty`, and `mpi` add those libraries. Select one
by name:

```bash
pixi run -e ira build
```

The same `-e` flag takes `sphericart`, `nauty`, or `mpi`.

## OpenMP target offload {#openmp-target-offload}

The builds on this page leave `with_openmp_offload` disabled. The
NVIDIA build is [OpenMP target offload](../user/howto/openmp-offload.md).

## Verify {#verify}

With `seams` on `PATH`, from the checkout:

```bash
seams --help
seams --version
seams --features
seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
```

`seams --version` prints `seams 2.14.0`. The read of the bundled
trajectory prints `nop 250 frame 1 box 40 40 180.203`. `--features`
lists the backends compiled into that binary.

LAMMPS, GROMACS, OpenMM, and PLUMED hooks follow `-Dwith_lammps=auto`,
`-Dwith_gromacs=auto`, `-Dwith_openmm=auto`, and `-Dwith_plumed=auto`.
Each hook is built when its library is found. The engine pages are
[LAMMPS](../user/howto/engine-lammps.md), [GROMACS](../user/howto/engine-gromacs.md),
[OpenMM](../user/howto/engine-openmm.md), and [PLUMED](../user/howto/engine-plumed.md).
The standalone PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in
[PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).

## Language bindings {#language-bindings}

Each binding is its own repository. Use these install commands:

- Python: `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'` from
  [PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib).
- Lua and Fennel: clone [yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct)
  and run `luarocks make` in the checkout.
- R: `remotes::install_github("d-SEAMS/dseams-r")` from
  [dseams-r](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-r).
- Julia: `Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl")` from
  [Dseams.jl](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl).
- Rust: `cargo add dseams@2.14.0`, or
  `cargo add dseams --git https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-rs` from
  [dseams-rs](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-rs).
- Fortran: add [dseams-fortran](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran)
  as an fpm Git dependency.

[Use a language binding](../user/howto/bindings.md) lists what each one links.

# Quickstart {#quickstart}

Install the engine, classify one cubic cell, then read one LAMMPS frame.
Commands below are run from the repository root.

## Install {#install}

The build needs a C++20 compiler, Eigen 3.4, and Rust (linkcell,
minimage, and readcon). The install page pins conda-forge `eigen` to
the 3.4 series. An unpinned `eigen` package on that channel currently
resolves to 5.0.1, and this release builds with Eigen 3.4.

```bash
meson setup build -Dwith_tests=false
meson compile -C build
./build/seams --version
```

`-Dwith_tests=false` leaves out the test suite. The compile still writes
`./build/seams`, `libyodaLib`, `libseams` (`include/seams.h`), and
`libseams_lang`. `./build/seams --version` prints `seams 2.14.0`.

Source and pixi builds are on
[Install the engine](install.md).

The Python binding is
[PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib). `import dseams`
is the array API below, and `import pydseams` is the Frame API:

```bash
pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'
```

Every language is listed on
[Use a language binding](../user/howto/bindings.md).

## Eight cubic molecules {#eight-cubic-molecules}

The cell is the eight-atom diamond. The nearest-neighbour distance is
2.75 Å, so the cubic lattice constant is `2.75 * 4 / sqrt(3)`.

```python
import dseams
a = 2.75 * 4 / 3**0.5
sites = (
    (0, 0, 0),
    (0.5, 0.5, 0),
    (0.5, 0, 0.5),
    (0, 0.5, 0.5),
    (0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
    (0.75, 0.75, 0.25),
    (0.75, 0.25, 0.75),
    (0.25, 0.75, 0.75),
)
xyz = [[x * a, y * a, z * a] for x, y, z in sites]
labels, counts = dseams.chill_plus(xyz, [a, a, a])
print(int(counts[0]))
assert counts[0] == 8
```

`dseams.chill_plus` returns one label per atom and nine counts, in the
order of `seams_label_name`. Index 0 is cubic. The call uses the
published rule and the cutoff neighbour list at 3.5 Å. The program
prints `8`: every atom is cubic.

The same cell is `docs/examples/quickstart.c`. That program prints
`cubic 8`.

```bash
cc -I include -I build/src docs/examples/quickstart.c -L build/src -lseams -lm -Wl,-rpath,"$PWD/build/src" -o quickstart
./quickstart
```

`-I build/src` is the generated `seams_version.h`. The calls in that
file are:

```c
seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
seams_system_set_ortho(sys, xyz, 8, 0, 0, 0, a, a, a, NULL, NULL);
seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels, counts);
printf("cubic %d\n", counts[0]);
seams_system_destroy(sys);
```

`a` is the lattice constant, `xyz` is the 24 coordinates, `labels` is
one int per atom, and `counts` is nine ints. Index 0 is
`SEAMS_LABEL_CUBIC`.

## Read a frame {#read-a-frame}

`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` is one frame of 750 atoms: 250
oxygens and 500 hydrogens, 250 TIP4P waters. Type 2 is oxygen. Type 1
is hydrogen.

```bash
./build/seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
```

```default
nop 250 frame 1 box 40 40 180.203
```

`nop` is the number of atoms kept. `box` is the three bound spans, in
the file’s coordinate units. When `--type` is omitted, the reader keeps
type 2 if the file contains it, and type 1 otherwise. `--type 2` names
oxygen. On this file it prints the same line.

## CHILL+ and cages {#chill-and-cages}

```bash
./build/seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
./build/seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2 --graph mutual
./build/seams cages input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 interClathrate 9 water 241
nop 250 clathrate 1 interClathrate 7 water 242
nop 250 graph seeded hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 250
```

The lines are in command order. The first CHILL+ command uses the
cutoff list: every pair closer than 3.5 Å. `--graph mutual` keeps the
mutual four nearest neighbours, with candidates inside the cutoff plus
1.5 Å. `interClathrate` is the three-eclipsed star. It is a different
label from `interfacial`.

`seams cages` defaults to `--graph seeded`: mutual four-nearest seeds,
then union completions. `hexagonal` is the hexagonal cage, `cubic` is
the double-diamond cage, and `both` is an oxygen that belongs to both
cages. This frame has none of those cages. Cage membership is a different score from the
CHILL+ star. The walk-through is
[Classify ice on the mixed TIP4P example](../user/tutorials/bulk-ice.md).

## Other counts {#other-counts}

```bash
./build/seams rings input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
./build/seams steinhardt input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
./build/seams symmetry input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
```

`mW_cubic.lammpstrj` is 4096 atoms of type 1.

- [Primitive rings](../user/howto/rings.md)
- [Local q4 and q6](../user/howto/q4-q6.md)
- [The symmetry classifier](../user/howto/symmetry-classifier.md)
- [CHILL+](../user/howto/chill-plus.md)
- [Cages and TRACE](../user/howto/cages-trace.md)

## Backends {#backends}

```bash
./build/seams --features
```

The command prints `Compile-time features:` and one line per backend.
The names are OpenMP, MPI, Highway SIMD, vesin cutoff fallback,
linkcell pairs_within, chemfiles, readcon-core, readcon-db, IRA/SOFI,
spglib, sphericart, and nauty. Each line ends with `enabled` or
`disabled`. Which lines are enabled depends on the build. chemfiles is
the PDB, GRO, and DCD reader. readcon-core is the CON reader.

Frame, atom type, cutoff, and graph are flags, or the variables
printed by `./build/seams --print-config`. The names and the
precedence of `./seams.env` and `SEAMS_CONFIG` are on the
[seams CLI](../reference/cli.md) page.

The seams command reads ice Ih and prints the neighbour count, q6, published CHILL+, and the six-ring count.

## LAMMPS {#lammps}

LAMMPS run_hook scores five calls on the cubic cell, then one step on the ice Ih dump.

## OpenMM {#openmm}

OpenMM scores the ice Ih dump and prints the hexagonal count, the six-ring count, and q6.

The PLUMED driver scores the ice Ih dump and prints the hexagonal count, the six-ring count, and q6.

## In situ {#insitu}

The OpenMM how-to and the in-situ call score the ice Ih dump.

## Basal interface {#interface}

Published CHILL+ on the basal interface frame prints hexagonal 352 and water 434.

## Primitive rings {#rings}

The recording counts primitive rings on exampleTraj, then the six-rings of ice Ih.

## Cages {#cages}

The recording counts hexagonal cages on ice Ih, double-diamond cages on the cubic cell, and the sI, sII, and sH cages.

## Brine front {#brine}

The brine tutorial prints the ice front on three frames, then the paper frame of 864 waters and 9 ions.

## Nucleation {#nucleation}

The recording prints q6bar for frame 1 and frame 148 of the nucleation trajectory.

## Migrate from 1.x {#migrate}

# Classify ice on the mixed TIP4P example {#classify-ice-on-the-mixed-tip4p-example}

You classify one in-tree frame two ways: CHILL+ (a staggered or eclipsed star on each oxygen) and cage membership (hexagonal cage or double-diamond cage).
The result is a labeled oxygen set and a reason the two scores disagree.

## Prerequisites {#prerequisites}

- A seams-core checkout.
  Work from the repository root so `input/traj/` is a child.
- `seams` on `PATH`. `pixi run build` writes `./bbdir/seams`. `nix build` writes `./result/bin/seams`.
- The dump `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` (one frame, 750 atoms, 250 TIP4P waters; LAMMPS type 2 oxygen, type 1 hydrogen).

## Learning Objectives {#learning-objectives}

By the end of this tutorial you will be able to:

1. Read a LAMMPS dump with `seams read` and name the oxygen type.
2. Run CHILL+ and read the four-neighbour star histogram.
3. Run cages on the same oxygens and read HC / DDC membership.
4. State why the two scores disagree on this mixed frame.

## Step 1: Read the frame {#step-1-read-the-frame}

```bash
seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
```

```default
nop 250 frame 1 box 40 40 180.203
```

With no `--type`, a dump is read as oxygen: type 2 when that type is present, otherwise type 1.
Pass `--type 2` on the classifiers so the type is explicit.

## Step 2: CHILL+ from the CLI {#step-2-chill-from-the-cli}

CHILL+ labels each oxygen from the staggered and eclipsed bonds in its neighbour shell.
A bond is staggered or eclipsed from the pair correlation `c_ij`.
`--graph cutoff` (the default) bonds every pair closer than `--cutoff` (default 3.5 Å).
`--graph mutual` keeps a bond only when each oxygen lists the other among its four nearest.
The candidate search for that list uses `--cutoff + 1.5` as the cell-size hint.

The label needs a shell of exactly four neighbours. The star is then:

| label | condition |
| --- | --- |
| cubic | four staggered bonds |
| hexagonal | three staggered bonds and one eclipsed bond |
| clathrate | four eclipsed bonds |
| interClathrate | three eclipsed bonds |
| interfacial | two staggered bonds and a neighbour with more than two staggered bonds, or three staggered bonds, no eclipsed bond, and a neighbour with more than one staggered bond |
| water | any other star, including a shell that is not four neighbours |

`interClathrate` is the interfacial-clathrate label.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 interClathrate 9 water 241
```

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2 --graph mutual
```

```default
nop 250 clathrate 1 interClathrate 7 water 242
```

On the cutoff list, nine oxygens have three eclipsed bonds and the rest are water.
On the mutual list, one oxygen has four eclipsed bonds, seven have three, and the rest are water.
Neither list labels a cubic or hexagonal oxygen.

Original CHILL uses a narrower eclipsed window.

```bash
seams chill input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 water 250
```

## Step 3: Cages from the CLI {#step-3-cages-from-the-cli}

Cages ask a different question: does this oxygen belong to a complete hexagonal cage (HC, ice Ih, 12 waters) or a complete double-diamond cage (DDC, ice Ic, 14 waters)?
The search walks primitive six-rings.
The default graph is `--graph seeded`: mutual four-nearest seeds, then union completions.
An oxygen in both cage types is counted as `both`, not as hexagonal and not as cubic.
The four counts sum to `nop`.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 graph seeded hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 250
```

This mixed frame has no complete HC or DDC.

## Step 4: Why the two scores differ {#step-4-why-the-two-scores-differ}

CHILL+ is a four-neighbour star.
An oxygen is cubic or hexagonal when its four bonds look like ice, even when those neighbours do not close a cage.

Cages are topological unit matching.
An oxygen is ice Ih when it belongs to a hexagonal cage, and ice Ic when it belongs to a double-diamond cage.
Anything else is water, including a three-eclipsed star.

On this frame the cutoff list labels 9 oxygens `interClathrate`, and the mutual list labels 1 `clathrate` and 7 `interClathrate`.
The seeded cage score is 250 water.

The longer argument is [CHILL+ versus cages](../../explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md).

## Step 5: A cubic crystal {#step-5-a-cubic-crystal}

`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj` holds 11 frames of 4096 mW sites, type 1.
With no `--last`, the commands read frame 1.
Every site is cubic under CHILL+, and every site sits in a double-diamond cage.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
seams chill-plus input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
```

```default
nop 4096 graph seeded hexagonal 0 cubic 4096 both 0 water 0
nop 4096 cubic 4096
```

`--graph cutoff`, `--graph knn`, and `--graph knn-union` print the same cage counts, with that graph name on the line.
`seams chill-plus --graph mutual --type 1` also prints `nop 4096 cubic 4096`.
The mixed TIP4P frame is the one that separates the two scores.

## Step 6: Python {#step-6-python}

Install `pydseamslib` 2.14.0 with `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'` and import `from dseams import userframe`, the Frame over `libseams_lang`.

```python
from dseams import userframe as ds

frame = ds.read("input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj", atom_type=2)
print(frame.chill_plus())
print(frame.chill_plus(graph="mutual"))
print(frame.cages())
assert str(frame.chill_plus()) == "IceCounts(interClathrate=9, water=241)"
assert str(frame.chill_plus(graph="mutual")) == "IceCounts(clathrate=1, interClathrate=7, water=242)"
assert str(frame.cages()) == "CageScore(n_ih=0, n_ic=0, n_water=250)"
```

Those three lines are the cutoff histogram, the mutual histogram, and the seeded cage score from Steps 2 and 3.
The Frame walkthrough is the [Python Frame](../../reference/python-frame.md) page.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

- `nop 0` or an empty histogram: wrong `--type`.
  Mixed TIP4P in this tree is type 2.
  mW is type 1.
- Unknown command, exit 2: the binary is `seams`.
  The ice commands used here are `read`, `chill`, `chill-plus`, and `cages`.
- `ModuleNotFoundError: dseams`: install the binding with `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'`.

## Next steps {#next-steps}

- [Classify a dump you already have](../howto/classify-cli.md) (frame ranges, `--graph`, `--jobs`)
- [CHILL+ versus cages](../../explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md)
- [Python Frame](../../reference/python-frame.md)
- [The other language bindings](../howto/bindings.md)

## Summary {#summary}

You read one mixed TIP4P frame.
Cutoff CHILL+ printed 9 `interClathrate` and 241 water.
Mutual CHILL+ printed 1 `clathrate`, 7 `interClathrate`, and 242 water.
Seeded cages printed zero hexagonal, zero cubic, zero both, and 250 water.
A three-eclipsed star is not cage membership.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/ice-and-clathrate.md -->

# Ice and clathrate labels {#ice-and-clathrate-labels}

You label one frame two ways.
CHILL+ reads a staggered or eclipsed star.
A cage signature counts closed polyhedra of a given ring census.
Install `pydseamslib` 2.14.0 with `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'` and import `from dseams import userframe`, the frame over `libseams_lang`.

## The mixed TIP4P frame {#the-mixed-tip4p-frame}

`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` has 750 atoms and 250 oxygens (LAMMPS type 2).

```python
from dseams import userframe as ds

frame = ds.read("input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj", atom_type=2)
print(frame.chill_plus())
print(frame.chill_plus(graph="mutual"))
print(frame.cages())
assert str(frame.chill_plus()) == "IceCounts(interClathrate=9, water=241)"
assert str(frame.chill_plus(graph="mutual")) == "IceCounts(clathrate=1, interClathrate=7, water=242)"
assert str(frame.cages()) == "CageScore(n_ih=0, n_ic=0, n_water=250)"
```

`graph="cutoff"` is the default, the same neighbour list as `seams chill-plus`.
`graph="mutual"` is `seams chill-plus --graph mutual`.
The cage score is the seeded hexagonal and double-diamond membership: no cage is complete, so the water count is 250.
The CLI lines are `nop 250 interClathrate 9 water 241` and `nop 250 clathrate 1 interClathrate 7 water 242`.

## Cubic ice and an sI cage {#cubic-ice-and-an-si-cage}

`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj` frame 1 is 4096 mW sites.
The file holds 11 frames. `frame=1` selects the first.
Both the cutoff list and the mutual list label every site cubic, and every site sits in a double-diamond cage.

```python
from dseams import userframe as ds

ice = ds.read("input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj", frame=1, atom_type=1)
assert ice.n_atoms == 4096
assert ice.chill_plus().cubic == 4096
assert ice.chill_plus(graph="mutual").cubic == 4096
assert ice.cages().n_ic == 4096
assert ice.cages().n_water == 0
```

`input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj` is 46 waters, type 1.
`cages_by_signature("512")` is the $5^{12}$ census: 2 cages and 40 vertices.
`cages_by_signature("51262")` is $5^{12}6^{2}$: 6 cages and 46 vertices.

The default face-edge window is `2.65,3.15` in the coordinate units of the file.
These dumps are angstroms.
`edge="none"` is `--cage-edge none`: every ring the neighbour list already accepted can be a face.
On this sI cell the default and `none` return the same two cages.
The same agreement holds for the sII and sH files in [Classify a clathrate](clathrate.md).
The signature sets the ring depth. An extra `max_ring_size` on this frame is ignored.

```python
from dseams import userframe as ds

frame = ds.read("input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
found = frame.cages_by_signature("512")
assert len(found) == 2 and found.n_atoms == 40
found = frame.cages_by_signature("512", edge="none")
assert len(found) == 2 and found.n_atoms == 40
found = frame.cages_by_signature("51262")
assert len(found) == 6 and found.n_atoms == 46
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/clathrate.md -->

# Classify a clathrate {#classify-a-clathrate}

Hexagonal cages on ice Ih, double-diamond cages on cubic ice, and the sI, sII and sH census on the repeated cells.
The commands below use the unit cells in this tree.

GenIce builds the three empty clathrate hosts. The cage search is a signature census: closed polyhedra whose faces match a ring-size list.

| cell | file | waters | census |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sI | input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj | 46 | 2 of 5^{12}, 6 of 5^{12}6^{2} |
| sII | input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj | 136 | 16 of 5^{12}, 8 of 5^{12}6^{4} |
| sH | input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj | 136 | 12 of 5^{12}, 8 of 4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}, 4 of 5^{12}6^{8} |

The sH unit cell is 3 of $5^{12}$, 2 of $4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and 1 of $5^{12}6^{8}$.
The file is that cell four times, so the census is $12, 8, 4$.
sH is skewed: the dump stores an `xy` tilt.
sI and sII are orthogonal.

The default face-edge window is `2.65,3.15` in the coordinate units of the file.
These dumps are angstroms.
On all three files that window and `--cage-edge none` print the same cage counts.
`none` keeps every primitive ring the neighbour list already accepted, and the cage bound is the face census alone.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph cutoff --signature 512+51262
seams cages input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph cutoff --signature 512+51264
seams cages input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph cutoff --signature 512+sh+51268
```

```default
nop 46 graph cutoff signature 5:12 cages 2 atoms 40
nop 46 graph cutoff signature 5:12,6:2 cages 6 atoms 46
nop 136 graph cutoff signature 5:12 cages 16 atoms 136
nop 136 graph cutoff signature 5:12,6:4 cages 8 atoms 128
nop 136 graph cutoff signature 5:12 cages 12 atoms 136
nop 136 graph cutoff signature 4:3,5:6,6:3 cages 8 atoms 112
nop 136 graph cutoff signature 5:12,6:8 cages 4 atoms 120
```

`512` is $5^{12}$, `51262` is $5^{12}6^{2}$, `51264` is $5^{12}6^{4}$, `sh` is $4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and `51268` is $5^{12}6^{8}$.
The same three commands with `--cage-edge none` print these lines again.

![sI host with one methane in each cage.](../../_images/overlay-web2.png)

*sI with one methane in each cage. The census above is the empty host.*


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/classify-cli.md -->

# Classify a dump {#classify-a-dump}

You have a LAMMPS water dump and want counts. The flag table is
[seams CLI](../../reference/cli.md). Counts for the mixed TIP4P
frame are in [the mixed TIP4P tutorial](../tutorials/bulk-ice.md).
The CHILL+ rules are on [CHILL+](chill-plus.md).

Run the blocks below from a seams-core checkout, so `input/traj/`
resolves. On your own dump, pass the same flags with that path.

## One frame {#one-frame}

`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` is one frame of mixed TIP4P:
750 atoms, type 2 oxygen, type 1 hydrogen. The default cutoff is
3.5 Å.

```bash
seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
seams cages input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
seams rdf input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --cutoff 10
```

`read` prints `nop 250`. `chill-plus` prints `interClathrate 9 water 241`.
`cages` prints `water 250`.

`chill` is the original CHILL rule.
`chill-plus` is the published CHILL+ rule: a crystal row has exactly
four neighbours inside the cutoff, q3 is the mean over the four
nearest of them, and the Table 1 neighbour test stays on.
`chill_plus` is an alias of `chill-plus`.
`ovito-chill+` is the OVITO 3.17.2 rule: the same shell of four, q3
over that whole shell, and the neighbour test off.
`ovito_chill_plus` is an alias of `ovito-chill+`.
`--rule ovito-chill+` selects the OVITO rule on `chill-plus`.
A path given to `--rule` is read as text and scanned for a `rule` or
`chill-plus` key, written `rule:` or `rule =`. Comments are skipped.
When `--rule` is absent, `CHILL_PLUS_RULE` in the environment, or in
`./seams.env` when that file is loaded, is the same string.

`chill` and `chill-plus` read one neighbour list. The stored default
graph name is `seeded`, and both commands map that name onto the
cutoff list: every pair closer than `--cutoff`.
`--graph mutual` keeps the mutual four nearest neighbours.
`--cutoff` is the cell-size hint for that search.

## Type {#type}

`--type 0`, the default, keeps type 2 on a single LAMMPS frame when
any atom has it, and type 1 otherwise.
`--type` is that load filter.
`--water-types` is the neighbour mask: the mixed frame is loaded,
and ice is scored on the named LAMMPS types only. Substrate and ions
stay out of the neighbour list.
`--family` defaults to `waterIce`. `chill`, `chill-plus`, `cages`,
and `ions` exit 2 for every other family. The message names the family.

`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj` is single-site mW, type 1.
`input/traj/agi_water_tiny.lammpstrj` has water type 1 and ion types
3 and 4.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
seams chill-plus input/traj/agi_water_tiny.lammpstrj --water-types 1
seams cages input/traj/agi_water_tiny.lammpstrj --graph seeded --water-types 1
seams ions input/traj/agi_water_tiny.lammpstrj --ion-types 3,4 --water-types 1
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --family ionicLiquid  # exits 2
```

The family command prints `CHILL/TUM refused for family ionicLiquid`.
A dump with more than two LAMMPS types, and no `--family`, prints a
hint and still exits 0. The AgI commands above do that.
A triclinic dump uses the stored tilt. See
[Sheared cells](sheared-cells.md).

## Frame range {#frame-range}

Frames are 1-based. `--last` is inclusive. On a LAMMPS dump, a
`--last` past the end of the file stops at the last frame.
`--jobs` is the OpenMP worker count for that dump. `--jobs 1` is
serial. `mW_cubic.lammpstrj` has 11 frames.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --frame 1 --last 2 --jobs 2
```

## Bond graph for cages {#bond-graph-for-cages}

`seeded` is the default: mutual k-nearest seeds and the union of
each atom’s k nearest. `k` defaults to 4. `-k` sets it.
`--complete` fills the last vertex of a six-ring when the other
vertices already carry a label.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph seeded
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph seeded --complete
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph cutoff --cutoff 3.5
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph knn -k 4
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph knn-union -k 4
```

On that cubic cell each of the four graphs prints `cubic 4096`.

## Features of this binary {#features-of-this-binary}

```bash
seams --features
```

Each line is a compile-time switch, `enabled` or `disabled`.
OpenMP, chemfiles, and readcon-core are the switches the other
how-tos name.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/chill-plus.md -->

# CHILL+ {#chill}

Label every oxygen with the published CHILL+ rule, or with the OVITO
rule. Cage membership is a separate score. Why the two disagree is in
[CHILL+ versus cages](../../explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md).

## The default list {#the-default-list}

`seams chill-plus` bonds every pair closer than `--cutoff` (default
3.5 Å). The stored name of that default graph is `seeded`. CHILL and
CHILL+ map `seeded` onto the cutoff list. `--graph mutual` keeps the
mutual four nearest neighbours inside `--cutoff` + 1.5 Å. `seams cages` leaves `seeded` as its own two-list graph.

```bash
# excerpt: docs/orgmode/user/tutorials/bulk-ice.org
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
```

```bash
# excerpt: docs/orgmode/user/tutorials/bulk-ice.org
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2 --graph mutual
```

The cutoff list prints:

```default
nop 250 interClathrate 9 water 241
```

The mutual list prints:

```default
nop 250 clathrate 1 interClathrate 7 water 242
```

A count of zero is omitted. The names are the CHILL+ labels, including
`interClathrate`.

`--water-types` builds the neighbour graph on those LAMMPS types,
including pairs between them, and leaves every other atom
unclassified. A multi-atom dump with no `--type` infers the oxygen of
each molecule.

## The OVITO rule {#the-ovito-rule}

`--rule ovito-chill+` averages $q_3$ on the full cutoff shell and
skips the published neighbour test. `seams ovito-chill+` is that rule
as its own command. The C constants are `SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED` and
`SEAMS_CHILL_OVITO`. The 18-atom liquid fixture, and the 250 atoms
that change label on the 4096-molecule liquid, are on
[the published rule and the OVITO rule](../../explanation/chill-plus-rules.md).

## From the library {#from-the-library}

`seams_chill_plus` writes one label per atom and nine counts, one per
CHILL+ label.

```c
seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels, counts);
```

On the 64-atom cubic cell this published cutoff call labels every atom
`SEAMS_LABEL_CUBIC`. The OVITO rule on the mutual list does the same.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/symmetry-classifier.md -->

# The symmetry classifier {#the-symmetry-classifier}

Name the ice shell of each oxygen. The shell, the bond cutoff, and
the fit are on [Local symmetry](../../explanation/symmetry.md).
This page is the command and the library call.

## The CLI {#the-cli}

`seams symmetry` prints the matcher backend, a space-group line, one
shell overlay when a crystal shell matches, and a tally of the labels
that occur. `ice-Ih`, `ice-Ic` and `ice-Isd` appear when the frame
has them. Unmatched atoms are the last count:

```default
shells ice-Ic N unmatched U
```

The per-atom codes are ice Ih (0), ice Ic (1), stacking-disordered
(2), or -1. The command prints the names. Those labels, and the shell
overlay, come from the built-in shell kernel. The scale-free residual
ceiling on that kernel is 0.15.

The backend line is `ira` when the build linked IRA, and `kabsch`
otherwise. spglib supplies the space group when it is linked. A build
without spglib prints `space-group off`. A cluster that matches one
template also prints a `whole` overlay and a point-group line. The
point-group line is `off` when SOFI is not linked.

```bash
seams symmetry input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
```

The 4096-molecule cubic mW cell tallies `shells ice-Ic 4096 unmatched 0`.
The matching shell on that file is ice-Ic with rmsd 0.0119309, and the
overlay names its backend `kernel`.

## The library {#the-library}

`seams_frame_symmetry` writes the same integer labels. The second
argument is the residual ceiling. Pass 0.15 to match the command.
The declaration is:

```c
// excerpt: bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h
int seams_frame_symmetry(seams_frame *frame, double shell_rmsd, int *labels);
```

```c
seams_frame_symmetry(frame, 0.15, labels);
```

Python `dseams.symmetry` writes those labels from the same call.

# Rings, cages, and order {#rings-cages-and-order}

Primitive rings, cage signatures, Steinhardt parameters, and the neighbour list they share.

[Primitive rings](tutorials/rings.md)[Bond-orientational order parameters](tutorials/order-parameters.md)[Primitive rings](howto/rings.md)[Cages and TRACE](howto/cages-trace.md)[Local q4 and q6](howto/q4-q6.md)[Linkcell neighbours and carried updates](howto/linkcell-carried.md)[Cutoff neighbour lists](howto/neighbour-lists.md)[Choosing a cutoff and padding](howto/cutoff-padding.md)

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/rings.md -->

# Primitive rings {#primitive-rings}

The recording counts primitive rings on the mixed TIP4P frame, 511
rings, then the 256 six-rings of ice Ih.

A primitive ring is a cycle that passes Franzblau’s shortest-path test.
For every pair of vertices on the cycle, a shortest path between them
lies on the cycle. The worked example is on
[Primitive rings and the full graph](../../explanation/primitive-rings.md).

`seams rings` counts those rings on the cutoff neighbour list. The
default cutoff is 3.5 Å. The default deepest ring is 6.

## The mixed frame {#the-mixed-frame}

`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` has 750 atoms. Type 2 is the 250
oxygens. Type 1 is hydrogen.

```bash
seams rings input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --cutoff 3.5
```

```default
nop 250 rings 511
3 37
4 273
5 34
6 167
```

The histogram is 37 three-rings, 273 four-rings, 34 five-rings, and 167
six-rings. `--max-ring 8` prints the same histogram.

## Ice Ih {#ice-ih}

```bash
seams rings input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5
```

```default
nop 128 rings 256
6 256
```

The default census stops at six-membered rings. This cell has 256 of
them. A deeper `--max-ring` also reports larger rings. With
`--max-ring 12` the extra lines are `8 352`, `10 512`, and `12 512`.

![Five-rings and six-rings of the sI host.](../../_images/overlay-web.png)

*Five-rings and six-rings of the sI host, drawn on the oxygen cell.*


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/order-parameters.md -->

# Bond-orientational order parameters {#bond-orientational-order-parameters}

The local Steinhardt parameter of atom $i$ is

$$
q_l(i) = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{2l+1} \sum_{m=-l}^{l} |q_{lm}(i)|^2}
$$

with

$$
q_{lm}(i) = \frac{1}{N_b(i)} \sum_{j \in N(i)} Y_{lm}(\hat r_{ij}).
$$

$N(i)$ is every neighbour inside the cutoff. The Lechner-Dellago
average replaces $q_{lm}(i)$ with the mean of $q_{lm}$ over $i$
and its neighbours, then uses the same sum.

The library computes degrees 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12. `seams steinhardt`
prints the finite mean of each degree named by `--l`. The default list
is 4 and 6. Degrees 4 and 6 use the solid-harmonic kernel on that
cutoff list. Degrees 3, 8, and 12 are computed when `--l` names them.

## One mixed frame {#one-mixed-frame}

`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` has 750 atoms. Type 2 is the 250
oxygens. Type 1 is hydrogen.

```bash
seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 frame 1 box 40 40 180.203
```

```bash
seams steinhardt input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --cutoff 3.5 --l 3
```

```default
nop 250 q3 0.374897 q3bar 0.187542
```

`q3` is the mean of the finite local $q_3$ values. `q3bar` is the
mean of the finite Lechner-Dellago values. On this frame those means
are 0.374897 and 0.187542.

```bash
seams steinhardt input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --cutoff 3.5 --l 3,4,6,8,12
```

```default
nop 250 q3 0.374897 q3bar 0.187542 q4 0.693844 q4bar 0.648011 q6 0.420854 q6bar 0.33063 q8 0.587703 q8bar 0.481713 q12 0.51294 q12bar 0.341973
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/rings.md -->

# Primitive rings {#primitive-rings}

Count primitive rings on a frame you already have. The definition is
on [Primitive rings](../../explanation/primitive-rings.md). The
learning path is [the rings tutorial](../tutorials/rings.md).

## One frame {#one-frame}

`seams rings` prints `nop`, the number of primitive rings, and one
histogram row for each size that occurs. The neighbour list is the
cutoff list (default 3.5 Å). An orthorhombic cell uses the full CSR
of that list. `--type` keeps one LAMMPS type. On the mixed TIP4P dump
the oxygen is type 2. `--max-ring` is the largest ring (default 6).

```bash
# excerpt: docs/orgmode/getting-started/quickstart.org
seams rings input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 rings 511
3 37
4 273
5 34
6 167
```

## From the C API {#from-the-c-api}

`seams_rings_find` then `seams_rings_histogram` is the same census.
`counts[k]` is the number of primitive rings of size `k`. The buffer
must be longer than the largest ring. On a 64-atom cubic cell the
six-ring count is positive.

```c
seams_rings_find(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, 6, &rings);
seams_rings_histogram(rings, counts, 13);
```

## A trajectory {#a-trajectory}

A `--frame` / `--last` walk on one worker (`--jobs 1`, the default)
keeps one ring updater. A bond that did not change keeps its rings. A
changed bond recomputes the sources next to it. The census matches a
full search of that frame. `--rebuild` recomputes every frame. The
measured speedups are on
[Linkcell neighbours and carried updates](linkcell-carried.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/cages-trace.md -->

# Cages and TRACE {#cages-and-trace}

Ask which molecules sit in a complete ice cage, or which polyhedra
match a ring-size signature. TRACE, as run by ClavisCage, searches a
hydrogen-bond graph for hydrate polyhedra. The commands below are the
d-SEAMS counts.

## Ice cages {#ice-cages}

`seams cages` reports hexagonal cages (HC, ice Ih), double-diamond
cages (DDC, ice Ic), molecules that sit in both, and water. The
default graph is `seeded`: the mutual four-nearest list and the union
of each atom’s four nearest neighbours, both taken inside
`--cutoff` + 1.5 Å. The cutoff default is 3.5 Å. Water is every
selected molecule that is in neither complete cage.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
```

The mixed TIP4P frame, oxygen type 2, prints:

```default
nop 250 graph seeded hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 250
```

The 4096-molecule cubic mW cell prints:

```default
nop 4096 graph seeded hexagonal 0 cubic 4096 both 0 water 0
```

## A signature {#a-signature}

`--signature` names a face census. `512` is twelve pentagons and
prints `5:12`. `51262` is twelve pentagons and two hexagons and prints
`5:12,6:2`. Other names are `51264`, `51268`, `hc`, `ddc`, `sh`,
`sodalite` and `alpha`. The default face-edge window is `2.65,3.15`
in the coordinate units of the file. `--cage-edge none` keeps every
face from the ring census. `--guest-types` names the LAMMPS types of
guests. Each guest is assigned to the nearest cage center inside
`--guest-radius` (default 4.0). The language call is
`seams_frame_signature`. A window is `seams_frame_signature_edge`.

On the default graph name `seeded`, a signature search uses the union
list. The command below reads the structure I cell on the cutoff
graph, the oxygen list used for ice and for the TIP4P oxygens in the
TRACE comparison. Joining names with `+` prints one line per
signature. The cell is orthogonal, and `--cage-edge none` on this
command prints the same two lines.

```bash
# excerpt: docs/orgmode/user/tutorials/clathrate.org
seams cages input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph cutoff --signature 512+51262
```

```default
nop 46 graph cutoff signature 5:12 cages 2 atoms 40
nop 46 graph cutoff signature 5:12,6:2 cages 6 atoms 46
```

## TRACE {#trace}

ClavisCage 0.3.18 runs TRACE, the hydrogen-bond cage search of Hsu
and Lin, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025
([10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459)).
The two constructions are
[TRACE and signature cages](../../explanation/trace-assembly.md).
d-SEAMS counts $5^{12}$, $5^{12}6^{2}$ and $5^{12}6^{4}$ with
`seams cages --signature` and `seams_frame_signature`. It does not
call TRACE.

The comparison places hydrogens 0.96 Å from each oxygen along an
out-degree-2 orientation of the oxygen neighbour graph. TRACE then
uses its default 0.35 nm cutoff and a 35 degree angle. On ice and on
the TIP4P oxygens that graph is the 3.5 Å list. The dense frame
`input/traj/dump-l.lammpstrj` (512 atoms of type 1) has median degree
56 inside 3.5 Å. TRACE at 0.35 nm does not return on that shell, so
that frame is compared on the four nearest neighbours.

Ideal ice has no five-rings. `seams rings` on
`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` and on the cubic mW cell prints only
six-rings, so those three cages are absent. The clathrate cells,
where the cages are present, are the table on
[ClavisCage TRACE](../../explanation/clavis-trace.md). The ice
rows are in
[Literature head-to-head](literature-h2h.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/q4-q6.md -->

# Local q4 and q6 {#local-q4-and-q6}

Compute the local Steinhardt parameters on the cutoff shell. Degrees
4 and 6 use the solid-harmonic kernel. The Lechner-Dellago average is
printed beside each local mean.

## The CLI {#the-cli}

`seams steinhardt` prints one `qL` / `qLbar` pair for each degree
named by `--l`. The default is `4,6`. Degrees 3, 8 and 12 are
computed only when named. `--l 3,4,6,12` is the former four-degree
line. The neighbour list is the cutoff shell (default 3.5 Å).

```bash
# excerpt: docs/orgmode/getting-started/quickstart.org
seams steinhardt input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250 q4 0.693844 q4bar 0.648011 q6 0.420854 q6bar 0.33063
```

## The C API {#the-c-api}

`seams_q4q6` writes one local $q_4$ and one local $q_6$ per atom.
One of the two pointers may be null. Passing both null is an error.
On a 64-atom cubic cell the mean $q_6$ is above 0.3.

```c
seams_q4q6(sys, 3.5, 0, q4, q6);
```

`seams_frame_q4_q6` is the same pair on `libseams_lang`, and it can
also write the Lechner-Dellago averages. A null `q4bar` or `q6bar`
skips that average. The Python frame method is `q4q6`. The `q4_q6`
wrappers in the Python, R and Julia binding repositories call
`seams_frame_q4_q6`.

## Empty shells {#empty-shells}

An atom with no neighbour inside the cutoff keeps an empty
spherical-harmonic row. The kernel does not divide by a neighbour
count of zero, so the local $q_l$ and the Lechner-Dellago average
are both 0. freud and pyscal3 store NaN for that atom.

0 leaves the mean, CHILL+, and the nucleation $\bar q_6$ finite.
The neighbour count of that atom is already 0. There is no option
that writes NaN.

On the liquid comparison, an empty shell is 0 here and NaN in freud
and pyscal3. Every atom that has a shell matches pyscal3 to
$10^{-10}$.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/linkcell-carried.md -->

# Linkcell neighbours and carried updates {#linkcell-neighbours-and-carried-updates}

Build the cutoff neighbour list, then keep rings when only part of
the next frame moved. The scaling argument is
[Linkcell strong scaling](../../explanation/linkcell-scaling.md).
The list itself is
[Cutoff neighbour lists](neighbour-lists.md).

## The cutoff list {#the-cutoff-list}

`neighListO` builds one shared CSR with `nneigh::orthoFullCsr` when
the OpenMP team has more than one thread and the caller is outside a
team. The box is orthorhombic (length 3) or a restricted triclinic
dump (length at least 6). On one thread, and when that CSR call is
not taken, a linked linkcell fills the rows with
`linkcell::pairs_within`. vesin is the fallback when linkcell is
absent or the call fails.
`nneigh::preferSerialCutoff(true)` forces the one-thread builder.

Published CHILL+ calls `orthoFullCsr` on those boxes
(`chill::chillPlusPublishedCutoff`). Cutoff q4 and q6 do the same
(`chill::steinhardtQlCutoff`). The ring census reads the atom-ID rows.
The pair set does not depend on the thread count.

The half list keeps each pair on the lower index. The test that locks
this is the Catch2 case `half cutoff list is the lower index of the full list`:

```cpp
// excerpt: tests/test_neighbours.cpp
  REQUIRE(nneigh::orthoFullCsr(cloud, nullptr, 3.5, fullOff, fullCols, false));
  REQUIRE(nneigh::orthoFullCsr(cloud, nullptr, 3.5, halfOff, halfCols, true));
```

A skin reuses the wide list while every atom stays inside the Verlet
shell. Bonds are the pairs still inside the cutoff.

## Carried rings {#carried-rings}

A frame range on one worker visits frames in order through one
`FrameCarry`. `RingUpdater` redoes only the sources near a changed
bond. The result equals `ringNetwork` on that frame.

Carry is off for a single frame (`--last` omitted or equal to
`--frame`) and whenever `--rebuild` is set. On a LAMMPS dump,
`--jobs` above 1 also turns it off, because the frames are split
across workers. A non-dump range keeps one carry when `--jobs` is
above 1. More than one MPI rank on a dump leaves carry off as well.

The hop-ball test moves one atom across a periodic face and requires
the carried rings to match a full search, with fewer sources recomputed
than the atom count:

```cpp
// excerpt: tests/test_ring_hop.cpp
  const auto &carried = updater.update(moved);
  const auto full = primitive::ringNetwork(moved, 6);
  REQUIRE(carried == full);
```

## What was timed {#what-was-timed}

[Benchmarks](benchmarks.md) records both windows at 4096 molecules,
200 transitions, and eight threads. Every transition stayed inside the
hop ball, and the carried rings matched a full search. Speedup is
rebuild divided by carry.

The mW window (10 fs step) at 0.1, 1, and 10 ps is on that page. The
strict seeded graph there is the row `seeded-strict`.

The TIP4P/2005 ice/water slab (2 fs step) is finer: 0.01, 0.1, and
1 ps. An oxygen moves farther in one picosecond than an mW site. The
`seeded-strict` speedups are 8.31, 3.28, and 2.59.

```python
# excerpt: tests/cli_surface.py
        ["--frame", "1", "--last", "2", "--jobs", "1", "--rebuild", "read", cubic],
```

That argv is the walk with carry forced off. To keep the updater, drop
`--rebuild`, pass a `--last` past `--frame`, and leave `--jobs` at 1
on a dump.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/neighbour-lists.md -->

# Cutoff neighbour lists {#cutoff-neighbour-lists}

Build the cutoff list, choose the thread count, and read the pinned
session that compared it with vesin, freud, matscipy, mdapy, and OVITO.
The calls are on the [API map](../../reference/api.md).
The drivers are on [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md).

## Box {#box}

`nneigh::orthoFullCsr` reads `PointCloud.box`.

A length of 3 is orthorhombic. `box[0..2]` are `Lx, Ly, Lz`.
The minimum image on each axis is `dr - L * floor(dr / L + 0.5)`.

A length of at least 6 is a restricted triclinic LAMMPS dump.
`box[0..2]` are the bound spans `xhi_bound - xlo_bound` and so on.
`box[3..5]` are the tilt factors `xy, xz, yz` in the same length unit.
`boxLow` is the bound origin.
Any other length makes the call return false.
`gen::makeFracBox` recovers the edge lengths

- `lx = xspan - max(0, xy, xz, xy+xz) + min(0, xy, xz, xy+xz)`
- `ly = yspan - max(0, yz) + min(0, yz)`
- `lz = zspan`

and the perpendicular widths `wx, wy, wz`.
The cartesian image of a fractional shift `(sx, sy, sz)` is

- `x = lx * sx + xy * sy + xz * sz`
- `y = ly * sy + yz * sz`
- `z = lz * sz`

Cells are sized from those perpendicular widths.
When every axis has reach 1 and at least two cells, both boxes walk
the 27 image shifts filled once for that call.
A reach above 1 uses the fractional minimum image.
The pair is kept when the squared length is strictly below the cutoff
squared.

`nneigh::setBoxFromLammpsEdges` stores edge lengths plus tilt as that
dump box. A zero tilt stays three spans, so the orthorhombic loop is
unchanged. `seams read` prints the three bound spans. When the box has
six entries it appends `xy`, `xz`, and `yz`, each followed by its value.
There is no tilt flag.

## CSR {#csr}

`offsets` has length `nop + 1`.
`cols[offsets[i] .. offsets[i + 1]]` is sorted by cloud index and has
no self entry.
A null subset is every atom.
`half` keeps the pair only on the lower cloud index.
The pair set does not depend on the thread count.
The call returns false when the box is not usable.
Outside a parallel region the scratch stays allocated and is refilled
on the next call. Inside one, the call uses a local scratch.

`idRowsFromCsr` and `indexRowsFromCsr` put the atom itself first and
then the CSR partners, as atom ids or as cloud indices.
`halfIdRowsFromCsr` keeps the pair on the lower index.
`neighListO`, `halfNeighList`, and `getNewNeighbourListByIndex` build
this CSR and then those rows.

`CutoffSkin` builds candidates at `cutoff + skin`.
`update` calls `moved`. That is true when the atom count, the box, the
origin, or any minimum-image displacement exceeds `skin / 2`, and also
when the subset pointer or the half flag changes.
Otherwise `lastReused` is true.
`filter` then copies the wide CSR down to pairs still inside `cutoff`.
`moved` and `filter` are private. `offsets` and `cols` are the filtered
list.

`chill::classifyBondsCsr` labels the bonds of that CSR.
`chill::chillPlusFromCsr` keeps the four nearest of each row, accumulates
the real spherical harmonics at `l = 3`, and returns the cubic count.
`symm::diamondFromCsr` accepts the CSR and does not read it. The shell
kernel builds its own 3.5 Å bonds. A clean cubic shell is 1, a clean
hexagonal shell is 0, stacking-disordered ice is 2, and any other shell
is -1.
`chill::steinhardtQlCutoff` builds the CSR for one atom type and returns
`q_l`. The Lechner-Dellago average is filled only when `average` is true.
Degrees other than 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12 return zeros. `l = 12` runs on the
host.

## Threads {#threads}

`orthoFullCsr` sets `omp_set_dynamic(0)` and sizes its scratch for
`omp_get_max_threads`.
The thread count is `OMP_NUM_THREADS`.
`orthoFullCsr`, `CutoffSkin`, and the row converters take no thread
argument.
Outside a parallel region, an orthorhombic list whose subset has fewer
than 2048 atoms sets the team to one thread for that call and then
restores the previous count. A triclinic list leaves
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` as it was.
The parallel region starts at 256 atoms.
A call that is already inside an OpenMP region uses one thread.
The skin filter and the row converters use a parallel for from 256
atoms. The row converters skip that team when already inside one.
`nneigh::preferSerialCutoff(true)` keeps `neighListO` on the one-thread
builder.
The pinned session also sets `OMP_PROC_BIND=close`, `OMP_PLACES=cores`,
`OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE`, and `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE`, and pins the process
with `taskset` to cores `0 .. T-1`.

## Orthorhombic session {#orthorhombic-session}

Ice Ic, lattice constant 6.35 Å, cutoff 3.5 Å.
Each conventional cell holds 8 molecules, so the three frames are
10648, 110592, and 884736 molecules.
The full list has four neighbours per molecule, `4N` directed pairs.
Rows are sorted by cloud index.
The same checksum is produced at 1, 2, 4, and 8 threads.

The host is a KVM guest, kernel 6.12.113+, one socket, Intel Xeon
family 6 model 207 stepping 2, 8 cores, one thread per core, 2.4 GHz.
Caches are L1d 384 KiB, L1i 256 KiB, L2 16 MiB, L3 320 MiB, with 47 GiB
of RAM. The compiler is GCC 15.2.0, release `-O3`.
The guest does not expose hardware performance counters.
vesin is 0.6.2, freud is 3.6.1, matscipy is 1.3.1 with ASE 3.29.0.
Every code returned `4N` pairs. A later sitting, six calls and the
language API, is in [Literature head-to-head](literature-h2h.md). There the
one-thread vesin pool is 51.194 ms and an explicit eight-thread pool
is 22.269 ms, both full lists of 442368 pairs.

| molecules | threads | d-SEAMS CSR | d-SEAMS rows | vesin | freud | matscipy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10648 | 1 | 3.709 | 4.160 | 5.674 | 9.508 | 8.458 |
| 10648 | 8 | 0.968 | 1.241 | 2.375 | 9.575 | 9.215 |
| 110592 | 1 | 25.080 | 29.510 | 52.801 | 104.725 | 76.528 |
| 110592 | 8 | 4.554 | 6.077 | 18.159 | 37.994 | 79.412 |
| 884736 | 1 | 244.517 | 291.817 | 1073.681 | 1067.929 | 585.680 |
| 884736 | 8 | 35.618 | 49.400 | 176.231 | 1068.058 | 590.335 |

The d-SEAMS columns in this table, and the triclinic and orthorhombic
columns of the shared-stencil table, were measured in one session on
8 cores. Eight timed calls after one warmup. The process is pinned to
cores 0 .. T-1, with OMP_NUM_THREADS=T, OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE,
OMP_PROC_BIND=close, OMP_PLACES=cores, and OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE.
`bench_cutoff_list` times this orthorhombic CSR and, separately, the
`neighListO` atom-ID rows. `bench_v2` `tilt` and `ortho` time the
shared-stencil CSR. The median is the 5th of the 8 sorted samples. The
interquartile range (IQR) is the linear 75th percentile minus the
linear 25th, with rank (n-1)p. No host name is part of the record. The
vesin, freud, and matscipy columns are the earlier comparison, not
this session.

Orthorhombic CSR median (IQR) in milliseconds, 1 thread then 8:
10648 is 3.709 (0.280) and 0.968 (0.040);
110592 is 25.080 (0.222) and 4.554 (0.322);
884736 is 244.517 (4.625) and 35.618 (1.582).
The row medians (IQR) are 4.160 (0.179) and 1.241 (0.104);
29.510 (0.500) and 6.077 (0.959);
291.817 (12.147) and 49.400 (2.016).

```bash
meson setup build-release --buildtype=release -Dwith_tests=true \
  -Dwith_cli=true -Dwith_mpi=disabled -Dwith_openmp_offload=disabled
ninja -C build-release tests/bench_cutoff_list
NEIGH_BENCH=$PWD/build-release/tests/bench_cutoff_list \
  python3 scripts/bench_neighbours_threads.py
```

`bench_cutoff_list` arguments are the molecule count, the thread count,
and the number of timed repeats. It builds the CSR once before those
repeats. The Python callers in the script discard two builds before
the timed repeats. The comparison environment is vesin 0.6.2,
freud-analysis, matscipy, and ASE. NEIGH_PYTHON selects that
interpreter. Do not install the PyPI package named freud.

## Triclinic session, before the shared stencil {#triclinic-session-before-the-shared-stencil}

The same ice, with `xy = 0.25 L`, `xz = 0.05 L`, `yz = 0.12 L`.
Eight timed calls after one warmup. The median is again the 5th sample.
This shear does not change which molecules are neighbours: the checksum
matches the orthorhombic list.
The numbers below are the list before both boxes shared one stencil.
mdapy is 2.0.0 and OVITO is 3.17.2.
OVITO is timed with a new pipeline on every sample, because a pipeline
caches its output. `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` points at the system libGL

## Shared stencil {#shared-stencil}

At 110592 molecules the perpendicular widths give 42 by 43 by 43 cells,
against 43 cubed for the cube. Both reaches are 1, so both lists use the
27-cell stencil. The walks test 4,297,540 and 4,204,334 candidate pairs.
The 43.250 ms triclinic row above rebuilt the cell matrix for every
candidate. The shared stencil fills the 27 cartesian images once, and
both boxes call that loop. The d-SEAMS columns are the same 8-core
session as the orthorhombic table: eight samples, median the 5th, IQR
defined there. vesin and freud are the earlier comparison.

| molecules | threads | triclinic | orthorhombic | vesin | freud |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 110592 | 1 | 31.594 | 26.408 | 51.994 | 122.628 |
| 110592 | 8 | 6.879 | 5.136 | 24.911 | 127.350 |
| 884736 | 1 | 448.170 | 305.342 | 1141.327 | 1191.634 |
| 884736 | 8 | 69.177 | 51.959 | 203.597 | 1153.981 |

Shared-stencil CSR median (IQR), triclinic then orthorhombic:
110592 at 1 thread is 31.594 (0.576) and 26.408 (0.392);
at 8 threads, 6.879 (1.388) and 5.136 (0.206);
884736 at 1 thread is 448.170 (27.448) and 305.342 (0.788);
at 8 threads, 69.177 (3.783) and 51.959 (18.696).

CHILL+ on this CSR, the shell label, and the short-hop ring search:

Every molecule of this ice is cubic, so the CHILL+ cubic count is `N`.
The symmetry driver prints the atom count as its sink and the number of
labels other than -1 as its crystal count. Both are `N` on this ice.
The ring counts match mdapy: 221184 at 110592 molecules and
1769472 at 884736. The OVITO ring sink is the particle count, because
FindRings does not write a structure code. PTM has no cubic-ice
template, so its structure code is 0 on this crystal.

```bash
NEIGH_BENCH=$PWD/build-release/tests/bench_v2 \
  python3 scripts/bench_neighbours_v2.py
```

The script times `tilt`, `chill`, `rings`, and `symmetry`.
It does not time the unsheared cell. Those rows are
`bench_v2 ortho N T 8` under the same pin: N is the molecule count
and T is the thread count. Any mode other than `tilt` builds that
cell. The usage line names `tilt`, `chill`, `rings`, and `symmetry`.
Unset, NEIGH_BENCH points at `bbdir-release/tests/bench_v2`.
The Python samples call the function once, take an untimed result,
then time the repeats.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/cutoff-padding.md -->

# Choosing a cutoff and padding {#choosing-a-cutoff-and-padding}

The neighbour cutoff is the `--cutoff` of `seams chill-plus`.
The default is 3.5 Å. `SEAMS_CUTOFF` sets that default when the flag
is omitted.
Open-face padding is the `openFace` argument of `symm::classifyIce`,
`symm::classifyIceCloud`, and `symm::classifyIceArrays`.
It completes a short second shell on a bonded neighbour that has fewer
than four bonds. A full coordination shell is never padded.
The argument defaults to false.
`seams symmetry` calls `classifyIce` with that default, so the command
leaves the completion off.
CHILL+ stays the published rule. It does not take `openFace`.

Pass `openFace` true when the bulk-liquid rows record no added false
positive. On an interface, read the layers whose label changed before
treating the extra shell labels as ice. The classify timings are the
same bulk liquid with the completion off and on.

A false positive is a non-negative shell label on an atom CHILL+ does
not call cubic or hexagonal. `dseams_off` and `fp_off` are the
classifier with the completion off. `dseams_on` and `fp_on` are the
same frame with it on.

## The bulk-liquid gate {#the-bulk-liquid-gate}

padding adds no false positive on the bulk liquid; the open-face completion stays on

False positives off are `0` and false positives on are `0`.

## Summary rows {#summary-rows}

Each row is one `summary` record. `frame` is the number of
frames that row adds.

| lane | temperature_K | frame | molecules | chill_ice | dseams_off | dseams_on | fp_off | fp_on | kind_changed | agree_off | agree_on | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mw-bulk | 230 | 10 | 40960 | 108 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 40852 | 40852 | sum of the ten hold frames |
| mw-bulk | 300 | 10 | 40960 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 40941 | 40941 | sum of the ten hold frames |
| tip4p-basal | 230 | 10 | 14640 | 9390 | 8491 | 8669 | 13 | 16 | 178 | 13715 | 13887 | sum of the ten basal frames |
| T230_m0_r0_t0 | 230 | 1 | 1536 | 776 | 743 | 745 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 1503 | 1503 | one pinned brine frame |
| T230_m0_r0_t1 | 230 | 1 | 1536 | 844 | 511 | 511 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1199 | 1199 | one pinned brine frame |
| T230_m0_r0_t2 | 230 | 1 | 1536 | 832 | 539 | 539 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1243 | 1243 | one pinned brine frame |
| T230_m0_r0_tend | 230 | 1 | 1536 | 856 | 577 | 577 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1255 | 1255 | one pinned brine frame |
| T230_m20_r0_t0 | 230 | 1 | 1496 | 734 | 693 | 706 | 2 | 4 | 13 | 1451 | 1460 | one pinned brine frame |
| T230_m20_r0_t1 | 230 | 1 | 1496 | 698 | 420 | 426 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1218 | 1224 | one pinned brine frame |
| T230_m20_r0_t2 | 230 | 1 | 1496 | 698 | 447 | 447 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1241 | 1241 | one pinned brine frame |

# Interfaces, nucleation, and brine {#interfaces-nucleation-and-brine}

Ice fronts, a growing nucleus, and salt across the interface.

[Ice-water interface](tutorials/interface.md)[Nucleation](tutorials/nucleation.md)[Brine and NaCl](tutorials/brine.md)[Basal profiles and the nucleation census](howto/science-front.md)[From a trajectory to the ice front](howto/from-trajectory.md)[Ionic-liquid dumps](howto/ionic-liquid.md)

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/interface.md -->

# Ice-water interface {#ice-water-interface}

The recording labels this basal frame with published CHILL+: hexagonal
352, water 434, and the stack `HHHHHHHH....C.`

`input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj` is one frame, 864 molecules of type 1.

## Read the frame {#read-the-frame}

```bash
seams read input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1
```

```default
nop 864 frame 1 box 22.9883 21.6093 52.5093
```

## Published CHILL+ {#published-chill}

The default list bonds every pair closer than `--cutoff`. `--layers`
bins cubic and hexagonal molecules, including reCubic and reHex, along
`--axis`. Axis 2 is $z$.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5 --layers --axis 2
```

```default
nop 864 clathrate 3 cubic 1 hexagonal 352 interClathrate 25 interfacial 49 water 434
phi-c 0.00283286 stack HHHHHHHH....C.
```

phi-c is the cubic count divided by the cubic and hexagonal counts.
reCubic is counted with cubic, and reHex with hexagonal. This frame has
no reCubic or reHex molecules, so phi-c is 1/353, printed as 0.00283286.

The stack is one character per layer along $z$. The 52.5093 Å edge is
split into 14 layers of equal width. H means the hexagonal count in
that layer exceeds the cubic count, C means the cubic count exceeds the
hexagonal count, and a dot means the layer has neither. The string is
eight H, four dots, one C, and a final dot.

## The ice front {#the-ice-front}

The front uses a second binning: slabs of 3.7 Å from $z = 0$. A
molecule is crystal when its label is cubic, hexagonal, reCubic, or
reHex. This frame has 353 crystal molecules.

From 7.4 Å through 14.8 Å every water in those slabs is crystal: 39,
then 72, then 69. The fraction then falls through one half.

| start (Å) | crystal | waters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18.5 | 39 | 41 |
| 22.2 | 34 | 71 |
| 25.9 | 4 | 62 |
| 44.4 | 1 | 65 |

The crossing is at 22.035 Å, between the slab at 18.5 Å (39/41) and the
slab at 22.2 Å (34/71). Later slabs stay under one half. The slab at
44.4 Å holds the remaining crystal molecule.

![Basal interface colored by published CHILL+.](../../_images/overlay-web10.png)

*Basal interface colored by published CHILL+.*

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/nucleation.md -->

# Nucleation {#nucleation}

The recording reports mean q6-bar on the 148-frame mW trajectory.
The first of those frames has q6-bar 0.26063, the value printed below.

The full file is figshare
[10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1).
`input/traj/nucleation_three.lammpstrj` is its first three frames,
timesteps 15677000, 15678000, and 15679000. Each frame has 4096
molecules of type 1.

## Labels {#labels}

Crystal labels are cubic, hexagonal, reCubic, and reHex. These three
frames print cubic and hexagonal only.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/nucleation_three.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5 --frame 1 --last 3
```

```default
nop 4096 clathrate 20 cubic 47 hexagonal 62 interClathrate 138 interfacial 240 water 3589
nop 4096 clathrate 16 cubic 50 hexagonal 60 interClathrate 145 interfacial 227 water 3598
nop 4096 clathrate 16 cubic 44 hexagonal 69 interClathrate 147 interfacial 228 water 3592
```

The lines are frames 1, 2, and 3, in that order.

## Mean q6-bar {#mean-q6-bar}

```bash
seams steinhardt input/traj/nucleation_three.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5 --l 6 --frame 1 --last 3
```

```default
nop 4096 q6 0.493523 q6bar 0.26063
nop 4096 q6 0.493773 q6bar 0.260923
nop 4096 q6 0.495485 q6bar 0.261047
```

q6-bar is one number per molecule. On the first frame it does not
separate the 47 cubic molecules from the 62 hexagonal ones. The CHILL+
line above does.

## Largest crystal cluster {#largest-crystal-cluster}

Two crystal molecules share a cluster when the 3.5 Å cutoff list joins
them. The largest cluster is smaller than the cubic-plus-hexagonal
count. The other crystal molecules sit in other components.

| frame | cubic | hexagonal | largest cluster |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 47 | 62 | 59 |
| 2 | 50 | 60 | 64 |
| 3 | 44 | 69 | 70 |

On the first frame the cubic and hexagonal counts sum to 109, and the
largest component holds 59 of them.

![First nucleation frame, colored by published CHILL+.](../../_images/overlay-web11.png)

*First nucleation frame, colored by published CHILL+.*

# Brine and NaCl {#brine-and-nacl}

The recording follows an ice front through a short brine run, then this
864-water frame with nine ions.

`input/traj/nacl_front.lammpstrj` is the basal interface with nine ions
added. The dump has 873 atoms. Type 1 is the 864 waters. Type 3 is
chloride, five ions, and type 4 is sodium, four ions. The water
coordinates are the same as `input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj`.

`seams read` keeps the oxygen.

```bash
seams read input/traj/nacl_front.lammpstrj --type 1
```

```default
nop 864 frame 1 box 22.9883 21.6093 52.5093
```

## Water labels {#water-labels}

CHILL+ runs on the water, so an ion receives no ice label. The census
matches the ion-free frame.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/nacl_front.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5 --layers --axis 2
```

```default
nop 864 clathrate 3 cubic 1 hexagonal 352 interClathrate 25 interfacial 49 water 434
phi-c 0.00283286 stack HHHHHHHH....C.
```

## Which side of the front {#which-side-of-the-front}

Slabs are 3.7 Å along $z$, measured from the box origin. A water is
crystal when its label is cubic, hexagonal, reCubic, or reHex. A slab
is ice when at least half of its water is crystal.

The chloride at $z = 12$ Å is in the slab that starts at 11.1 Å.
All 72 waters in that slab are crystal. The other eight ions are in
slabs whose crystal fraction is under one half.

| start (Å) | ions | side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 11.1 | 1 chloride | ice |
| 33.3 | 1 chloride, 1 sodium | liquid |
| 37.0 | 1 chloride, 1 sodium | liquid |
| 44.4 | 1 chloride, 1 sodium | liquid |
| 48.1 | 1 chloride, 1 sodium | liquid |

The slab at 44.4 Å is on the liquid side of that cut and still holds
one crystal water, the same molecule counted on the ion-free interface.

![NaCl front. Water colored by published CHILL+, with sodium and chloride.](../../_images/overlay-web1.png)

*NaCl front. Water colored by published CHILL+, with sodium and chloride. The chloride in the ice slab has no ice label.*
