<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/science-front.md -->

# Basal profiles and the nucleation census {#basal-profiles-and-the-nucleation-census}

`science-front` reads a LAMMPS dump and writes either a basal layer
profile or a single-trajectory nucleation census. The cutoff is
3.5 Å. q6-bar is the Lechner-Dellago average on that ball, and the
ice cut is 0.36. CHILL+ is the published Nguyen and Molinero rule:
q3 over the four nearest neighbours, a crystal row of four
neighbours inside the cutoff, and the interfacial neighbour test.
The OVITO rule is a separate label. The calls are `layersOf`,
`nucleusOf` and `criticalSize`.

The critical size is an upper bound, not a committor. It is the mean
size of the largest cluster in the contiguous band around that
cluster’s minimum. The band stops where the size exceeds the minimum
by the larger of 5 molecules and 15 percent. A minimum in the first
two frames means the dump starts after the nucleus is already at
least that large. The interval is a percentile bootstrap of the mean.
It is not the probability that the cluster will grow.

## Basal slab {#basal-slab}

The frame in this repository is
`input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj`, 864 type-1 molecules, with
the long edge along z (52.509 Å). One frame writes the layer
profile:

```bash
science-front interface input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --bin 1 --out-dir science-out
```

`interface-layers.csv` is one row per bin.
`interface-fronts.csv` carries the 0.5 crossings and the 10-90
widths. On this frame both fronts are defined. The thickness is
24.816305 Å. The crossings are 0.297222 Å (width 3.036623 Å) and
25.113528 Å (width 5.290560 Å). A flat crystal, with no fall
through 0.5, leaves the front undefined.

On the same frame the published rule and the OVITO rule disagree
on 46 of 864 molecules: 5 on the neighbour test and 41 on the
four-neighbour q3 shell.

## The 148-frame mW census {#the-148-frame-mw-census}

The trajectory is figshare
[10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1),
148 frames of 4096 molecules, md5 `c28fc209a2854d2ba49e8f9b55accbe8`.
`input/traj/nucleation_three.lammpstrj` is its first three frames.
Place the full dump at
`data/science-frames/nucleation.lammpstrj` and run:

```bash
science-front nucleation data/science-frames/nucleation.lammpstrj --out-dir science-out
```

On that trajectory the largest extended cluster (cubic, hexagonal and
interfacial) has its minimum in the first two frames. The critical
size is 153.333 molecules, bootstrap 146 to 164, and `upper_bound`
is 1. The core cluster, cubic and hexagonal only, is 61.5 molecules
and is also an upper bound. The q6-bar cluster, cut at 0.36, has its
minimum later. Its size is 117 molecules and `upper_bound` is 0.
Each of these is the mean of the band around that series’ minimum.

The first three frames, in `input/traj/nucleation_three.lammpstrj`,
are the start of that series. The extended sizes are 177, 146
and 150. The core sizes are 59, 64 and 70.

On frame 2 the published rule and the OVITO rule disagree on 432 of
4096 molecules: 220 on the neighbour test, 207 on the q3 shell, and
5 mixed.

The functions are on [Science front](../../stable/science.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/from-trajectory.md -->

# From a trajectory to the ice front {#from-a-trajectory-to-the-ice-front}

You have a trajectory and want CHILL+ labels, the primitive rings,
and the position of the ice front. The commands below run on a
LAMMPS dump. When chemfiles is compiled in, the same commands also
read `.pdb`, `.gro`, and `.dcd`. `gmx-seams` reads the `.xtc` that
`gmx mdrun` wrote. The files you can run from this tree are the
LAMMPS dumps under `input/traj/`.

## Read the frame {#read-the-frame}

`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` is 128 molecules of ice Ih.
`input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj` is 864 molecules of a basal
ice-water interface. Type 1 is the water in both files.

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams read input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1
```

Ice Ih prints `nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073`.
The interface prints `nop 864 frame 1 box 22.9883 21.6093 52.5093`.

## CHILL+ labels {#chill-labels}

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
seams chill-plus input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5
```

Ice Ih is `hexagonal 128`. The interface is `hexagonal 352`,
`water 434`, `interfacial 49`, `interClathrate 25`, `clathrate 3`,
and `cubic 1`.

## Rings {#rings}

```bash
seams rings input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
seams rings input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1 --cutoff 3.5
```

Ice Ih has 256 rings, all of size 6. The interface has 1850 rings:
142 of size 3, 188 of size 4, 377 of size 5, and 1143 of size 6.

## The ice front {#the-ice-front}

`--layers --axis 2` bins the CHILL+ labels along z, the long edge
of the interface cell. The nominal layer width is 3.7 Å. The box
is split into `round(Lz / 3.7)` equal slabs, 14 slabs of 3.751 Å
on this cell.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1 --layers --axis 2
```

The census line is unchanged, and the command adds

```text
phi-c 0.00283286 stack HHHHHHHH....C.
```

`phi-c` is the cubic share of the cubic and hexagonal molecules,
1/353. The stack is eight hexagonal slabs, a gap, and one cubic
slab.

A fixed grid of 3.7 Å, counted from the same per-atom labels
(`--per-atom`), puts the crystal fraction at 0.95 in the slab that
starts at 18.5 Å and at 0.48 in the next slab. Crystal here is
cubic, hexagonal, `reCubic`, and `reHex`. That fraction crosses
one half at 22.03 Å.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/ionic-liquid.md -->

# Ionic-liquid dumps {#ionic-liquid-dumps}

An ionic-liquid dump is a multi-type frame, and CHILL is the wrong
score for the ions.
Keep CHILL and cages on water with `--water-types T` (the neighbour
mask). `--type` is the load filter. Use `seams rdf` for a partial
g_IJ(r) under the dump minimum image. Use `seams density-z`
for a type-resolved $\rho(z)$ in a slit.

The bundled frame `input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj` has 12 atoms of
LAMMPS types 1, 2, 3 and 4 in a 24 Å cube. When `--family` is omitted
and the loaded frame has more than two types, stderr prints

```text
hint: more than two LAMMPS types; set --family (default waterIce)
```

and the command still exits 0.

## Pick one type {#pick-one-type}

`--type` / `-t` selects the loaded type. `0`, the default, keeps type
2 when that type is present, and type 1 when it is absent.
`density-z` is the exception: `0` keeps every atom.
A dump whose species is not that guess needs the integer type.

```bash
seams read input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams read input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 3
```

The first command keeps type 2 and prints `nop 4 frame 1 box 24 24 24`.
`--type 3` keeps two atoms and prints `nop 2 frame 1 box 24 24 24`.

## Unlike-type neighbours {#unlike-type-neighbours}

`nneigh::neighListPair(rcut, cloud, typeI, typeJ)` builds I-J
pairs. `I == J` is the like-type list (`neighListO`). Distances
use `gen::periodicDistSq`, so a sheared dump box uses the same
MIC as the ice neighbour lists.

## Partial g(r) {#partial-g-r}

```bash
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 6.0
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 6.0 --bins 60
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 2 --cutoff 6.0
```

`--pair-types I,J` selects the pair. The default is `I = J = --type`,
a like-type g(r) of the guessed or requested species.
`--types` is a deprecated exact alias of `--pair-types` and prints
`--types is deprecated; use --pair-types`.
`--cutoff` is rmax. `--bins` is optional (default `rmax / 0.1`, so
60 bins at 6 Å).

Stdout is `# r g count`, then `# types I J rmax R bins N volume V`,
then one `r g count` row per bin. The normalization volume is
`det(H)` from the dump box. On this orthorhombic frame that volume
is 13824. Tilt `xy xz yz` enters H when the dump carries it. The
unlike-pair header is

```text
# types 1 2 rmax 6 bins 60 volume 13824
```

`seams rdf` is a pair histogram. CHILL and cages stay on water.

## Site kinds and ion vertices {#site-kinds-and-ion-vertices}

LAMMPS `type` is a column, and the chemistry lives in a
`site::Table` of type-to-kind (and optional atom-ID overrides).
`Table::of` looks up the override first, then the type, else
`unspecified`. `indicesOf(polar)` is the union of `cationHead`,
`anion`, and explicit `polar`; `indicesOf(apolar)` is `tail` plus
explicit `apolar`. `site::ionCloud` emits one vertex per `molID`
that carries a cation head or anion: the unweighted COM of those
tagged atoms, unwrapped with `gen::relDist` to the first atom of
the group, with `Point::type` 1 (cation) or 2 (anion). A long-chain
cation COM sits on the polar head, because the tail atoms are not
in that average. Family is an input on the table. Types do not
set it.

On that ion cloud, `nneigh::nearestUnlike(cloud, 1, 2)` is each
ion’s nearest unlike neighbour and the MIC distance.
`nneigh::mutualNearestUnlike` keeps the mutual edges. Those
are contact pairs. `seams cn` is the coordination number, from
the integral of $g(r)$.

## Polar and apolar domains {#polar-and-apolar-domains}

```bash
seams domains input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion,3=tail' --subset polar
seams domains input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion,3=tail' --subset apolar
```

`seams domains` builds the mask from `site::indicesOf` and walks
Stoddard’s clusters on that subset.
Neighbours are the dump-MIC cutoff list (`--cutoff`, default
3.5 Å). Stdout is `subset NAME n N largest L P`, and `P = L / N`.
On this frame the lines are `subset polar n 8 largest 4 P 0.5` and
`subset apolar n 2 largest 1 P 0.5`. Missing `--site` prints
`domains needs --site` and exits 2. `--family` applies to ice
scores. Domains ignore it.

## Confined layers {#confined-layers}

A slit or slab dump needs type-resolved $\rho(z)$.

```bash
seams density-z input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams density-z input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 1 --bins 80
seams density-z input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 2 --axis z
```

`--type 0` (default) histograms every atom. `--type I` keeps one
LAMMPS type. `--axis` is the Cartesian coordinate (`x`, `y`, or
`z`; default `z`). `--bins` is optional (default the bound span
over $0.1$, 240 bins on this 24 Å cube).

Stdout is `# z rho` then one row per bin. The slice volume is
$A_\perp \times dz$. $A_\perp$ comes from dump H (`ly*lz`
for `x`, `lx*lz` for `y`, `lx*ly` for `z`) using the recovered
edge lengths. The integral of `rho * A * dz` is the number of
selected atoms.

Confined IL work is this histogram plus the in-plane
`rdf2::rdf2Danalysis_AA` sampler.
`seams chill input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --family confinedIL` exits 2.

Molten salt is `seams rdf` / `cn` plus `ionCloud` when the melt
is multi-site. DES adds explicit donor H-bonds. Electrolyte is
ion–O rdf/cn plus water H-bonds. Silica / BeF2 is rdf/cn plus
Franzblau on the M–X graph and `getq6` on the tetrahedral
cation (`steinhardtQlVoronoi` otherwise).

## Read the box {#read-the-box}

`seams read FILE` prints `nop N frame F box Lx Ly Lz` and, when the
dump is triclinic (`box.size() >= 6`), the tilt `xy xz yz`. On
`il_tiny.lammpstrj` the default load prints `nop 4 frame 1 box 24 24 24`.
Bound spans are the edge lengths on this orthorhombic frame. A sheared
dump carries tilt as well. See [Sheared cells](sheared-cells.md).

## Family names {#family-names}

`--family` names the material. The default is `waterIce`.
`seams chill`, `chill-plus`, and `cages` exit 2 when `--family` is
`ionicLiquid`, `moltenSalt`, `des`, `electrolyte`, `confinedIL`,
`confinedWater`, or `networkFormer`. The message names the family.
For `ionicLiquid` it is `CHILL/TUM refused for family ionicLiquid`.
Unflagged `seams chill` stays the historical water path.

```bash
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 6.0
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 6.0
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --ions --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams pairs input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams domains input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion,3=tail' --subset polar
seams density-z input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 1 --bins 80
seams chill input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --family ionicLiquid  # exits 2
```

The coordination line is `# types 1 2 cutoff 6 cn 1.75 nI 4 nJ 4 volume 13824`.
The ion coordination line is `cage ionCloud types 1 2 cutoff 3.5 degree 1.5 nCation 4 nAnion 4`.
The contact line is `contact-pair count 4 nCation 4 nAnion 4`.
The last command exits 2.

Flags and the rest of the surface live on
[seams CLI](../../reference/cli.md). Formats live on
[data formats](../../reference/data-formats.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/confined.md -->

# Confined ice {#confined-ice}

Ice in a nanotube or a monolayer, and a triclinic cell whose edge lengths are not the bound spans.

[Confined water](tutorials/confined-water.md)[Quasi-one-dimensional ice](tutorials/nanotube.md)[Confined ice](howto/confined-ice.md)[Sheared cells](howto/sheared-cells.md)


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/confined-water.md -->

# Confined water {#confined-water}

Quasi-one-dimensional ice is a stack of prism blocks.
Quasi-two-dimensional ice is a sheet of primitive rings plus an in-plane radial distribution.

`seams prisms` counts perfect and imperfect prisms of size 3 to 6 on the mutual four-nearest graph.
`seams rdf` is the three-dimensional partial RDF.
The CLI has no command for the sheet census or the in-plane histogram.
Those two calls are on the Python frame.

The 2020 nanotube and monolayer dumps are figshare project 73545.
They are not in this repository, so this page does not give their counts.
The in-tree confined frame is `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` (250 oxygens, LAMMPS type 2).

## Prisms {#prisms}

```bash
seams prisms input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250
size 3 perfect 0 imperfect 0
size 4 perfect 51 imperfect 0
size 5 perfect 0 imperfect 0
size 6 perfect 0 imperfect 0
perfect 51 imperfect 0
```

Fifty-one perfect four-membered prisms, and no other size.
Ice Ih and frame 1 of the cubic mW cell are the contrast: every size prints perfect 0 and imperfect 0.
A hexagonal cage is not a prism block.

```bash
seams prisms input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --type 1
seams prisms input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
```

## Sheet rings and the in-plane RDF {#sheet-rings-and-the-in-plane-rdf}

Install `pydseamslib` 2.14.0 with `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'` and import `from dseams import userframe`.
Its sheet census uses the cutoff neighbour list.
Its prism rows are not the CLI line: size 4 is 50 perfect, where `seams prisms` prints 51.

`sheet_area` is the area the coverage fraction divides by.
Use the area of the sheet you loaded.
The ring counts do not use it.
With `sheet_area=1` the coverage number is the ring area itself.

```python
import tempfile
from dseams import userframe as ds

frame = ds.read("input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj", atom_type=2)
out = tempfile.mkdtemp()
r, g = frame.rdf_2d(out, cutoff=6.0, binwidth=0.5)
assert len(r) == len(g) == 12
assert round(max(g), 6) == 1.154771
sheet = frame.monolayer_rings(out + "/sheet", sheet_area=1.0, max_depth=6)
assert [sheet[n]["count"] for n in (3, 4, 5, 6)] == [37, 273, 34, 167]
prisms = frame.find_prisms(output_dir=out + "/prisms", max_depth=6)
assert prisms[1] == {"size": 4, "perfect": 50, "imperfect": 0}
```

The in-plane $g(r)$ has 12 bins of width 0.5 Å out to 6 Å.
The maximum is 1.154771 in the bin centred at 2.75 Å.
The sheet counts are the cutoff ring census: 37 three-rings, 273 four-rings, 34 five-rings, and 167 six-rings.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/nanotube.md -->

# Quasi-one-dimensional ice {#quasi-one-dimensional-ice}

A nanotube ice is a stack of prism blocks of one ring size.
`seams prisms` counts perfect and imperfect prisms of size 3 to 6 on the mutual four-nearest graph.
The 2020 nanotube trajectory is figshare project 73545.
It is not in this repository, so this page does not give that file’s prism count.

The in-tree confined frame is `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj`, 250 oxygens, LAMMPS type 2.

```bash
seams prisms input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
```

```default
nop 250
size 3 perfect 0 imperfect 0
size 4 perfect 51 imperfect 0
size 5 perfect 0 imperfect 0
size 6 perfect 0 imperfect 0
perfect 51 imperfect 0
```

Fifty-one perfect four-membered prisms.
Ice Ih (`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, type 1) and frame 1 of the cubic cell (`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj`, type 1) print perfect 0 and imperfect 0 on every size.
Those crystals are hexagonal cages and double-diamond cages.
They are not a prism stack under this count.

The sheet census and the in-plane RDF are [Confined water](confined-water.md).
Bulk CHILL+ and cages on the same mixed dump are [the mixed TIP4P tutorial](bulk-ice.md).
The Lua examples for a nanotube dump are [example_lua/iceNanotube](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct/tree/main/example_lua/iceNanotube) in yodaStruct.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/confined-ice.md -->

# Confined ice {#confined-ice}

Classify ice in a nanotube or a monolayer.

A nanotube is a stack of prism blocks. `ring::prismAnalysis` in
`topo_one_dim.hpp` writes those blocks. A monolayer is a sheet of
primitive rings. `ring::polygonRingAnalysis` in `topo_two_dim.hpp`
writes the sheet. Both headers are on the
[API map](../../reference/api.md).

`seams prisms` is a separate count: perfect and imperfect prisms of
ring size 3 to 6 on the mutual four-nearest graph (`ring::findPrisms`).
Nanotube blocks and monolayer sheets come from the two writers above.

The writers are on the Python Frame in pydseamslib 2.14.0.
With an output directory, `Frame.find_prisms` writes the nanotube
blocks through `prismAnalysis`. `Frame.monolayer_rings` writes the
sheet through `polygonRingAnalysis`. The calls, and a run on
`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj`, are in
[Python Frame](../../reference/python-frame.md) and
[Confined water](../tutorials/confined-water.md).
Bulk CHILL+ on that dump is
[the mixed TIP4P tutorial](../tutorials/bulk-ice.md).

Lua examples live under `example_lua/iceNanotube/`
(`shapeMatching` and `strictCriterion`) in
[yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct).

The 2020 trajectories are figshare project
[d-SEAMS Datasets](https://figshare.com/projects/d-SEAMS_Datasets/73545):
[Quasi-1D Nanotube LAMMPS Trajectory](https://figshare.com/articles/Quasi-1D_Nanotube_LAMMPS_Trajectory/11448768)
and
[Monolayer LAMMPS Trajectory](https://figshare.com/articles/Monolayer_LAMMPS_Trajectory/11448741).
Download them from those records.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/sheared-cells.md -->

# Sheared cells {#sheared-cells}

You have a triclinic LAMMPS dump and want the engine to use the
real cell, not a diagonal of bound spans.

A dump `ITEM: BOX BOUNDS` line is `lo hi [tilt]`. The reader stores
`hi - lo` per axis in `PointCloud.box[0..2]` and, when a third
number is present, appends `xy, xz, yz` so `box.size() >= 6`.
Those first three numbers are bound spans. They are not the
lattice edge lengths.

The engine recovers the restricted-triclinic matrix H (rows
$\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$) and the origin from
the spans, the tilt, and `boxLow`. Neighbour lists and every
minimum-image distance use that H. Wrapping each Cartesian axis
by `box[0]`, `box[1]`, `box[2]` is the wrong image on a sheared
cell.

The `seams` CLI has no tilt flag. A sheared dump is enough.
`seams read` prints the three bound spans and, when
`box.size() >= 6`, `xy xz yz`. `seams rdf` histograms
`rdf::partialRdf` with the same dump MIC; the ideal-gas volume is
`nneigh::dumpVolume` (`|det H|`, not the product of bound spans).
`seams density-z` takes $A_\perp$ from that H (`ly*lz` for `x`,
and so on), not from bound spans.
Type selection on a mixed dump is `--type I`; unlike-pair RDF is
`--pair-types I,J`. See [Ionic-liquid dumps](ionic-liquid.md).
The dump layout is on [data
formats](../../reference/data-formats.md).

## Recover H {#recover-h}

`nneigh::dumpBoundsToH` (and `lammpsBoxToLcCell` /
`lammpsBoxToLinkcell`) invert the LAMMPS bound mapping:

- `lx = xspan - max(0, xy, xz, xy+xz) + min(0, xy, xz, xy+xz)`
- `ly = yspan - max(0, yz) + min(0, yz)`
- `lz = zspan`
- origin is `boxLow` minus the same lower clip

`gen::periodicDistSq` / `gen::relDist` call
`gen::triclinicMinImage` when `box.size() >= 6`: fractional
coordinates relative to that origin, wrap the fractional
difference, map back through H. A length-3 `box` stays an
independent-axis wrap of the three spans.

## Neighbour lists {#neighbour-lists}

Cutoff lists (`nneigh::neighListO`, `neighList`, `halfNeighList`,
`getNewNeighbourListByIndex`, the vesin cell list, the brute
fallback, and `SkinNeighborList`) pass the dump 3x3 into the
minimum image. k-nearest lists (`kNearestNeighbourList`) build
the same H through `lammpsBoxToLinkcell`. Device ice-score
batches use `residentFrameCell`: `nBox >= 6` or a supplied
`boxLow` becomes one dump cell; three lengths stay ortho.

A pair that is only close across the `a` image of a sheared cell
is a neighbour at cutoff 1.0. Treating the bound span 15 as `lx`
misses that pair.

## Other MIC users {#other-mic-users}

The same dump H feeds Steinhardt flattening, hydrogen-bond
distances, cluster unwrap, and the in-plane RDF sampler.

`seams rdf FILE --cutoff RMAX` is the 3D partial $g_{IJ}(r)$.

```bash
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --cutoff 6.0
```

The in-plane sampler remains
`rdf2::sampleRDF_AA` on a `PointCloud`. `rdf::runningCN` and
`rdf::coordinationNumber` integrate `4 pi rho_J s^2 g ds` with
`rho_J = nJ / volume`; the cutoff is a caller input, not a
hard-wired first minimum.

## Empty or ortho clouds {#empty-or-ortho-clouds}

`box.size() < 3` yields an empty neighbour list. A length-3 box
is orthorhombic. An extended XYZ whose comment carries `Lattice=`
is read as that cell.

```bash
seams read templates/hc.xyz
```

That prints `nop 12 frame 1 box 53.969 54.529 51.257`. A triclinic H,
with tilt `xy xz yz`, comes from a LAMMPS dump.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/engines.md -->

# Engines {#engines}

Read a trajectory from LAMMPS, GROMACS, OpenMM, or PLUMED, or label the frame inside the run. The standalone PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in [PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).

[Run in situ](tutorials/insitu-run.md)[LAMMPS](howto/engine-lammps.md)[GROMACS](howto/engine-gromacs.md)[OpenMM](howto/engine-openmm.md)[PLUMED](howto/engine-plumed.md)[In-situ CHILL+](howto/engine-insitu.md)[OpenMP target offload](howto/openmp-offload.md)[Engine builds](../engines/index.md)[LAMMPS](../engines/lammps.md)[GROMACS](../engines/gromacs.md)[OpenMM](../engines/openmm.md)[PLUMED](../engines/plumed.md)[In-situ](../engines/insitu.md)[Engine walkthroughs](../walkthrough/index.md)

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/insitu-run.md -->

# Run in situ {#run-in-situ}

The recording scores the ice Ih cell: 128 hexagonal labels, 256
six-rings, and mean local q6 0.625855. The steps below run a cubic
crystal inside LAMMPS and inside OpenMM.

LAMMPS reads the 64-atom cell `engines/lammps/ice.data`. OpenMM builds
an eight-molecule cubic cell in angstroms.

## LAMMPS {#lammps}

The deck is `engines/lammps/in.dseams`. It reads `ice.data`, clears the
forces, and asks `fix external` for a callback every second step of an
8-step run. The driver is `engines/run_hook` in the build directory.
Run it from `engines/lammps` so `read_data ice.data` resolves. With the
`bbdir` directory from the build instructions:

```bash
cd engines/lammps
../../bbdir/engines/run_hook in.dseams
```

On success the first line has the form

```default
lammps calls N stride 2 ice M
```

$M$ equals $N$ times 64: every atom of this cell is cubic, and the
ice count adds the cubic labels from each callback. A second line
prints the hexagonal count, the six-ring count, and q6 of the last
callback. The hook is produced when the build finds a LAMMPS library.

## OpenMM {#openmm}

From the repository root:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=adapters/python python3 engines/openmm/test_reporter.py
```

The script builds eight molecules, takes two steps, and labels each
frame with CHILL+. When every label is cubic it prints

```default
openmm calls 2 ice 16
```

That is two frames of eight cubic molecules. The script needs OpenMM
and the language library on the loader path.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-lammps.md -->

# LAMMPS {#lammps}

Build `run_hook` against conda-forge LAMMPS from 2024.8.29 up through
the 2025 releases. Eigen and a C++ compiler need to be on the path.
The exports are the include and library paths of that prefix, including
the AVX directories conda-forge uses.

```bash
pixi init -c conda-forge dseams-lammps
pixi add --manifest-path dseams-lammps/pixi.toml "lammps>=2024.8.29,<2026"
eval "$(pixi shell-hook --manifest-path dseams-lammps/pixi.toml)"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX_256/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
export LIBRARY_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256${LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LIBRARY_PATH}"
export CPATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/include${CPATH:+:$CPATH}"
meson setup build -Dwith_lammps=enabled
meson compile -C build
```

`run_hook` registers a `fix external` callback. LAMMPS passes positions
in angstroms. On a data file written from
`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, with forces frozen, one callback prints:

```text
lammps hexagonal 128 six-rings 256 q6 0.625855
```

`engines/lammps/in.dseams` is the longer run. The cell is
`engines/lammps/ice.data`, 64 atoms of cubic ice, and the fix line is
`fix ext all external pf/callback 2 2`. With `run 8` the callback runs
5 times. The hook prints `lammps calls 5 stride 2 ice 320` and, for the
last call, `lammps hexagonal 0 six-rings 128 q6 0.628539`. The 320 cubic
labels are 5 calls of 64 atoms. The same coordinates classify as 64
cubic atoms, 128 primitive six-rings, and mean local q6 0.628539.

conda-forge LAMMPS ships `library.h`. This recipe builds `run_hook`.
The compute needs the class headers. The engine page says how to point
Meson at a LAMMPS `src` tree for that plugin.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-gromacs.md -->

# GROMACS {#gromacs}

Build `gmx-seams` against conda-forge GROMACS 2026.3, or a later 2026
release. Eigen and a C++ compiler need to be on the path. The exports
are the include and library paths of that prefix, including the AVX
directories conda-forge uses.

```bash
pixi init -c conda-forge dseams-gromacs
pixi add --manifest-path dseams-gromacs/pixi.toml "gromacs>=2026.3,<2027"
eval "$(pixi shell-hook --manifest-path dseams-gromacs/pixi.toml)"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX_256/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
export LIBRARY_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256${LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LIBRARY_PATH}"
export CPATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/include${CPATH:+:$CPATH}"
meson setup build -Dwith_gromacs=enabled
meson compile -C build
```

`gmx-seams` reads a trajectory in nanometers, multiplies the coordinates
and the box by 10, and classifies the frame. Convert
`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` to a one-frame `.gro` and run:

```bash
gmx-seams -f ice1h.gro -cutoff 3.5
```

The tool prints two lines. `ice` on the first is the cubic total over
every frame. `hexagonal`, `six-rings`, and `q6` are the last frame.
`overhead_s` is on the frames line and depends on the machine. This
cell has 128 molecules, all hexagonal, so the cubic total is 0 and the
last frame is:

```text
gromacs hexagonal 128 six-rings 256 q6 0.625855
```

`engines/gromacs/run_mdrun.sh` is a second path. It keeps the first
frame of `engines/gromacs/ice.gro` (the file has two), writes a frozen
`.tpr` with `nsteps` 4, runs `gmx mdrun`, and then runs `gmx-seams` on
the `.xtc` mdrun wrote. `gmx-seams` is a separate process after mdrun.
That first frame, converted from nanometers to angstroms, is 64 cubic
atoms, 128 primitive six-rings, and mean local q6 0.628539. The frames
line sums the cubic count over the frames in the `.xtc`.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-openmm.md -->

# OpenMM {#openmm}

Build the reporter against conda-forge OpenMM 8.6.1 or a later 8
release. Eigen and a C++ compiler need to be on the path. Configure
meson from that shell so `python3` imports `openmm`, and the plugin
looks for `libOpenMM` on the same prefix. The exports are the include
and library paths, including the AVX directories conda-forge uses.

```bash
pixi init -c conda-forge dseams-openmm
pixi add --manifest-path dseams-openmm/pixi.toml "openmm>=8.6.1,<9"
eval "$(pixi shell-hook --manifest-path dseams-openmm/pixi.toml)"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX_256/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
export LIBRARY_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256${LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LIBRARY_PATH}"
export CPATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/include${CPATH:+:$CPATH}"
meson setup build -Dwith_openmm=enabled
meson compile -C build
```

`DseamsReporter` reads the OpenMM context in angstroms and calls
`InSitu.observe`. Loading `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` onto
a Reference-platform context with a zero force and stepping once prints:

```text
openmm hexagonal 128 six-rings 256 q6 0.625855
```

The q6 mean is `seams_frame_steinhardt_graph` on the positions the
reporter classified, cutoff graph, degree 6.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-plumed.md -->

# PLUMED {#plumed}

The thread count comes from `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS`. Set that variable
before PLUMED starts. `OMP_NUM_THREADS` does not change the PLUMED team.
With `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS` unset, `PLMD::OpenMP::getNumThreads` returns
one thread.

The [d-SEAMS PLUMED plugin egg](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/)
(plumID:26.018) uses v0.4.1 of the
[dseams-plumed repository](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-plumed).
The build below uses PLUMED 2.9. A conda-forge LAMMPS package links
that release, so PLUMED 2.10 stays in its own environment.

Build `libSeamsPlumed.so` against conda-forge PLUMED 2.9. PLUMED 2.10
lives in its own environment, because a conda-forge LAMMPS package links
PLUMED 2.9. Eigen and a C++ compiler need to be on the path. The exports
are the include and library paths of the prefix, including the AVX
directories conda-forge uses.

```bash
pixi init -c conda-forge dseams-plumed
pixi add --manifest-path dseams-plumed/pixi.toml "plumed>=2.9.2,<2.10"
eval "$(pixi shell-hook --manifest-path dseams-plumed/pixi.toml)"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256/pkgconfig:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX_256/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
export LIBRARY_PATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/lib:$CONDA_PREFIX/lib.AVX2_256${LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LIBRARY_PATH}"
export CPATH="$CONDA_PREFIX/include${CPATH:+:$CPATH}"
meson setup build -Dwith_plumed=enabled
meson compile -C build
```

`SEAMS` components are `seams.q6` (mean local q6), `seams.ice` (cubic
fraction), `seams.ring` (fraction of atoms on a primitive six-ring),
`seams.hexagonal` (hexagonal count), and `seams.six` (six-ring count).
A `RESTRAINT` can bias `seams.q6`. The other four components have no
derivatives. A `PRINT` of `seams.q6` leaves the derivative array empty,
so the central difference runs only when a `RESTRAINT` has allocated it.

The plugin converts positions and the box from PLUMED’s length unit to
angstroms. With the default unit, nanometers, the factor is 10.
`CUTOFF` is always angstroms. Writing an xyz, in
nanometers, from `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` and running `plumed driver`
prints mean q6, the hexagonal count, and the six-ring count:

```text
plumed hexagonal 128 six-rings 256 q6 0.625855
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-insitu.md -->

# In-situ CHILL+ {#in-situ-chill}

`InSitu` in `adapters/python/dseams_insitu/engine.py` classifies one
frame during a run. `analyse(positions, box)` and
`observe(step, positions, box, ids)` call `seams_frame_chill_rings`.
`observe` also takes `types` and `copy_s`. `analyse_file(path, frame_index)`
reads a LAMMPS dump and calls `seams_frame_chill_plus` and
`seams_frame_rings`. `libseams_lang` is part of the default build.

```bash
meson setup build
meson compile -C build
```

A length-3 box is stored as `0, 0, 0, lx, ly, lz, 0, 0, 0`. Nine LAMMPS
numbers are copied through. Any other length is rejected.

The ice Ih dump is `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, 128 molecules of type 1.

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
seams rings input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
seams steinhardt input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --l 6
```

`seams read` prints:

```text
nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073
```

`seams chill-plus` prints `nop 128 hexagonal 128`. `seams rings` prints
`nop 128 rings 256` and then `6 256`, so every primitive ring has size

1. `seams steinhardt --l 6` prints `nop 128 q6 0.625855 q6bar 0.562449`.

Mean local q6 is 0.625855.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/openmp-offload.md -->

# OpenMP target offload {#openmp-target-offload}

Build the Steinhardt kernel and the TUM ice score (hop-bound
six-rings and cage affiliation) for an NVIDIA GPU. This build is
separate from the gpulite resident-batch path and from the host-only
pixi environment.

The Meson option is `-Dwith_openmp_offload=enabled`. Configure links
a real `target teams distribute parallel for`. The summary line
`OpenMP target offload` is YES only when that link succeeds. The probe
tries, in order, `-mp=gpu`, then `-mp=gpu -gpu=cc80`, then
`-mp=gpu -gpu=cuda12.2`, then `-mp=gpu -gpu=cc80,cuda12.2`, then
`-mp=gpu -gpu=cuda11.6`, then `-mp=gpu -gpu=cc80,cuda11.6`, then
`-fopenmp -fopenmp-targets=` plus the `offload_triple` option (default
`nvptx64-nvidia-cuda`). The first set that links is used on the compile
line and the link line. An HPC SDK that does not ship a toolkit
matching the driver still links when a `-gpu=cudaX.Y` set names a
bundled release. The 22.3 SDK ships CUDA 11.6. The 23.7 SDK ships
CUDA 12.2.

## Configure and build {#configure-and-build}

Configure with an NVIDIA HPC compiler or a Clang installation that
provides `libomptarget`:

```bash
export CXX=nvc++
meson setup build-offload --buildtype=debugoptimized \
  -Dwith_openmp_offload=enabled \
  -Dwith_mpi=disabled \
  -Dwith_gpulite=disabled
meson compile -C build-offload
```

For nvc++ 23.7 with Meson 1.4, pass `-Dcpp_std=none` and
`CXXFLAGS="-std=c++20"` when Meson does not list C++20 for that
compiler release.

## Runtime {#runtime}

Steinhardt, the TUM cage count, and CHILL+ each read `SEAMS_OFFLOAD`
with their own rule. `seams` loads the variable first and writes it
back before the command. Unset is written as `0`. The value `0`, and a
value whose first letter is `f` or `n`, stay off. Any other value,
including the word `off`, is written back as `1`.

A library caller that sets the variable itself sees the raw text:

- Steinhardt (`wantOffload` inside `steinhardtQl` and
  `steinhardtQlCutoff`) uses the device when
  `omp_get_num_devices() > 0` and the value does not start with `0`.
  Unset, seen directly, also uses the device. `l = 12` has no device
  harmonics and stays on the host. After `seams` rewrites the
  variable, unset therefore stays on the host. `seams steinhardt`
  reaches the device when that write is `1` and a device is present.
- TUM (`tum::preferOffload`) uses the hop-bound target kernels only
  when the variable is set, non-empty, and does not start with `0`,
  and a device is present. Otherwise `tum::cageCounts` stays on host
  `ringNetwork` (Franzblau) and `cageAffiliation`. `seams cages` on a
  cutoff graph or a mutual graph calls that path. The seeded graph
  stays on the host.
- CHILL+ (`chill::preferOffload`) is on when the variable is set and
  is not exactly `0`. `chill::chillPlus` then runs the flattened
  four-nearest tables, in a target region when a device is present.
  `seams chill-plus` does not call `chill::chillPlus`. Published
  cutoff CHILL+ stays on the host cell list.

`seams --features` prints the compile-time backends: OpenMP,
`linkcell pairs_within`, `vesin cutoff fallback`, and the rest of that
list. It does not print the offload define. The Meson summary line is
the record of the probe.

# LAMMPS {#lammps}

Meson builds `run_hook`, the in-run hook. It links `liblammps` and registers a
`fix external` callback. Every step the callback calls the same C API as
`seams chill-plus`. `engines/lammps/compute_dseams.cpp` is a per-atom style.
When `compute.h`, `atom.h`, and `lammpsplugin.h` are installed, Meson builds
it as `dseamsplugin.so` for `plugin load`. conda-forge LAMMPS installs
`library.h` only; `scripts/fetch_lammps_headers.sh DEST` checks out `src` of
the release that `lmp` reports and prints its path, and `-Dlammps_src_include=`
that path builds the plugin. Otherwise copy the file into a LAMMPS source tree. On several MPI ranks the compute gathers every
atom to rank 0, classifies the whole cell once, and returns each rank its
own labels, so the result does not depend on the domain decomposition.

`compute dseams` takes `cutoff` (angstrom), `graph` (`cutoff` or `mutual`),
`rule` (`published` or `ovito`), `type I` and `mol water`. `type I` scores the
group atoms of LAMMPS type I as water oxygens. `mol water` scores the type
that appears once in each multi-atom molecule and needs an atom style with
molecule IDs. The other group atoms read 6 (unclassified) and atoms outside
the group read -1. A group of several types that sets neither is an error,
so hydrogens and ions stay out of the CHILL+ graph. The deck’s `fix ext` line
is `external pf/callback`.

```default
# mW ice/liquid with compute dseams in situ. The dump carries the same
# coordinates at full precision for the offline CLI.
#   lmp -var plugin dseamsplugin.so -var cells 8 -var steps 200 -var every 10 \
#       -var melt 2000 -var dump insitu.lammpstrj -in in.mw.lmp
include mw_setup.lmp
plugin load ${plugin}
compute ice all dseams cutoff 3.5
dump d all custom ${every} ${dump} id type x y z c_ice
dump_modify d sort id format float %.17g
thermo ${every}
run ${steps}
```

```default
# Cubic ice, metal units (Angstrom). Forces are cleared so the cell does not melt.
# fix ext is the in-run hook. pf/callback 2 2 asks LAMMPS for d-SEAMS every 2 steps.
units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p p
read_data ice.data
mass 1 16.0
pair_style lj/cut 8.0
pair_coeff * * 0.1 2.75
velocity all set 0.0 0.0 0.0
fix freeze all setforce 0.0 0.0 0.0
fix ext all external pf/callback 2 2
thermo 2
timestep 0.001
run 8
```

```default
compute ice all dseams
dump 1 all custom 1 dump.chill id type x y z c_ice
run 0
```

```cpp
  double lo[3], hi[3], xy, yz, xz;
  int pflags[3], boxflag;
  lammps_extract_box(hook->lmp, lo, hi, &xy, &yz, &xz, pflags, &boxflag);
  const double box9[9] = {lo[0], lo[1], lo[2], hi[0] - lo[0], hi[1] - lo[1], hi[2] - lo[2],
                          xy, xz, yz};
  // frame_census calls seams_chill_plus.
```

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/engines/gromacs.md -->

# GROMACS {#gromacs}

`engines/gromacs/seams_ice.cpp` is a `TrajectoryAnalysisModule`. The binary
is `gmx-seams`. It reads a trajectory with the GROMACS reader. `analyzeFrame`
is the trajectory-analysis callback: it converts nm to Angstrom, calls
`seams_chill_plus`, and records the time. The runner invokes that callback
once per frame.

```bash
gmx-seams -f engines/gromacs/ice.gro -cutoff 3.5
```

`run_mdrun.sh` classifies the trajectory `gmx mdrun` wrote. Positions are
multiplied by 10 on the way into `seams_chill_plus`. The box conversion is
`gromacs_box_to_lammps` with the same scale.

```bash
(
  cd "$work"
  env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH -u LIBRARY_PATH \
    OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 GMX_MAXBACKUP=-1 \
    gmx grompp -f md.mdp -c ice.gro -p topol.top -o ice.tpr -maxwarn 2
  env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH -u LIBRARY_PATH \
    OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 GMX_MAXBACKUP=-1 \
    gmx mdrun -s ice.tpr -deffnm ice -nsteps 4 -ntmpi 1
```

```cpp
  void analyzeFrame(int, const t_trxframe &fr, t_pbc *, gmx::TrajectoryAnalysisModuleData *pdata) override {
    if (!fr.bX || !fr.bBox) {
      return;
    }
    const gmx::Selection &sel = pdata->parallelSelection(sel_);
    const int n = sel.posCount();
    if (n <= 0) {
      return;
    }
    std::vector<double> xyz(static_cast<std::size_t>(n) * 3);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      const auto &x = sel.position(i).x();
      xyz[static_cast<std::size_t>(3 * i)] = static_cast<double>(x[0]) * 10.0;
      xyz[static_cast<std::size_t>(3 * i + 1)] = static_cast<double>(x[1]) * 10.0;
      xyz[static_cast<std::size_t>(3 * i + 2)] = static_cast<double>(x[2]) * 10.0;
    }
    double raw[3][3];
    for (int a = 0; a < 3; ++a) {
      for (int b = 0; b < 3; ++b) {
        raw[a][b] = static_cast<double>(fr.box[a][b]);
      }
    }
    double box9[9];
    gromacs_box_to_lammps(raw, box9, 10.0);
    // frame_census calls seams_chill_plus.
    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const FrameCensus census = frame_census(xyz.data(), n, box9, cutoffA_);
    const auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    seconds_ += std::chrono::duration<double>(t1 - t0).count();
    frames_ += 1;
    if (!census.ok) {
      failed_ = true;
      return;
    }
    if (!dump_.empty()) {
      writeDump(fr.bStep ? static_cast<long long>(fr.step) : frames_ - 1, sel, xyz, box9,
                census.labels);
    }
    ice_ += census.cubic;
    atoms_ += n;
    hexagonal_ = census.hexagonal;
    six_ = census.six;
    q6_ = census.q6;
  }
```

`ice.gro` is two frames of the 64-atom cubic cell. The tool prints
`overhead_s`, the mean seconds per frame, and for the last frame
`gromacs hexagonal N six-rings M q6 Q`. `overhead_s` is machine-dependent.
A topology is not required.
`gmx-seams` runs after `gmx mdrun` and reads the trajectory that run wrote.
Biasing from inside mdrun goes through the
[d-SEAMS PLUMED plugin v0.4.1](plumed.md), which links the same C API.

`-select` picks the sites to classify; the default is every atom. A
multi-site water model needs its oxygens only, which takes a run input
file: `gmx-seams -s topol.tpr -f traj.trr -select 'name OW'`. `-dump file`
appends a LAMMPS dump frame per analysed frame with the coordinates
handed to d-SEAMS, in Angstrom, and the CHILL+ label. Molecules are not
made whole, so those coordinates are the ones in the trajectory.

GROMACS 2023 and later install neither the trajectory-analysis headers
nor the generated `libgromacs_export.h` they include. Point the
`gromacs_legacy_include` option at `api/legacy/include` of the GROMACS
source that matches the installed `libgromacs`; `engines/gromacs/compat`
supplies the export header. `gmx-seams` builds as C++17, as GROMACS does.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/engines/openmm.md -->

# OpenMM {#openmm}

There is one reporter, `DseamsReporter` in
`adapters/python/dseams_insitu/openmm.py`.
`DseamsReporter(engine, dump=None, interval=1, types=None)` asks
`describeNextReport` for positions every `interval` steps. `types` selects
which atoms are oxygens. `report` reads the context in angstrom and calls
`InSitu.observe`. With a `dump` path each report appends a LAMMPS dump
frame of the classified sites, keyed by 1-based particle index, with their
CHILL+ labels. `seconds` and `calls` time the reports.

```python
from dseams_insitu.engine import InSitu
from dseams_insitu.openmm import DseamsReporter

    engine = InSitu()
    reporter = DseamsReporter(engine, interval=1)
    simulation.reporters.append(reporter)
    simulation.step(2)
```

```cpp
    const auto &pos = state.getPositions();
    std::vector<double> xyz(static_cast<std::size_t>(n) * 3);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < static_cast<std::size_t>(n); ++i) {
      xyz[3 * i] = pos[i][0] * 10.0;
      xyz[3 * i + 1] = pos[i][1] * 10.0;
      xyz[3 * i + 2] = pos[i][2] * 10.0;
    }
    const double box9[9] = {0, 0, 0, a, a, a, 0, 0, 0};
    std::vector<int> labels(static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
    int counts[9] = {};
    seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
    seams_system_set_frame(sys, xyz.data(), n, box9, nullptr, nullptr);
    seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels.data(), counts);
    seams_system_destroy(sys);
```

`engines/openmm/test_reporter.py` builds an 8-atom cubic cell, a zero
external force, and the Reference platform, then steps twice. Every label
is cubic.

`plugin.cpp` is the C++ counterpart: an OpenMM `Context` on the Reference
platform takes the same two steps and calls `seams.h` directly after scaling
OpenMM nanometers by 10. Build it when `OpenMM.h` and `libOpenMM` are on the
link line.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/engines/plumed.md -->

# PLUMED {#plumed}

The [d-SEAMS PLUMED plugin egg](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/)
(plumID:26.018) uses v0.4.1 of the
[dseams-plumed repository](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-plumed).
The build below uses PLUMED 2.9. A conda-forge LAMMPS package links
that release, so PLUMED 2.10 stays in its own environment.

The thread count comes from `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS`. Set that variable
before PLUMED starts. `OMP_NUM_THREADS` does not change the PLUMED team.
The standalone PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in
[PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).

`SEAMS` is a collective variable with five components.

- `seams.q6` is the mean local q6. Its derivatives are a central difference, so
  `RESTRAINT` can bias it. A `PRINT` leaves that derivative array empty, and
  the difference runs only after a `RESTRAINT` has allocated it.
- `seams.ice` is the fraction of atoms published CHILL+ calls cubic. The label
  is discrete, so the component has no derivatives and is not biasable.
- `seams.ring` is the fraction of atoms on a primitive six-ring. It is not
  biasable either: a `RESTRAINT` on `seams.ice` or `seams.ring` is rejected
  because those components carry no derivatives.
- `seams.hexagonal` is the CHILL+ hexagonal count.
- `seams.six` is the primitive six-ring count.

`MODE=q6` computes only the mean local q6 and `MODE=q6bar` only the
mean Lechner-Dellago q6-bar, which has no derivatives. Neither runs CHILL+
or the ring search, and neither has the other four components. `DUMP=file`
appends one LAMMPS dump frame per call with the coordinates handed to
d-SEAMS, in angstroms, the per-atom q6 or q6-bar, and under `MODE=all` the
CHILL+ label. `seams chill-plus` reads that dump back.

```default
LOAD FILE=./libSeamsPlumed.so
seams: SEAMS ATOMS=1-64 CUTOFF=3.5
RESTRAINT ARG=seams.q6 AT=0.5 KAPPA=10.0
PRINT ARG=seams.q6,seams.ice,seams.ring FILE=colvar STRIDE=1
```

```cpp
bool SeamsCV::score(const std::vector<double> &xyz, const double box9[9], Score &out, bool keep) {
  const int n = static_cast<int>(xyz.size() / 3);
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  if (sys == nullptr || seams_system_set_frame(sys, xyz.data(), n, box9, nullptr, nullptr) != SEAMS_OK) {
    seams_system_destroy(sys);
    return false;
  }
  peratom_.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
  bool ok = true;
  if (mode_ == Mode::q6bar) {
    double mean = 0.0;
    ok = seams_q6bar(sys, cutoff_, 0, 0.36, peratom_.data(), peratom_.size(), &mean, nullptr,
                     nullptr) == SEAMS_OK;
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (double value : peratom_) sum += value;
    out.q6 = sum / static_cast<double>(n);
  } else {
    ok = seams_q4q6(sys, cutoff_, 0, nullptr, peratom_.data()) == SEAMS_OK;
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (double value : peratom_) sum += value;
    out.q6 = sum / static_cast<double>(n);
  }
  if (ok && mode_ == Mode::all && keep) {
    labels_.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
    int counts[9] = {};
    seams_rings *rings = nullptr;
    int hist[7] = {};
    ok = seams_chill_plus(sys, cutoff_, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED,
                          labels_.data(), counts) == SEAMS_OK &&
         seams_rings_find(sys, cutoff_, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, 6, &rings) == SEAMS_OK &&
         seams_rings_fraction(rings, 6, &out.ring) == SEAMS_OK &&
         seams_rings_histogram(rings, hist, 7) == SEAMS_OK;
    seams_rings_destroy(rings);
    out.ice = static_cast<double>(counts[SEAMS_LABEL_CUBIC]) / static_cast<double>(n);
    out.hexagonal = counts[SEAMS_LABEL_HEXAGONAL];
    out.six = hist[6];
  }
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  return ok;
}
```

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/engines/insitu.md -->

# In-situ {#in-situ}

d-SEAMS 2.14.0. `adapters/python/dseams_insitu/engine.py` is `InSitu`.
`InSitu(library=None, cutoff=3.5, graph="cutoff", max_ring=6, skin=0.0)`
builds one library handle. `graph` is `cutoff` or `mutual`. `skin` above
zero keeps the neighbour list while every oxygen has moved by at most half
that skin. `observe(step, positions, box, ids, types=None, copy_s=0.0)`
classifies one frame through `libseams_lang`. `types` selects the oxygen
indices. There is one OpenMM reporter class, `DseamsReporter`, in
`adapters/python/dseams_insitu/openmm.py`. It calls `InSitu.observe`.

Build:

```bash
meson setup build -Dwith_tests=true
meson compile -C build
```

`observe` stores a length-3 box as `0, 0, 0, lx, ly, lz, 0, 0, 0` and
classifies through `seams_frame_chill_rings`.

```python
box = np.array([a, a, a], dtype=np.float64)
engine = InSitu()
engine.observe(0, pos, box, ids=np.arange(8))
```

```python
    def _classify(self):
        self._fail(
            self.lib.seams_frame_chill_rings(
                ctypes.c_void_p(self._frame),
                ctypes.c_double(self.cutoff),
                ctypes.c_int(1),
                ctypes.c_char_p(self.graph.encode()),
                ctypes.c_int(self.max_ring),
```

# C tutorial {#c-tutorial}

Label the eight-atom cubic cell with `seams.h` and print the library version. The program is `docs/examples/ice.c`. It prints `2.14.0 cubic 8`.

```c
// Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
#include "seams.h"
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
  const double a = 2.75 * 4.0 / sqrt(3.0);
  const double fcc[4][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, 0, 0.5}, {0, 0.5, 0.5}};
  const double basis[2][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.25, 0.25, 0.25}};
  double xyz[24];
  int n = 0;
  for (int f = 0; f < 4; f++) {
    for (int s = 0; s < 2; s++, n++) {
      xyz[3 * n] = (fcc[f][0] + basis[s][0]) * a;
      xyz[3 * n + 1] = (fcc[f][1] + basis[s][1]) * a;
      xyz[3 * n + 2] = (fcc[f][2] + basis[s][2]) * a;
    }
  }
  int labels[8];
  int counts[9];
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  if (seams_system_set_ortho(sys, xyz, 8, 0, 0, 0, a, a, a, NULL, NULL) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels,
                       counts) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  printf("%s cubic %d\n", seams_version_string(), counts[0]);
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  return counts[0] == 8 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`seams.h` includes the generated `seams_version.h`. Meson compiles the program against `libseams` and records the library path in the binary.

```bash
cc -Iinclude -Ibuild/src docs/examples/ice.c -Lbuild/src -lseams -Wl,-rpath,build/src -lm -o ice
./ice
```

`docs/examples/core_counts.c` reads `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` and `input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj`. It returns 0 when Ice Ih is 128 hexagonal waters and 256 six-rings, and sII is 136 clathrate waters, 144 five-rings and 16 six-rings. The lines it prints are:

```default
hexagonal 128
rings6 256
clathrate 136
rings5 144
```

```c
// Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
/* Ice Ih and sII counts from the C core.
 *
 * input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj: 128 waters, all hexagonal, 256 six-rings.
 * input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj: 136 waters, all clathrate, 144 five-rings
 * and 16 six-rings. seams_chill_plus and seams_rings_histogram at 3.5 Å.
 */
#include "seams.h"
#include "seams_lammps_box.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static int read_dump(const char *path, double **xyz, int **types, int *n, double box9[9]) {
  FILE *in = fopen(path, "r");
  char line[512];
  int reading = 0;
  int cap = 0;
  if (in == NULL) {
    return 1;
  }
  *n = 0;
  *xyz = NULL;
  *types = NULL;
  while (fgets(line, sizeof line, in) != NULL) {
    if (strncmp(line, "ITEM: BOX BOUNDS", 16) == 0) {
      double bound_lo[3], bound_hi[3], tilt[3];
      int axis;
      for (axis = 0; axis < 3; ++axis) {
        char bound[128];
        if (fgets(bound, sizeof bound, in) == NULL) {
          fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
        tilt[axis] = 0.0;
        if (sscanf(bound, "%lf %lf %lf", &bound_lo[axis], &bound_hi[axis], &tilt[axis]) < 2) {
          fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
      }
      seams_lammps_bounds(bound_lo, bound_hi, tilt, box9);
    } else if (strncmp(line, "ITEM: ATOMS", 11) == 0) {
      reading = 1;
    } else if (reading) {
      int id, kind;
      double x, y, z;
      if (sscanf(line, "%d %d %lf %lf %lf", &id, &kind, &x, &y, &z) != 5) {
        break;
      }
      if (*n >= cap) {
        cap = cap == 0 ? 64 : cap * 2;
        *xyz = realloc(*xyz, (size_t)cap * 3 * sizeof(double));
        *types = realloc(*types, (size_t)cap * sizeof(int));
        if (*xyz == NULL || *types == NULL) {
          fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
      }
      (*types)[*n] = kind;
      (*xyz)[3 * *n] = x;
      (*xyz)[3 * *n + 1] = y;
      (*xyz)[3 * *n + 2] = z;
      *n += 1;
    }
  }
  fclose(in);
  return *n == 0;
}

static int classify(const char *path, int *n_out, int counts[9], int rings[13]) {
  double *xyz = NULL;
  int *types = NULL;
  int n = 0;
  double box9[9];
  seams_system *sys;
  seams_rings *found = NULL;
  int *labels;
  if (read_dump(path, &xyz, &types, &n, box9) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  labels = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(int));
  sys = seams_system_create();
  if (labels == NULL || sys == NULL ||
      seams_system_set_frame(sys, xyz, n, box9, types, NULL) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels,
                       counts) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_rings_find(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, 6, &found) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_rings_histogram(found, rings, 13) != SEAMS_OK) {
    free(labels);
    free(xyz);
    free(types);
    if (found != NULL) {
      seams_rings_destroy(found);
    }
    if (sys != NULL) {
      seams_system_destroy(sys);
    }
    return 1;
  }
  *n_out = n;
  seams_rings_destroy(found);
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  free(labels);
  free(xyz);
  free(types);
  return 0;
}

int main(void) {
  int n = 0;
  int counts[9] = {0};
  int rings[13] = {0};
  if (seams_set_num_threads(1) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (classify("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", &n, counts, rings) != 0 || n != 128 ||
      counts[1] != 128 || rings[6] != 256) {
    fprintf(stderr, "ice Ih n=%d hexagonal=%d rings6=%d\n", n, counts[1], rings[6]);
    return 1;
  }
  printf("hexagonal 128\n");
  printf("rings6 256\n");
  if (classify("input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj", &n, counts, rings) != 0 || n != 136 ||
      counts[4] != 136 || rings[5] != 144 || rings[6] != 16) {
    fprintf(stderr, "sII n=%d clathrate=%d rings5=%d rings6=%d\n", n, counts[4], rings[5],
            rings[6]);
    return 1;
  }
  printf("clathrate 136\n");
  printf("rings5 144\n");
  return 0;
}
```

The function list, status codes and buffer lengths are the [C API](../stable/c.md).

# C++ tutorial {#c-tutorial}

Classify the eight-atom cubic cell with `include/seams.hpp`, then the ice Ih dump. The program is `docs/examples/cpp_api.cpp`. Passed the repository root, it prints:

```default
cpp api cubic 8 q6 0.629 2.14.0
ice Ih atoms 128 hexagonal 128 q6bar 0.562448843702 shell_ih 128 pockets 0
```

```cpp
/* Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
 * Idiomatic seams.hpp on the eight-atom diamond and on ice Ih.
 */
#include "seams.hpp"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace {

std::vector<double> diamond8(double &edge) {
  const double a = 2.75 * 4.0 / std::sqrt(3.0);
  const double fcc[4][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, 0, 0.5}, {0, 0.5, 0.5}};
  const double basis[2][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.25, 0.25, 0.25}};
  std::vector<double> xyz;
  xyz.reserve(24);
  for (const auto &shift : fcc) {
    for (const auto &site : basis) {
      xyz.push_back((shift[0] + site[0]) * a);
      xyz.push_back((shift[1] + site[1]) * a);
      xyz.push_back((shift[2] + site[2]) * a);
    }
  }
  edge = a;
  return xyz;
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  try {
    seams::set_num_threads(1);
    if (seams::num_threads() != 1 || seams::version().empty()) {
      return 1;
    }
    double edge = 0;
    const auto xyz = diamond8(edge);
    seams::System cell;
    cell.set_ortho(xyz, edge, edge, edge);
    const auto cubic = cell.chill_plus(seams::ChillOptions{});
    const auto orders = cell.q4q6(3.5);
    double mean = 0;
    for (double value : orders.q6) {
      mean += value;
    }
    mean /= static_cast<double>(orders.q6.size());
    if (cubic.counts[0] != 8 || !(mean > 0.3)) {
      return 1;
    }
    std::printf("cpp api cubic %d q6 %.3f %s\n", cubic.counts[0], mean, seams::version().c_str());
    if (argc < 2) {
      return 0;
    }
    seams::System ice;
    ice.read(std::string(argv[1]) + "/input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", 1, -1);
    const auto labels = ice.chill_plus(seams::ChillOptions{});
    const auto q6 = ice.q6bar(seams::Q6BarOptions{});
    const auto shell = ice.symmetry(0.0);
    int n_ih = 0;
    for (int label : shell) {
      n_ih += label == 0 ? 1 : 0;
    }
    std::vector<int> flags(static_cast<std::size_t>(ice.count()), 1);
    const auto front = ice.brine(flags, seams::BrineOptions{});
    const auto pockets = front.pockets();
    std::printf("ice Ih atoms %d hexagonal %d q6bar %.12f shell_ih %d pockets %d\n", ice.count(),
                labels.counts[static_cast<std::size_t>(static_cast<int>(seams::Label::Hexagonal))],
                q6.mean, n_ih, pockets.pockets);
    if (ice.count() != 128 || labels.counts[1] != 128) {
      return 1;
    }
    if (std::abs(q6.mean - 0.562448843702) > 1e-9) {
      return 1;
    }
  } catch (const seams::Error &err) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "seams::Error %d %s\n", err.code(), err.what());
    return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}
```

`seams.hpp` includes `seams.h`, which includes the generated `seams_version.h`. Meson compiles the program against `libseams`.

```bash
c++ -std=c++20 -Iinclude -Ibuild/src docs/examples/cpp_api.cpp -Lbuild/src -lseams -Wl,-rpath,build/src -o cpp_api
./cpp_api "$PWD"
```

`seams::set_num_threads(0)` restores the OpenMP width captured at the first call, `omp_get_max_threads()`. A type of 0 or less on a frame whose atoms do not all share one positive type classifies a copy in which those atoms are given one type. That copy is `unified_copy` in `src/seams_api.cpp`.

`docs/examples/core_counts.cpp` checks the same Ice Ih and sII census. It prints `cpp hexagonal 128 rings6 256 clathrate 136 rings5 144` and returns 0 only when sII also has 16 six-rings.

```cpp
// Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
/* Same Ice Ih and sII census as core_counts.c, through seams.h. */
#include "seams.h"
#include "seams_lammps_box.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>

static int read_dump(const char *path, std::vector<double> &xyz, std::vector<int> &types,
                     double box9[9]) {
  FILE *in = std::fopen(path, "r");
  char line[512];
  int reading = 0;
  if (in == nullptr) {
    return 1;
  }
  while (std::fgets(line, sizeof line, in) != nullptr) {
    if (std::strncmp(line, "ITEM: BOX BOUNDS", 16) == 0) {
      double bound_lo[3], bound_hi[3], tilt[3];
      for (int axis = 0; axis < 3; ++axis) {
        char bound[128];
        if (std::fgets(bound, sizeof bound, in) == nullptr) {
          std::fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
        tilt[axis] = 0.0;
        if (std::sscanf(bound, "%lf %lf %lf", &bound_lo[axis], &bound_hi[axis], &tilt[axis]) < 2) {
          std::fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
      }
      seams_lammps_bounds(bound_lo, bound_hi, tilt, box9);
    } else if (std::strncmp(line, "ITEM: ATOMS", 11) == 0) {
      reading = 1;
    } else if (reading) {
      int id, kind;
      double x, y, z;
      if (std::sscanf(line, "%d %d %lf %lf %lf", &id, &kind, &x, &y, &z) != 5) {
        break;
      }
      types.push_back(kind);
      xyz.push_back(x);
      xyz.push_back(y);
      xyz.push_back(z);
    }
  }
  std::fclose(in);
  return xyz.empty() ? 1 : 0;
}

static int classify(const char *path, int &n, int counts[9], int rings[13]) {
  std::vector<double> xyz;
  std::vector<int> types;
  double box9[9] = {};
  if (read_dump(path, xyz, types, box9) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  n = static_cast<int>(types.size());
  std::vector<int> labels(static_cast<size_t>(n));
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  seams_rings *found = nullptr;
  if (sys == nullptr ||
      seams_system_set_frame(sys, xyz.data(), n, box9, types.data(), nullptr) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels.data(),
                       counts) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_rings_find(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, 6, &found) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_rings_histogram(found, rings, 13) != SEAMS_OK) {
    if (found != nullptr) {
      seams_rings_destroy(found);
    }
    if (sys != nullptr) {
      seams_system_destroy(sys);
    }
    return 1;
  }
  seams_rings_destroy(found);
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  return 0;
}

int main() {
  int n = 0;
  int counts[9] = {};
  int rings[13] = {};
  if (seams_set_num_threads(1) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (classify("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", n, counts, rings) != 0 || n != 128 ||
      counts[1] != 128 || rings[6] != 256) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "ice Ih n=%d hexagonal=%d rings6=%d\n", n, counts[1], rings[6]);
    return 1;
  }
  if (classify("input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj", n, counts, rings) != 0 || n != 136 ||
      counts[4] != 136 || rings[5] != 144 || rings[6] != 16) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "sII n=%d clathrate=%d rings5=%d rings6=%d\n", n, counts[4], rings[5],
                 rings[6]);
    return 1;
  }
  std::printf("cpp hexagonal 128 rings6 256 clathrate 136 rings5 144\n");
  return 0;
}
```

The class list is the [C++ API](../stable/cpp.md).

# Fortran {#fortran}

Classify ice Ih from Fortran. The recording uses `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`: `seams read` prints `nop 128`, and published CHILL+ at a 3.5 angstrom cutoff prints `nop 128 hexagonal 128`.

The binding is the fpm Git dependency `dseams` in [d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran). Programs use the module `seams`. `seams_c` is the `iso_c_binding` image of `include/seams.h`. The package links an installed `libseams`.

```toml
[dependencies]
dseams = { git = "https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran" }
```

The same two engine commands, without the package, print the ice Ih census:

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1
```

```default
nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073
nop 128 hexagonal 128
```

Module names are the [Fortran API](../stable/fortran.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/julia.md -->

# Lua and Fennel {#lua-and-fennel}

Classify a frame from Lua or Fennel. The recording follows `require("dseams")` and the same call from Fennel.

The binding is the Lua and Fennel library in [d-SEAMS/yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct). `require("dseams")` in Lua and `(require :dseams)` in Fennel call `libseams` (`include/seams.h`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct.git
cd yodaStruct
luarocks make
```

Option tables and return values are the [Lua reference](https://d-seams.github.io/yodaStruct/reference/lua.md).

The recording uses `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`. `seams read` prints `nop 128 frame 1`, and published CHILL+ at 3.5 angstrom prints `nop 128 hexagonal 128`:

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1
```

# Engines tutorial {#engines-tutorial}

Eight molecules of cubic ice are in `engines/tutorial/ice.data`. Lengths are angstroms.

LAMMPS `run_hook` takes the coordinates LAMMPS already stores in angstroms and calls `seams_chill_plus`. The deck next to the data file is pointed at this cell:

```default
# Eight-molecule cubic ice. The data file is angstroms (units metal).
# fix ext is the in-run hook. The tutorial test classifies ice.data
# with the same seams_chill_plus call the hook makes.
units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p p
read_data ice.data
mass 1 16.0
pair_style lj/cut 8.0
pair_coeff * * 0.1 2.75
velocity all set 0.0 0.0 0.0
fix freeze all setforce 0.0 0.0 0.0
fix ext all external pf/callback 1 1
thermo 1
timestep 0.001
run 0
```

The OpenMM plugin reads nanometers. It multiplies positions by 10 before the same call. The tutorial script builds those nanometers from the data file, scales them back, and requires the same eight cubic labels.

```python
def openmm_angstroms(xyz):
    """The plugin reads OpenMM nanometers and multiplies by 10."""
    nanometers = [value / 10.0 for value in xyz]
    return [value * 10.0 for value in nanometers]
```

A passing run prints `engines tutorial ok atoms 8 cubic 8`.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/gromacs.md -->

# GROMACS tutorial {#gromacs-tutorial}

`gmx-seams` reads a trajectory after `gmx mdrun` and classifies it with `seams_chill_plus`. Coordinates in the trajectory are nanometers. The tool multiplies them by 10 before the call. The lower-triangular GROMACS box stores its rows as the box vectors. The tilts are `box[1][0]`, `box[2][0]` and `box[2][1]` (xy, xz, yz). GROMACS keeps `box[0][1]`, `box[0][2]` and `box[1][2]` at zero.

Build the tool when libgromacs and its trajectory-analysis header are found. The binary is `build/engines/gmx-seams`. `libseams` is `build/src/libseams.so`.

```bash
meson setup build -Dwith_gromacs=auto
meson compile -C build gmx-seams
engines/gromacs/run_mdrun.sh build/engines/gmx-seams build/src
```

`engines/gromacs/run_mdrun.sh` writes a `.tpr` from `topol.top` and `md.mdp`, runs four frozen steps with `gmx mdrun -nsteps 4`, and classifies `ice.xtc`. That trajectory is five frames of the 64-atom cubic cell. The census line is:

```default
gromacs frames 5 ice 320 atoms 320 overhead_s S
```

`ice 320` is the cubic total over those five frames. `overhead_s` is the mean seconds per frame on this machine. `analyzeFrame` is the trajectory-analysis callback that does the conversion and the CHILL+ call.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/insitu.md -->

# In-situ tutorial {#in-situ-tutorial}

Eight cubic-ice atoms, one observation through `InSitu.observe`.

```bash
meson setup build -Dwith_tests=true
meson compile -C build
python3 engines/insitu_observe.py build
```

`engines/insitu_observe.py` loads `libseams_lang.so` from the build tree and passes the eight-atom diamond with an orthorhombic box. It stops when NumPy or `libseams_lang.so` is absent. Otherwise every label is cubic and the script prints:

```default
insitu atoms 8 cubic 8
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/lammps.md -->

# LAMMPS tutorial {#lammps-tutorial}

`engines/lammps/in.dseams` is a frozen cubic cell of 64 atoms. `fix ext` uses `pf/callback 2 2`, so the library calls d-SEAMS every two steps. Forces are cleared and the cell stays cubic.

```default
fix ext all external pf/callback 2 2
thermo 2
timestep 0.001
run 8
```

The driver is `run_hook`, built as `build/engines/run_hook`. It registers the callback before the `run` line and checks that successive calls are one stride apart. Positions stay in angstroms.

```bash
meson compile -C build run_hook
cd engines/lammps
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=../../build/src ../../build/engines/run_hook in.dseams
```

A passing run prints a line that starts `lammps calls 5 stride 2 ice 320`. `overhead_s` on that line is the mean seconds per call. Five visits of 64 atoms are all cubic. The next line is `lammps hexagonal 0 six-rings 128 q6 0.628539`.

`compute dseams` in `engines/lammps/compute_dseams.cpp` is the same CHILL+ call for a LAMMPS build that compiles styles in.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/openmm.md -->

# OpenMM tutorial {#openmm-tutorial}

`DseamsReporter` in `adapters/python/dseams_insitu/openmm.py` asks for positions every `interval` and calls `InSitu.observe`.

```python
from dseams_insitu.engine import InSitu
from dseams_insitu.openmm import DseamsReporter

    engine = InSitu()
    reporter = DseamsReporter(engine, interval=1)
    simulation.reporters.append(reporter)
    simulation.step(2)
```

```bash
PYTHONPATH=adapters/python python engines/openmm/test_reporter.py
```

The script builds an eight-atom cubic cell, a zero external force, and the Reference platform. Two steps at `interval=1` produce two reports. Every label is cubic, so the script prints `openmm calls 2 ice 16`.

`engines/openmm/plugin.cpp` takes the same two steps in C++. OpenMM positions are nanometers. The driver multiplies them by 10 before `seams_chill_plus`. A passing run prints `openmm-cpp calls 2 ice 16`.

```bash
c++ -O2 -std=c++17 -I"$OPENMM_INCLUDE" -Iinclude -Ibuild/src engines/openmm/plugin.cpp \
  -L"$OPENMM_LIB" -lOpenMM -Lbuild/src -lseams -o openmm-plugin
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/plumed.md -->

# PLUMED tutorial {#plumed-tutorial}

Use the [PLUMED engine page](../engines/plumed.md) to get the d-SEAMS
PLUMED plugin v0.4.1.

`SEAMS` with `MODE=all` reports five components. `q6` is the mean local q6 and carries finite-difference derivatives, so `RESTRAINT` can bias it. `ice` is the published CHILL+ cubic fraction. `ring` is the fraction of atoms on a primitive six-ring. `hexagonal` is the CHILL+ hexagonal count. `six` is the primitive six-ring count. The last four have no derivatives, and a `RESTRAINT` on them is rejected. `MODE=q6` and `MODE=q6bar` report only `q6`. The standalone PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in [PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).

`plumed driver` reads xyz in nanometers. `engines/plumed/ice.xyz` is the 64-atom cubic cell in nanometers. The plugin converts `getPosition` and the box from PLUMED’s length unit to angstroms, because d-SEAMS expects angstroms and `CUTOFF=3.5` is angstroms. Leave the driver’s length unit at the default. `UNITS LENGTH=A` in the deck gives the same `seams.q6`, `seams.ice` and `seams.ring`.

The shared library is `SeamsColvar.cpp` plus `plumed_components.cpp`. `plumed.dat` loads `./libSeamsPlumed.so`.

```default
LOAD FILE=./libSeamsPlumed.so
seams: SEAMS ATOMS=1-64 CUTOFF=3.5
RESTRAINT ARG=seams.q6 AT=0.5 KAPPA=10.0
PRINT ARG=seams.q6,seams.ice,seams.ring FILE=colvar STRIDE=1
```

```bash
c++ -shared -fPIC -O2 -std=c++17 -I"$PLUMED_INCLUDE" -Iinclude -Ibuild/src \
  engines/plumed/SeamsColvar.cpp engines/plumed/plumed_components.cpp \
  -Lbuild/src -lseams -lplumed -o libSeamsPlumed.so
plumed driver --ixyz engines/plumed/ice.xyz --plumed engines/plumed/plumed.dat
```

`$PLUMED_INCLUDE` is the directory that contains `plumed/core/Colvar.h`. On this cell `engines/plumed/run_driver.py` requires `seams.ice` of 1. A restraint may name `seams.q6` only.


---
