<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/upgrade-2.14.md -->

# Upgrade from 2.13 to 2.14 {#upgrade-from-2-13-to-2-14}

These notes cover the step from 2.13.0 to 2.14.0.
The release notes are
[2.14.0](../../reference/release-2.14.md).
Rebuild the engine, then relink anything that calls `libseams`.

## C and C++ {#c-and-c}

Add `#include "seams.h"` and link `libseams`. The header is C linkage
(`extern "C"`), so a C++ caller includes it as it stands.
`seams_set_num_threads(0)` restores the OpenMP width captured at first
use: `omp_get_max_threads()` when OpenMP is linked, and 1 otherwise.
A negative width is rejected. Frame, neighbour, CHILL+, q4/q6, and ring
calls are on that header.

A program that already used the C++ classes keeps those classes.
`BondClassifier` is still three doubles and one int, the 2.13 layout,
so a caller that passes the struct by value is unchanged.
`FingerprintOptions::color_types` colors fingerprint vertices by LAMMPS
type.

The language ABI is `seams_lang.h` and `libseams_lang`. Use it when
the program reads a trajectory path or keeps a frame across calls.
`seams_lang_version()` returns the Meson project version.

## Language bindings {#language-bindings}

2.14 moves every language binding out of this repository. Each one is
its own repository and package, built against the seams-core 2.14.0 tag
and versioned 2.14.0:

| Language | 2.13 location | 2.14 repository | Package |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python | PydSEAMSlib (pydseams) and the supplied dseams module | PydSEAMSlib | pydseamslib: import dseams and import pydseams |
| Lua, Fennel | yodaStruct (1.x) | yodaStruct | Git source, require("dseams") |
| R | none | dseams-r | dseams |
| Julia | none | Dseams.jl | Dseams and Seams, over libseams_jll |
| Rust | none | dseams-rs | crates dseams-sys and dseams |
| Fortran | none | dseams-fortran | fpm Git dependency dseams |

`pip install -U 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'` installs that package, with
`import dseams` and `import pydseams`.
Julia reads `libseams_lang` from `SEAMS_LANG_LIB`.
Rust reads the directory that holds `libseams` from `SEAMS_LIB_DIR`.
R reads `SEAMS_LIBDIR` and `SEAMS_INCLUDE`.
New calls and renamed options are in each repository’s changelog.
This repository provides `bindings/cxx` (`seams_lang.h` and `libseams_lang`).

## Engines {#engines}

`-Dwith_lammps`, `-Dwith_gromacs`, `-Dwith_openmm`, and `-Dwith_plumed`
default to `auto`. Meson builds a plugin when it finds that library.
The build and the census for each engine are
[LAMMPS](engine-lammps.md),
[GROMACS](engine-gromacs.md),
[OpenMM](engine-openmm.md), and
[PLUMED](engine-plumed.md). The standalone PLUMED action
(`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in
[PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).

| engine | what to change |
| --- | --- |
| LAMMPS | The hook and compute dseams read angstroms, with no unit conversion. engines/lammps/in.dseams is the in-tree deck (metal units). The sources to copy into a LAMMPS tree, and their deck, are under extras/lammps. |
| GROMACS | gmx-seams multiplies coordinates and the lower-triangular box by 10, then runs CHILL+. |
| OpenMM | The C++ plugin reads positions in nanometers and multiplies by 10. The Python DseamsReporter asks the context for angstroms and passes them to InSitu.observe. |
| PLUMED | The SEAMS collective variable multiplies positions and the box by 10. A q6 derivative is with respect to nanometers. Set PLUMED_NUM_THREADS before PLUMED starts. OMP_NUM_THREADS does not set the PLUMED team. |

## Threads {#threads}

`OMP_NUM_THREADS` is the OpenMP width.
`seams_set_num_threads(n)` sets the width of later calls, and `n = 0`
restores the width captured at first use.
A per-atom walk requests that width. The library does not reduce the
request to four threads below 8192 atoms.

The orthorhombic cutoff list runs on one thread when the frame has
fewer than 2048 atoms. A ring search that fills neighbour balls does
the same below 2048 vertices.

The library does not change `OMP_WAIT_POLICY`, and it does not shut the
OpenMP team down between calls. `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, or
`seams_set_num_threads(1)`, keeps the work on the calling thread.

When other processes hold the cores, a call may narrow its team, down
to a quarter of the requested width. `SEAMS_FAIR_WIDTH=0` keeps the
requested width. That narrowing does not pin the calling thread for
the rest of the process.

## Deprecations and breaks {#deprecations-and-breaks}

`--types` remains the deprecated alias of `--pair-types` and still
warns.

Fingerprint options use the American spelling.
`seams fingerprint --color-types` is the name help shows.
`--colour-types` is a hidden alias of that option: it is accepted, it
does not appear in help, and it does not warn.
`seams_fingerprint` takes `color_types`.
A key library writes `colors` in its header. The reader accepts
`colours` as a deprecated alias of that word, so a 2.13 library file
with `colours 1` keeps its type colors. The library has no warning
channel, so that read is silent.

The stored graph name is `seeded`.
CHILL and CHILL+ treat `seeded`, and an empty graph name, as the cutoff
list. Pass `--graph mutual` for the four-nearest graph.
`seams_frame_chill` and `seams_frame_chill_plus` accept `cutoff` and
`mutual`. A null graph is `cutoff`. The string `seeded` is rejected.
`seams cages` still treats `seeded` as its own graph.

A bad flag exits 2. A missing LAMMPS dump prints
`Fatal Error` with the path and `seams read` exits 0 with `nop 0`.
A missing XYZ file exits 2.

`seams steinhardt` prints each degree named by `--l`, and the
Lechner-Dellago average of that degree. The default `--l` is `4,6`,
so the default line carries q4, q4bar, q6, and q6bar. When both
degrees are requested they share one cutoff list.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/migrate-1x.md -->

# Migrate from d-SEAMS 1.x {#migrate-from-d-seams-1-x}

1.x was a Lua script plus `yodaStruct -c lua_inputs/config.yml`.
The config named the trajectory and switched analyses on. 2.14 is one
`seams` subcommand, or one call in `seams.h` / `seams_lang.h`, for
each of those switches.

1.x Lua had plain globals only. It has no `dseams` table and no
`require("dseams")`. v1.0.0 and v1.0.1 register the same globals.
Later Lua names first shipped in
[yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct) 2.x, which calls
`seams.h`. This repository does not register Lua names.

Each row is one analysis. Where the row has both a command and a C
call, they read the same trajectory.

## yodaStyle config {#yodastyle-config}

| 1.x key | 2.14 command | 2.14 C call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bulk.topologicalNetworkCriterion | seams cages | seams_frame_cages |
| bulk.bondOrderParameters | seams steinhardt | seams_frame_steinhardt_graph |
| topoOneDim | seams prisms | seams_frame_prisms |
| topoTwoDim | seams_frame_monolayer | seams_frame_monolayer |

`topoTwoDim` has no `seams` subcommand. The monolayer census is
`seams_frame_monolayer` (language frame) and `seams_monolayer`
(`seams.h`). The counts buffer is indexed by ring size and must hold
at least `max_depth + 1` integers.
On the mixed TIP4P dump `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` the call
takes oxygen type 2.

## Lua globals and later Lua names {#lua-globals-and-later-lua-names}

The first column is the v1.0.1 global. v1.0.0 registers the same
names. A row marked new in 2.x had no 1.x global; the parenthetical
is the yodaStruct release that added the Lua names. Each later column
is the name that release first registered. `require("dseams")` starts
at yodaStruct 2.2.0. The last two columns are the 2.14 replacement.

| 1.x global (v1.0.1) | yodaStruct 2.0.0 | yodaStruct 2.2.0 | yodaStruct 2.4.1 | yodaStruct 2.7.0 | yodaStruct 2.8.0 | yodaStruct 2.9.0 | 2.14 command | 2.14 C call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| readFrame / readFrameOnlyOne | readLammpsTrjO | dseams.read |  | readLammpsTrj |  |  | seams read | seams_frame_read |
| chillPlus_cij / chillPlus_iceType | getCorrelPlus / getIceTypePlus | dseams.chill_plus |  |  |  |  | seams chill-plus | seams_frame_chill_plus |
| chill_cij / chill_iceType | getCorrel / getIceType | dseams.chill |  |  |  |  | seams chill | seams_frame_chill |
| getPrimitiveRings | ringNetwork |  |  |  |  |  | seams rings | seams_frame_rings |
| averageQ6 | steinhardtQl |  |  |  |  |  | seams steinhardt | seams_frame_steinhardt_graph |
| bulkTopologicalNetworkCriterion | seededCageAffiliation | dseams.cages |  |  |  |  | seams cages | seams_frame_cages |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.9.0) |  |  |  |  |  | findBySignature / dseams.cages_by_signature | seams cages --signature | seams_frame_signature_edge |
| neighborList / bondNetworkByIndex | neighListO | dseams.neighbors |  |  |  |  | seams_frame_neighbours | seams_neighbours_build |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.0.0) | kNearestNeighbourList | dseams.knn |  |  |  |  | seams_frame_neighbours | seams_neighbours_build |
| calcRDF |  |  | calcRDF3D | dseams.rdf |  |  | seams rdf | seams_frame_rdf |
| prismAnalysis |  |  |  |  |  |  | seams prisms | seams_frame_prisms |
| ringAnalysis |  |  |  |  |  |  | seams_frame_monolayer | seams_frame_monolayer |
| getHbondNetwork |  |  |  | dseams.hbonds |  |  | seams hbonds | seams hbonds |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.4.1) |  |  | calcCN / dseams.cn |  |  |  | seams cn | seams cn |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.7.0) |  |  |  | densityByType / dseams.density |  |  | seams density-z | seams density-z |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.8.0) |  |  |  |  | topologyFingerprint / dseams.fingerprint |  | seams fingerprint | seams fingerprint |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.7.0) |  |  |  | contactPairs / dseams.pairs |  |  | seams pairs | seams pairs |
| new in 2.x (yodaStruct 2.7.0) |  |  |  | domainStats / dseams.domain |  |  | seams domains | seams domains |

The 2.0.0 column names C++ functions in this tree (`readLammpsTrjO`,
`getCorrelPlus`, `ringNetwork`, `neighListO`, and the others). 1.x
called them under the globals in the first column.
`calcRDF` in 1.x is the in-plane RDF of the monolayer script
(`rdf2Danalysis_AA`). The 3D RDF that `seams rdf` prints first reached
Lua as `calcRDF3D`.
`ringAnalysis` is the 1.x `topoTwoDim` ring census and `prismAnalysis`
the 1.x `topoOneDim` one. No later column registers a new Lua name
for either.

The 2015 rule and the OVITO rule are selected with `--rule`.
The walk-through is
[the published rule and the OVITO rule](../../explanation/chill-plus-rules.md).

Neighbours have no `seams` subcommand. There are two rows.
`seams_frame_neighbours` counts the directed pairs on the language
frame. `seams_neighbours_build` builds that list through `seams.h`.
The cutoff row uses graph `cutoff`. The k-nearest row uses graph
`mutual`. The two calls report the same pair count.

Hydrogen bonds, coordination, the density profile, the fingerprint,
contact pairs, and domains repeat the command in the last column.
The functions in `seams.h` are `seams_hbonds`, `seams_coordination`,
`seams_density_axis`, `seams_fingerprint`, `seams_contact_pairs`, and
`seams_domains`.

On `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj`:

```bash
seams hbonds input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --htype 1
seams cn input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 4.5
seams density-z input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2 --bins 4
seams fingerprint input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --type 2
seams pairs input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --site 1=cationHead,2=anion
seams domains input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --site 1=cationHead,2=anion --subset polar
```

The lines are `nop 250 hbonds 460`,
`# types 1 2 cutoff 4.5 cn 9.144 nI 500 nJ 250 volume 288324`,
`classes 89`, `contact-pair count 0 nCation 0 nAnion 250`, and
`subset polar n 750 largest 750 P 1`.
`density-z` starts:

```text
# z rho
29.557 0.000887889
```

CHILL+ and rings use the cubic cell `input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj`,
type 1, cutoff 3.5 Å, graph `cutoff`.
`seams chill-plus --rule published` prints `nop 4096 cubic 4096`.
`seams rings` prints `nop 4096 rings 8192` and `6 8192`.
`seams_frame_chill_plus` and `seams_frame_rings` take that same frame.
The signature row is `seams cages --signature 512 --cage-edge none` on
`input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj`. That command prints
`nop 46 graph seeded signature 5:12 cages 2 atoms 40`.
`seams_frame_signature_edge` takes that same frame.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/bindings.md -->

# Use a language binding {#use-a-language-binding}

This repository builds the engine, the C API `libseams` (`include/seams.h`),
the C ABI `libseams_lang` (`bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h`), and the `seams`
command.

[C](../../stable/c.md) and [C++](../../stable/cpp.md) document those libraries.

Every other language is its own repository, with its own documentation,
tests, and releases. A binding’s version is the seams-core version it was
built against. The Python release for this engine is `pydseamslib` 2.14.0.
Each repository’s README has the install command.

## Languages {#languages}

| Language | Repository | Package | Links |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python | d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib | pydseamslib | libseams, libseams_lang |
| Lua, Fennel | d-SEAMS/yodaStruct | Git source, require("dseams") | libseams |
| R | d-SEAMS/dseams-r | dseams | libseams_lang |
| Julia | d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl | Dseams, engine from libseams_jll | libseams_lang, libseams |
| Rust | d-SEAMS/dseams-rs | crates dseams-sys, dseams | libseams |
| Fortran | d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran | fpm Git dependency dseams | libseams |

`import dseams` is the array API over `libseams`: `dseams.Frame`,
`chill_plus`, `q4q6`, `neighbours`, `rings`, and `from_ase`.
`import pydseams` and `import pydseamslib` are the trajectory package.
`pydseams.read` opens a dump. `dseams.userframe` is the Frame over
`libseams_lang`, documented on the
[Python Frame](../../reference/python-frame.md) page.
`Dseams` calls `libseams_lang` for a frame and `libseams` for the
re-exported `seams_*` functions. `libseams_jll` supplies the engine
binary. The same repository includes `Seams`, an example of the
`libseams` C API.
The R package compiles the engine it ships, and the calls in its README
use `libseams_lang`.

## Ice Ih {#ice-ih}

`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` is one orthorhombic frame of ice Ih: 128
oxygens, every atom LAMMPS type 1. The path is relative to a seams-core
checkout. `dseams.Frame` stores the coordinates and the three edge
lengths. Published CHILL+ labels every oxygen hexagonal, so `counts[1]`
is 128. The ring histogram holds 256 six-rings, so `histogram[6]` is 256.
The mean local q6 at 3.5 Å is 0.625855. The cutoff neighbour list holds
512 directed pairs, four per oxygen, so `offsets[-1]` is 512.

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import dseams
>>> def ice():
...     xyz, edges, reading = [], [], False
...     handle = open("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj")
...     try:
...         while True:
...             line = handle.readline()
...             if line == "":
...                 break
...             if line.startswith("ITEM: BOX BOUNDS"):
...                 edges = []
...                 for _ in range(3):
...                     lo, hi = handle.readline().split()[:2]
...                     edges.append(float(hi) - float(lo))
...             elif line.startswith("ITEM: ATOMS"):
...                 reading = True
...             elif reading:
...                 parts = line.split()
...                 if len(parts) < 5:
...                     break
...                 xyz.append([float(v) for v in parts[2:5]])
...     finally:
...         handle.close()
...     return xyz, edges
>>> xyz, edges = ice()
>>> len(xyz)
128
>>> frame = dseams.Frame()
>>> frame.set_frame(np.asarray(xyz), np.asarray(edges))
>>> frame.count()
128
>>> offsets, columns = frame.neighbours(3.5)
>>> int(offsets[-1])
512
>>> sizes, symmetry, histogram, fraction = frame.rings(3.5, 6)
>>> int(histogram[6])
256
>>> q4, q6 = frame.q4q6(3.5)
>>> round(float(q6.mean()), 6)
0.625855
>>> labels, counts = frame.chill_plus()
>>> int(counts[1])
128
```

These four commands print that census. `seams rings` prints two lines,
and the other three commands print one line each. `seams steinhardt`
also prints the Lechner-Dellago q6-bar. `seams cn` with this cutoff and
type prints `nI 128`, the number of atoms in the coordination sum.

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams rings input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1
seams steinhardt input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --l 6 --type 1
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1
```

```text
nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073
nop 128 rings 256
6 256
nop 128 q6 0.625855 q6bar 0.562449
nop 128 hexagonal 128
```

`dseams.from_ase` returns positions and a nine-number LAMMPS cell for
`set_frame`. The [Python Frame](../../reference/python-frame.md) page
runs that round trip on this file.

## What the bindings share {#what-the-bindings-share}

The classifiers run in the engine, and every binding calls those
functions. `seams_q4q6` in `include/seams.h` and `seams_frame_q4_q6` in
`bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h` compute cutoff-shell q4 and q6.
`seams steinhardt` prints the local mean and the Lechner-Dellago average
for each degree named by `--l`. The default is `4,6`. The accepted
degrees are 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12. Degrees 3 and 12 are the Zeron hydrate
pair. [Local q4 and q6](q4-q6.md) is that command.

Each binding below has a short screencast.
The full set is on the [videos](../../videos/index.md) page.

# FAQ {#faq}

## How do I install the engine? {#how-do-i-install-the-engine}

[Install the engine](../../getting-started/install.md). From a checkout, `pixi run build`
writes `./bbdir/seams`. `nix build` writes `./result/bin/seams`.

## Where is Python? {#where-is-python}

[PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib).
`pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'`.
`import pydseams` is the Frame package.
`import pydseamslib` is that same package.
`import dseams` is the array module.
The compiled extension is `pydseams.yoda`. `pydseams._core` and
`pydseams.cyoda` are the same object.

## Where is Lua / Fennel? {#where-is-lua-fennel}

[yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct).
`require("dseams")`. `require("yoda")` returns that table.
The meson project builds `dseams_core.so`. It does not build a
`yodaStruct` executable. The 1.x command `yodaStruct -c` is
[Migrate from 1.x](migrate-1x.md).

## Why do CHILL+ and cages disagree? {#why-do-chill-and-cages-disagree}

They answer different questions.
[CHILL+ versus cages](../../explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md).

## What does `--graph seeded` mean? {#what-does-graph-seeded-mean}

It is the default for `cages` only: mutual k-nearest seeds and the
union of each atom’s k nearest. `k` is 4 unless `-k` is set.
`chill` and `chill-plus` map that name onto the cutoff list.

## Which `--type` do I pass? {#which-type-do-i-pass}

On a single LAMMPS frame, `--type 0` (the default) keeps type 2 when
any atom has it, otherwise type 1.
Mixed TIP4P dumps here, including `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj`,
use type 2 for oxygen and type 1 for hydrogen.
Single-site dumps use type 1: `ice1h.lammpstrj`,
`interface_f0.lammpstrj`, and `mW_cubic.lammpstrj`.
Any other mixed dump needs the integer of the species you want; see
[Ionic-liquid dumps](ionic-liquid.md).
`density-z` treats `--type 0` as every atom.

## How does a sheared dump box work? {#how-does-a-sheared-dump-box-work}

The dump stores bound spans plus optional `xy`, `xz`, and `yz`.
The edge lengths are recovered from the spans and those tilt factors.
See [Sheared cells](sheared-cells.md).

## Why is chemfiles disabled on `nix build`? {#why-is-chemfiles-disabled-on-nix-build}

chemfiles is not in the flake closure. `seams --features` prints
`chemfiles: disabled`, and `.pdb`, `.gro`, and `.dcd` fail with
`chemfiles is not in this build`. The default pixi lock enables
chemfiles.

## How do I turn colors off? {#how-do-i-turn-colors-off}

Set `NO_COLOR` to a non-empty value. Set `FORCE_COLOR` to a
non-empty value to force color on.

## Does `seams` walk a trajectory? {#does-seams-walk-a-trajectory}

Yes. `--frame N` is the first frame and `--last M` is the last.
Both are 1-based, and `--last` is inclusive. On a LAMMPS dump, a
`--last` past the end of the file stops at the last frame.
`--jobs J` is the OpenMP worker count for that dump. `--jobs 1` is
serial. `.xyz`, `.pdb`, `.gro`, `.dcd`, and `.con` are read one
frame at a time. `seams --features` prints whether OpenMP is on.

## How do I view a classified dump? {#how-do-i-view-a-classified-dump}

`frame.to_solvis()` needs the solvis extra:
`pip install 'pydseamslib[solvis]==2.14.0'`.
The call on ice Ih is on [Python Frame](../../reference/python-frame.md).
The [PydSEAMSlib documentation](https://d-seams.github.io/PydSEAMSlib/)
is the Frame how-to.
`--per-atom FILE` on `chill`, `chill-plus`, `cages`, `fingerprint`,
and `ions` appends a LAMMPS dump with one extra column. OVITO and
VMD open that file.

## How do I cite this? {#how-do-i-cite-this}

[Citation](../../explanation/citation.md). The preferred citation
is the 2020 JCIM paper.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| symptom | cause | fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A command and a trajectory file are required / exit 2 | The command, the file, or both were omitted | seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj |
| unknown command: NAME / exit 2 | NAME is not a command | seams --help. chill_plus is chill-plus. ovito_chill_plus is ovito-chill+ |
| bad --pair-types (want I,J) / exit 2 | The value is not two integers separated by a comma | seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 |
| nop 0, exit 0 | The type filter kept no atoms, or the frame is empty | --type 2 on mixed TIP4P (exampleTraj.lammpstrj). --type 1 on single-site dumps (ice1h.lammpstrj, mW_cubic.lammpstrj). Another species needs its integer (Ionic-liquid dumps). --strict-input makes an empty frame exit 2 |
| Neighbours miss a pair across a sheared face | Bound spans were used as the edge lengths | The tilt factors in the dump are enough. The engine recovers H (Sheared cells) |
| chemfiles: disabled, then chemfiles is not in this build | This binary has no chemfiles. The suffix in the message is pdb, gro, or dcd | pixi run build (the default lock enables chemfiles). The nix flake leaves chemfiles out (Nix flake) |
| segfault in mmCIFFormat::read with conda-forge chemfiles 0.10.4 | That release writes label_seq_id . and omits label_entity_id | Use the pixi or Meson build. It rejects that library and builds tag 0.10.4 with cmake/patches/chemfiles-0.10.4-mmcif.patch. A library you linked yourself needs that patch (Install the engine) |
| readcon-core is not in this build; CON input needs it | seams --features shows readcon-core: disabled. The nix flake does not include it | A Meson build that finds readcon-core reads .con. -Dwith_readcon=disabled leaves the reader out |
| --jobs stays serial | OpenMP is off, or the file is not a LAMMPS dump | seams --features. --jobs is the OpenMP worker count on a LAMMPS dump range. --jobs 1 is serial. .xyz, .pdb, .gro, .dcd, and .con are one frame at a time |
| ModuleNotFoundError: pydseams | The Python package is PydSEAMSlib | pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0' (PydSEAMSlib) |
| Looking for yodaStruct -c lua_inputs/config.yml | That command is the 1.x driver | seams in this repository. Lua is require("dseams") from yodaStruct. See Migrate from 1.x |
| seams: command not found | The binary is not on PATH | After pixi run build or meson compile -C bbdir it is ./bbdir/seams. nix build writes ./result/bin/seams. pixi run install or meson install installs it |
| module 'dseams' not found / require("dseams") fails | Lua cannot see dseams.lua and dseams_core.so | Build yodaStruct with meson. Set LUA_PATH to lua/?.lua and LUA_CPATH to the directory that holds dseams_core.so. require("yoda") returns the same table |

Two commands on the bundled frames:

```bash
seams read input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2
```

When you file an issue, include `seams --version`, `seams --features`,
the command line, and a minimal dump.

# Worked examples {#worked-examples}

A tutorial is a learning path. You finish it with a skill, not a
lookup table.

| tutorial | you learn |
| --- | --- |
| Classify a clathrate | GenIce sI, sII and sH cage census |
| Ice-water interface | CHILL+ slabs along the normal, and the front |
| Nucleation | Largest crystal cluster on three of the 148 frames |
| Brine and NaCl | Ions per layer across the ice front |
| Run in situ | LAMMPS and OpenMM on one cubic cell, skipped when the library is absent |
| Classify ice on the mixed TIP4P example | seams read, CHILL+, cages, and why the scores disagree |
| Ice and clathrate labels | CHILL+ and cage signatures from Python |
| Primitive rings | Franzblau census on one frame |
| Bond-orientational order | q_l and the Lechner-Dellago average |
| Confined water | in-plane RDF, sheet rings, prisms |
| Quasi-one-dimensional ice | where the nanotube and monolayer examples live |
| Paper figures | the supplied numbers behind the 2020 figures |
| Interface slab | Published CHILL+ against the OVITO rule on a slab you build |
| Clathrate cages | GenIce sI, sII and sH |
| Ring statistics | Primitive rings and the shortest-path test |
| Ice in brine | The front, and the crystal count, along a short run |
| Nucleation score | Mean q6bar as a nucleus is restored |
| Science gallery | The full runs, drawn and captioned from their reports |

How-tos solve a goal you already have. Reference names flags and
headers. Explanation covers why CHILL+ and the cage census can disagree.

The paper tutorials provide a short example and the corresponding
full-size result. Each page explains the analysis and the number you should
see.

| In-situ CHILL+ | Labels and the ring histogram from libseams_lang |
| FAQ | Short answers |
| Troubleshooting | Symptom, cause, fix |

# Paper figures {#paper-figures}

The 2020 JCIM figures are drawn from figshare project 73545.
This page runs the same calls on the supplied example trajectories.
Python is `pip install 'pydseamslib==2.14.0'`; the import is `dseams.userframe`.
Run the block from the repository root.

| figure | trajectory | call | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cubic ice, CHILL+ | mW_cubic.lammpstrj frame 1, type 1 | chill_plus() | 4096 cubic |
| cubic ice, cages | the same frame | cages() | n_ic 4096 |
| sI 5^12 cages | =genice_sI.lammpstrj~, type 1 | cages_by_signature("512") | 2 cages, n_atoms 40 |
| mixed frame | =exampleTraj.lammpstrj~, type 2 | cutoff CHILL+ versus cages | interClathrate 9, water 241, cage n_ih 0, n_ic 0, n_water 250 |

`Frame.chill_plus` defaults to the cutoff neighbour list.
On the cubic mW frame that list and `chill_plus(graph="mutual")` both
return 4096 cubic. On the mixed frame the cutoff list is the row above.
The cage score has no hexagonal cage and no double-diamond cage, so
every oxygen is `n_water`.

The nucleation, nanotube, monolayer, and in-plane RDF figures use
trajectories from figshare project 73545.

```python
from dseams import userframe as ds

ice = ds.read("input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj", frame=1, atom_type=1)
print(ice.chill_plus().cubic, ice.chill_plus(graph="mutual").cubic, ice.cages().n_ic)
assert ice.chill_plus().cubic == 4096
assert ice.chill_plus(graph="mutual").cubic == 4096
assert ice.cages().n_ic == 4096

guest = ds.read("input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
found = guest.cages_by_signature("512")
print(len(found), found.n_atoms)
assert len(found) == 2 and found.n_atoms == 40

mixed = ds.read("input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj", atom_type=2)
labels = mixed.chill_plus()
score = mixed.cages()
print(labels.interClathrate, labels.water, score.n_ih, score.n_ic, score.n_water)
assert labels.interClathrate == 9 and labels.water == 241
assert score.n_ih == 0 and score.n_ic == 0 and score.n_water == 250
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-interface.md -->

# CHILL+ on an ice/water slab {#chill-on-an-ice-water-slab}

An interface is where a rule is easy to fool. The crystal half should
be hexagonal ice. The liquid half should be water. The molecules in
between are the ones where the published CHILL+ rule and the OVITO
rule can part company, because they do not use the same neighbour test.

This example builds a small slab.
GenIce supplies a 2 by 2 by 1 ice Ih cell, oxygen only, so the
hydrogen disorder is not part of the label. A copy of that cell is
shifted by one box length along z and shaken by less than an angstrom.
The shake is why the upper half is liquid: the oxygens are no longer
on lattice sites. OpenMM then minimises the stack for eight steps with
the lower half restrained. The restraint is why the crystal survives
the relax. The cutoff is 3.5 Å, the same shell CHILL+ will read, and
it has to sit under half the shortest box edge or OpenMM refuses the
periodic force.

The published rule prints

```text
interface published hexagonal 68 interfacial 19 water 41
```

The OVITO rule prints

```text
interface ovito hexagonal 68 interfacial 20 water 40
```

Both lines sum to 128, the oxygen count of the doubled cell. Both
rules call 68 oxygens hexagonal. They move one molecule between
interfacial and water. That single molecule is the reason to name the
rule when you quote an interface count.

## Full run {#full-run}

The supplied paper frame is `input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj`:
864 molecules, one frame.

```text
interface full input molecules 864 frames 1 file-frames 1 file input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj
interface full paper molecules 864 frames 1
interface full published hexagonal 352 interfacial 49 water 434 clathrate 3 interClathrate 25
interface full ovito hexagonal 346 interfacial 57 water 437 clathrate 3 interClathrate 20
interface full phi-c 0.00283286
interface full stack HHHHHHHH....C.
```

The stack is eight hexagonal slabs, a gap, and one cubic layer.
Hexagonal is 352 on the published rule and 346 on the OVITO rule.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-cages.md -->

# Cage census of sI, sII and sH {#cage-census-of-si-sii-and-sh}

A clathrate cage is a closed polyhedron of primitive rings. The
signature is the face list: $5^{12}$ is twelve pentagons, and
$5^{12}6^{2}$ adds two hexagons. Counting those polyhedra is how you
tell sI from sII from sH. GenIce builds the empty host. Guests would
sit in the cages and are left out here, because the census is of the
water rings.

Use only the oxygen sites in the LAMMPS trajectory. Hydrogens
and the massless site would change the neighbour list. sI and sII are
orthogonal. Their commands use the default face-edge window,
`2.65,3.15` in the angstroms of the dump. sH is skewed. The GenIce
HS3 cell has a tilt, and the dump keeps it. The sH command passes
`--cage-edge none`, so a face is kept from its ring census and is not
filtered by edge length. sI and sII do not pass that flag.

The cage census is

```text
cages sI 2 6
cages sII 16 8
cages sH 6 4 2
```

sI, one cell, 46 waters: 2 of $5^{12}$ and 6 of $5^{12}6^{2}$.
sII, 136 waters: 16 of $5^{12}$ and 8 of $5^{12}6^{4}$.
sH, the GenIce HS3 cell, 68 waters: 6 of $5^{12}$, 4 of
$4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and 2 of $5^{12}6^{8}$.

## Full run {#full-run}

The unit cell is already the right cage. A larger host has to hold
that census times the number of cells, or the count is wrong.
The full example repeats sI as 2 by 2 by 2, eight cells and 368 waters,
and sII and sH as 2 by 2 by 1, four cells, 544 and 272 waters. sH
keeps its tilt. `--cage-edge none` is still only the sH command.

The repeated cells give

```text
cages full input sI molecules 368 frames 1 file sI-full.lammpstrj
cages full sI 16 48
cages full input sII molecules 544 frames 1 file sII-full.lammpstrj
cages full sII 64 32
cages full input sH molecules 272 frames 1 file sH-full.lammpstrj
cages full sH 24 16 8
cages full paper unit sI molecules 46 cages 2 6
cages full paper unit sII molecules 136 cages 16 8
cages full paper unit sH molecules 68 cages 6 4 2
```

Eight sI cells hold 16 of $5^{12}$ and 48 of $5^{12}6^{2}$. Four
sII cells hold 64 of $5^{12}$ and 32 of $5^{12}6^{4}$. Four sH
cells hold 24 of $5^{12}$, 16 of $4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and 8 of
$5^{12}6^{8}$. Each number is the unit-cell count times the number
of cells.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-rings.md -->

# Primitive rings and the shortest-path test {#primitive-rings-and-the-shortest-path-test}

A ring search first walks every simple cycle up to a chosen size.
Many of those cycles are not useful: a chord gives a shorter route
between two vertices, so the long way around is not a ring of the
network. The Franzblau test keeps a cycle only when, for every pair
of its vertices, some shortest path between them lies on the cycle.
Those survivors are the primitive rings. `seams rings` reports that
census. The example also counts the cycles before the test, so you can
see what the filter removes.

The cell is GenIce ice Ih, one unit, 16 oxygens, cutoff 3.5 Å.
It is small on purpose. Every cycle of length 4, 5 or 6 can be
listed, and the same neighbour list is what the primitive search uses.
A larger crystal would hide the filter, because almost every six-cycle
in ice Ih already passes.

The ring search gives

```text
rings primitive 4 24 6 32
rings shortest 4 24 6 32
rings searched 4 24 6 128
```

The shortest-path test and `seams rings` agree: 24 four-rings and 32
six-rings. The unfiltered search found 128 six-cycles and no
five-ring. The other 96 six-cycles have a shortcut, so they are
dropped.

## Full run {#full-run}

The paper ring census is one frame of
`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj`. The dump holds 11 frames of 4096
molecules. Frame 1 has 4096 molecules and 8192 six-rings.

```text
rings full input molecules 4096 frames 1 file-frames 11 file input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj
rings full paper molecules 4096 frames 1 rings 8192
rings full nop 4096 rings 8192
rings full histogram 6 8192
```

The histogram has one bin: 8192 six-rings.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-brine.md -->

# Ice growing into brine {#ice-growing-into-brine}

The front is the height where the crystal slabs stop. CHILL+ labels
the waters. Slabs of 3.7 Å along z are written as a stack: `H` for
hexagonal, `C` for cubic, `.` for a slab that is neither. The front
is the first slab that is not crystal, times 3.7 Å. Ions are not
waters, so they stay out of that count. You still want them in the
box, because the liquid they sit in is the brine the ice is growing
into.

Packmol places six waters, one sodium and one chloride above a fixed
GenIce ice Ih block. OpenMM then relaxes three stages. At each later
stage the nearest brine oxygen is moved onto the next lattice plane
and restrained. That move is the growth step. The relax is why the
ions and the leftover liquid can answer it, instead of staying where
packmol left them.

The short example gives

```text
brine frame 0 hexagonal 31 water 38 front 7.40
brine frame 1 hexagonal 32 water 36 front 7.40
brine frame 2 hexagonal 32 water 35 front 7.40
```

The front stays at 7.40 Å, two slab widths, so the added hexagonal
water has not filled the next 3.7 Å slab. The hexagonal count rises
from 31 to 32 and stays there. The water count falls from 38 to 35.

## Full run {#full-run}

The supplied brine frame is
`input/traj/nacl_front.lammpstrj`: 864 waters and 9 ions, one frame.
CHILL+ is scored on the waters.

```text
brine full input molecules 873 frames 1 file-frames 1 file input/traj/nacl_front.lammpstrj
brine full paper waters 864 ions 9 frames 1
brine full waters 864 ions 9 hexagonal 352 water 434
```

Hexagonal is 352 and water is 434, the same counts as the
ion-free interface frame.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-nucleation.md -->

# Ice-likeness along a short nucleation run {#ice-likeness-along-a-short-nucleation-run}

Ice-likeness here is the mean Lechner-Dellago $\bar q_6$. A liquid
sits near 0.2. A crystal sits near 0.5. A nucleus in a liquid pulls
the mean up as it grows, which is why the score is the whole-frame
average and not a single molecule.

The example trajectory has three frames. GenIce ice
Ih is shaken into a liquid. The basal half of the original lattice is
the nucleus. Frame 0 is the shaken liquid. Frame 1 puts half of that
nucleus back on its lattice sites. Frame 2 puts the rest back. OpenMM
relaxes each frame for two steps with those sites restrained, so the
liquid can move and the nucleus cannot dissolve before you measure it.

The three frames give

```text
nucleation frame 0 q6bar 0.276023
nucleation frame 1 q6bar 0.320504
nucleation frame 2 q6bar 0.334254
```

The mean rises at each stage.

## Full run {#full-run}

The paper trajectory is figshare
[10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.11448702.v1):
148 frames of 4096 molecules, md5 `c28fc209a2854d2ba49e8f9b55accbe8`.
Run `seams steinhardt` on every frame.

```text
nucleation full paper molecules 4096 frames 148
nucleation full frame 1 q6bar 0.26063
nucleation full frame 148 q6bar 0.287256
nucleation full lines 148
```

Frame 1 of that file is the shipped
`input/traj/nucleation_f1.lammpstrj`. The mean $\bar q_6$ on frame
1 is 0.26063. Frame 148 is 0.287256.


---

# Science gallery {#science-gallery}

These pictures show the interface, brine, ring, cage, and nucleation examples.
Each caption explains the colors and reports the corresponding molecular
census.

## Interface slab {#interface-slab}

![Interface slab](../../_images/gallery-interface.png)

The picture is the 864-molecule paper frame, colored by published CHILL+. Published CHILL+ reports hexagonal 352 interfacial 49 water 434 clathrate 3 interClathrate 25. The OVITO rule reports hexagonal 346 interfacial 57 water 437 clathrate 3 interClathrate 20. Hexagonal ice is orange and liquid water is sky blue. The interfacial shell is where the two rules part.

```default
interface full input molecules 864 frames 1 file-frames 1 file input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj
interface full paper molecules 864 frames 1
interface full published hexagonal 352 interfacial 49 water 434 clathrate 3 interClathrate 25
interface full ovito hexagonal 346 interfacial 57 water 437 clathrate 3 interClathrate 20
interface full phi-c 0.00283286
interface full stack HHHHHHHH....C.
```

## sI and sII cages {#si-and-sii-cages}

![sI and sII cages](../../_images/gallery-cages-sI.png)

![sI and sII cages](../../_images/gallery-cages-sII.png)

The first cluster is sI and the second cluster is sII. Bonds draw the water rings that close the cages. sI holds 16 of the small cage and 48 of the large cage. sII holds 64 of the small cage and 32 of the large cage.

```default
cages full input sI molecules 368 frames 1 file sI-full.lammpstrj
cages full sI 16 48
cages full input sII molecules 544 frames 1 file sII-full.lammpstrj
cages full sII 64 32
cages full input sH molecules 272 frames 1 file sH-full.lammpstrj
cages full sH 24 16 8
cages full paper unit sI molecules 46 cages 2 6
cages full paper unit sII molecules 136 cages 16 8
cages full paper unit sH molecules 68 cages 6 4 2
```

tutorials.

# Science tutorials {#science-tutorials}

Three calculations from the papers: an ice-water interface, a brine
freezing front, and the sII and sH cages. The printed census is the
check. The figures are those same frames. The gallery collects the
four pictures.

**[Ice/liquid interface and nucleation](interface.md)**

`input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj` is 864 waters in a cell 23 by
22 by 53 angstrom. Published CHILL+ at 3.5 angstrom reports 352
hexagonal, 434 liquid, 49 interfacial, 25 interfacial clathrate, 3
clathrate, and 1 cubic. The nucleus is frame 1 of
`input/traj/nucleation_f1.lammpstrj` (4096 atoms): 47 cubic, 62
hexagonal, 3589 liquid, and 240 interfacial.

**[Brine freezing front](brine.md)**

The 230 K frames with 20 ion pairs come from the
`d-SEAMS/brine-front-230K` dataset. All 1496 oxygens match the
stored CHILL+ names. At 5 ns the count is 741 hexagonal, 621 liquid,
89 interfacial, 41 interfacial clathrate, 4 clathrate, and no cubic.
The rejection coefficient is 0.

**[sII and sH hydrate cages](cages.md)**

`input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj` and
`input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj` are guest-free hosts, 136 waters
each. sII holds 16 of $5^{12}$ and 8 of $5^{12}6^{4}$.
sH holds 12 of $5^{12}$, 8 of $4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and 4
of $5^{12}6^{8}$.

**[Science figures](gallery.md)**

The four molecular views, with the census repeated in the caption.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/science/interface.md -->

# Ice/liquid interface and nucleation {#ice-liquid-interface-and-nucleation}

The interface dump is `input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj`, 864 waters
in a cell 23 by 22 by 53 angstrom. The nucleus is frame 1 of the mW
trajectory released with the paper (`input/traj/nucleation_f1.lammpstrj`,
4096 atoms, timestep 15677000). Both are labeled with published CHILL+
at 3.5 angstrom on the cutoff graph.

Layer cubicity is the cubic share of the basal layers. On the slab the
stacking axis is z, the long edge. On the nucleus it is the box axis
whose crystal atoms have the strongest density wave in that period
window. The molecular view numbers the basal layers and shows liquid
with reduced opacity.

Python and C print the same census:

```text
interface hexagonal 352 water 434 interfacial 49 cubic 1
interface layers HHHHHHHHC cubicity 0.111111
nucleus cubic 47 hexagonal 62 water 3589 interfacial 240
nucleus axis x layers CHHHCHHHHHHHHH cubicity 0.142857
```

```python
    """Basal repeat, the same scan as science_render.layer_period."""
    best_score = -1.0
    best = 3.6
    centered = projection - float(np.mean(projection))
    for period in np.linspace(3.30, 4.05, 16):
        wave = np.exp(1j * (2.0 * math.pi / float(period)) * centered)
        score = float(np.abs(np.mean(wave)))
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best = float(period)
    return best

def layer_score(projection: np.ndarray, period: float) -> float:
    centered = projection - float(np.mean(projection))
    wave = np.exp(1j * (2.0 * math.pi / period) * centered)
    return float(np.abs(np.mean(wave)))

def layer_kinds(pos, chill, axis) -> list[int]:
    """Ih (1) or Ic (0) for each basal layer. Same rule as science_render."""
    chosen = np.flatnonzero(np.isin(chill, [0, 1]))
    axis = np.asarray(axis, dtype=float)
    axis = axis / np.linalg.norm(axis)
    projection = pos[chosen] @ axis
    kinds = chill[chosen]
    bins = np.floor((projection - projection.min()) / layer_period(projection)).astype(int)
    letters = []
    for index in range(int(bins.max()) + 1):
        selected = kinds[bins == index]
        hexagonal = int(np.sum(selected == 1))
        cubic = int(np.sum(selected == 0))
        if hexagonal + cubic == 0:
            continue
        letters.append(1 if hexagonal >= cubic else 0)
    return letters

def cubicity(kinds: list[int]) -> float:
    return sum(1 for kind in kinds if kind == 0) / float(len(kinds))
```

```c
  double mean = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    mean += projection[i];
  }
  mean /= (double)n;
  double best_score = -1;
  double best = 3.6;
  for (int step = 0; step < 16; step++) {
    double period = 3.30 + (4.05 - 3.30) * (double)step / 15.0;
    double re = 0;
    double im = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      double angle = (2.0 * 3.14159265358979323846 / period) * (projection[i] - mean);
      re += cos(angle);
      im += sin(angle);
    }
    double score = hypot(re, im) / (double)n;
    if (score > best_score) {
      best_score = score;
      best = period;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

static double layer_score(const double *projection, int n, double period) {
  double mean = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    mean += projection[i];
  }
  mean /= (double)n;
  double re = 0;
  double im = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    double angle = (2.0 * 3.14159265358979323846 / period) * (projection[i] - mean);
    re += cos(angle);
    im += sin(angle);
  }
  return hypot(re, im) / (double)n;
}

/* Returns the stacking string. axis is 0, 1, or 2. */
static void layer_string(const double *xyz, const int *chill, int n, int axis, char *out) {
  int crystal = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (chill[i] == 0 || chill[i] == 1) {
      crystal += 1;
    }
  }
  double *projection = malloc((size_t)crystal * sizeof(double));
  int *kinds = malloc((size_t)crystal * sizeof(int));
  int cursor = 0;
  double lo = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (chill[i] != 0 && chill[i] != 1) {
      continue;
    }
    projection[cursor] = xyz[3 * i + axis];
    kinds[cursor] = chill[i];
    if (cursor == 0 || projection[cursor] < lo) {
      lo = projection[cursor];
    }
    cursor += 1;
  }
  double period = layer_period(projection, crystal);
  int bins_max = 0;
  int *bin = malloc((size_t)crystal * sizeof(int));
  for (int i = 0; i < crystal; i++) {
    bin[i] = (int)floor((projection[i] - lo) / period);
    if (bin[i] > bins_max) {
      bins_max = bin[i];
    }
  }
  int length = 0;
  for (int index = 0; index <= bins_max; index++) {
    int hexagonal = 0;
    int cubic = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < crystal; i++) {
      if (bin[i] != index) {
        continue;
      }
      if (kinds[i] == 1) {
        hexagonal += 1;
      } else {
        cubic += 1;
      }
    }
    if (hexagonal + cubic == 0) {
      continue;
    }
    out[length++] = hexagonal >= cubic ? 'H' : 'C';
  }
  out[length] = '\0';
  free(projection);
  free(kinds);
  free(bin);
}

static int strongest_axis(const double *xyz, const int *chill, int n) {
  int crystal = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (chill[i] == 0 || chill[i] == 1) {
      crystal += 1;
    }
  }
  double *projection = malloc((size_t)crystal * sizeof(double));
  int best = 0;
  double best_score = -1;
  for (int axis = 0; axis < 3; axis++) {
    int cursor = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      if (chill[i] == 0 || chill[i] == 1) {
        projection[cursor++] = xyz[3 * i + axis];
      }
    }
    double period = layer_period(projection, crystal);
    double score = layer_score(projection, crystal, period);
    if (score > best_score) {
      best_score = score;
      best = axis;
    }
  }
  free(projection);
  return best;
}
```

![Primary prism face of the interface slab. Basal bilayers are vertical, growth runs up the page, and the cell is a rectangle.](../_images/interface.png)

*This is the primary prism face $(10\bar{1}0)$. The basal planes stand perpendicular to the interface, so the bilayers are vertical, and growth runs along z. The orthographic camera looks straight down x. The vertical axis reads `depth from lower ice surface (nm)`, the same axis as the brine figure, and the cell origin is the lowest hexagonal oxygen. Brackets with end ticks mark the liquid and the ice, with a gap between them. A dashed line across the cell is the growth front. The 1 nm bar is the on-screen length of 10 angstrom along the cell edge. The picture is clipped to one sphere radius outside the cell on every side. Liquid is radius 0.50 at 18 percent opacity. CHILL+ on the whole cell is 49 interfacial, 25 interfacial clathrate, 3 clathrate and 1 cubic. The picture keeps those colors only within 1.5 nm of the growth front. Farther from the front, everything except the hexagonal crystal is drawn as liquid. The classifier itself is unchanged. The legend is one row, in the same order as the brine figure.*

## What this tells you {#what-this-tells-you}

The slab is a hexagonal ice block against liquid. 352 molecules are
hexagonal, 434 are liquid, and 49 are the interfacial shell. One
molecule is cubic. The caption’s 25 interfacial clathrate and 3
clathrate molecules are the rest of the 864. Along z the old floor
bins count the cubic molecule as its own layer and the cubicity of
those nine bins is 1/9. The figure does not number it. The numbered
index is the basal stack: six bilayers of hexagonal ice. The nucleus
in the first saved frame is mixed: 47 cubic and 62 hexagonal molecules
in a liquid of 3589, with 240 interfacial. Molecule cubicity is
47/109. Along x, two of the fourteen layers are cubic-majority, so
the layer cubicity is 2/14. That mixed stacking is the quantity the
layer panel of the paper figure is drawn to show.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/science/brine.md -->

# Brine freezing front {#brine-freezing-front}

The
[d-SEAMS/brine-front-230K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/d-SEAMS/brine-front-230K)
dataset provides the initial and final frames for a 20-pair loading.
Download `T230_m20_r0_t0.xyz` and `T230_m20_r0_tend.xyz` before
running the analysis.

Each file stores a CHILL+ name on every oxygen. The engine is run again
on the oxygen coordinates. All 1496 oxygens match the stored names at
both times. Ice is hexagonal or cubic. Sodium is the ion, water is
type 1, the axis is z, and the bin count is 20. The rejection
coefficient is the bulk-ice molality divided by the bulk-liquid molality.

```text
brine t0 hexagonal 733 water 619 interfacial 91 cubic 1 agree 1496
brine t0 thickness 25.5618 k 0.0
brine tend hexagonal 741 water 621 interfacial 89 cubic 0 agree 1496
brine tend thickness 25.3740 k 0.0
```

```python
    box, rows = read_xyz(path)
    type_of = {"O": 1, "H": 2, "Na": 3, "Cl": 4}
    xyz = []
    types = []
    for species, x, y, z, _chill in rows:
        xyz.extend((x, y, z))
        types.append(type_of[species])
    count = len(rows)
    points = (ctypes.c_double * len(xyz))(*xyz)
    box9 = (ctypes.c_double * 9)(box[0], box[1], box[2], box[3], box[4], box[5], 0, 0, 0)
    kinds = (ctypes.c_int * count)(*types)
    system = lib.seams_system_create()
    if lib.seams_system_set_frame(system, points, count, box9, kinds, None) != 0:
        raise SystemExit(lib.seams_last_error())
    labels = (ctypes.c_int * count)()
    counts = (ctypes.c_int * 9)()
    if lib.seams_chill_plus(system, 3.5, 1, 0, 0, labels, counts) != 0:
        raise SystemExit(lib.seams_last_error())
    oxygen = [i for i, row in enumerate(rows) if row[0] == "O"]
    agree = sum(labels[i] == NAMES.index(rows[i][4]) for i in oxygen)
    histogram = {name: 0 for name in NAMES}
    for index in oxygen:
        histogram[NAMES[labels[index]]] += 1
    ice = (ctypes.c_int * count)(
        *[1 if rows[i][0] == "O" and labels[i] in (0, 1) else 0 for i in range(count)]
    )
    front = ctypes.c_void_p()
    # water type 1, sodium type 3, 20 bins, axis z.
    if lib.seams_brine_analyse(system, ice, count, 1, 3, 20, 2, ctypes.byref(front)) != 0:
        raise SystemExit(lib.seams_last_error())
    enter = ctypes.c_double()
    leave = ctypes.c_double()
    thick = ctypes.c_double()
    found = ctypes.c_int()
    if lib.seams_brine_fronts(
        front, ctypes.byref(enter), ctypes.byref(leave), ctypes.byref(thick), ctypes.byref(found)
    ) != 0:
        raise SystemExit("fronts")
    c_ice = ctypes.c_double()
    c_liquid = ctypes.c_double()
    coeff = ctypes.c_double()
    defined = ctypes.c_int()
    if lib.seams_brine_rejection(
        front, ctypes.byref(c_ice), ctypes.byref(c_liquid), ctypes.byref(coeff), ctypes.byref(defined)
    ) != 0:
        raise SystemExit("rejection")
    lib.seams_brine_destroy(front)
    lib.seams_system_destroy(system)
    return {
        "agree": agree,
        "oxygen": len(oxygen),
        "histogram": histogram,
        "found": int(found.value),
        "thickness": float(thick.value),
        "c_ice": float(c_ice.value),
        "k": float(coeff.value),
        "defined": int(defined.value),
    }
```

```c
  double *xyz = NULL;
  int *types = NULL;
  int n = 0;
  double box9[9];
  char(*chill)[16] = NULL;
  /* 4608 is the largest frame in this tutorial. Grow if the header says more. */
  FILE *probe = fopen(path, "r");
  char first[64];
  if (probe == NULL || fgets(first, sizeof first, probe) == NULL) {
    die(path);
  }
  fclose(probe);
  int declared = atoi(first);
  chill = calloc((size_t)declared, 16);
  if (read_xyz(path, &xyz, &types, chill, &n, box9) != 0) {
    die(path);
  }
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  if (seams_system_set_frame(sys, xyz, n, box9, types, NULL) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die("set_frame");
  }
  int *labels = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(int));
  int counts[9] = {0};
  if (seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 1, 0, 0, labels, counts) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die("chill+");
  }
  int agree = 0;
  int oxygen = 0;
  int histogram[9] = {0};
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (types[i] != 1) {
      continue;
    }
    oxygen += 1;
    histogram[labels[i]] += 1;
    if (strcmp(chill[i], LABELS[labels[i]]) == 0) {
      agree += 1;
    }
  }
  int *ice = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(int));
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    ice[i] = types[i] == 1 && (labels[i] == 0 || labels[i] == 1);
  }
  seams_brine *front = NULL;
  if (seams_brine_analyse(sys, ice, (size_t)n, 1, 3, 20, 2, &front) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die("brine");
  }
  double thickness = 0;
  int found = 0;
  double c_ice = 0;
  double coeff = 0;
  int defined = 0;
  if (seams_brine_fronts(front, NULL, NULL, &thickness, &found) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die("fronts");
  }
  if (seams_brine_rejection(front, &c_ice, NULL, &coeff, &defined) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die("rejection");
  }
  printf("brine %s hexagonal %d water %d interfacial %d cubic %d agree %d\n", tag,
         histogram[1], histogram[2], histogram[3], histogram[0], agree);
  printf("brine %s thickness %.4f k %.1f found %d defined %d\n", tag, thickness, coeff, found,
         defined);
  seams_brine_destroy(front);
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  free(xyz);
  free(types);
  free(labels);
  free(ice);
  free(chill);
  (void)oxygen;
}
```

![5 ns brine front with a color legend. Hexagonal ice is orange, the interface is yellow, liquid is a faint gray, clathrate is green, interfacial clathrate is pink, sodium is violet, and chloride is black.](../_images/brine.png)

*The 5 ns frame. Hydrogens are omitted. CHILL+ reports 741 hexagonal,
621 liquid, 89 interfacial, 41 interfacial clathrate, 4 clathrate,
and no cubic molecules. Sodium and chloride remain in the liquid.*

## What this tells you {#what-this-tells-you}

Over 5 ns at 230 K the hexagonal count moves from 733 to 741 and the
ice run stays near 25.5 angstrom. The bulk ice holds no sodium, so the
rejection coefficient is 0: the salt stays in the liquid. The printed
line names hexagonal, liquid, interfacial, and cubic. The other
oxygens are the 41 interfacial clathrate and 4 clathrate molecules in
the figure, and 741 + 621 + 89 + 41 + 4 is the 1496 that agree. The
stored labels and a fresh CHILL+ call name every oxygen the same way.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/science/cages.md -->

# sII and sH hydrate cages {#sii-and-sh-hydrate-cages}

`input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj` and `input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj`
are guest-free GenIce hosts, 136 waters each. sH keeps the triclinic
tilt. Closed cages are counted with `seams_cages_signature` at 3.5
angstrom on the cutoff graph. The signatures are `512` for
$5^{12}$, `51264` for $5^{12}6^{4}$, `sh` for
$4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and `51268` for $5^{12}6^{8}$.

```text
cages sII 512 16
cages sII 51264 8
cages sH 512 12
cages sH sh 8
cages sH 51268 4
```

```python
    system = lib.seams_system_create()
    if lib.seams_system_read(system, str(path).encode(), 1, -1) != 0:
        raise SystemExit(lib.seams_last_error())
    cages = ctypes.c_size_t()
    atoms = ctypes.c_size_t()
    if lib.seams_cages_signature(
        system, 3.5, 0, 0, spec.encode(), ctypes.byref(cages), ctypes.byref(atoms)
    ) != 0:
        raise SystemExit(lib.seams_last_error())
    lib.seams_system_destroy(system)
    return int(cages.value)
```

```c
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  if (seams_system_read(sys, path, 1, -1) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die(path);
  }
  size_t cages = 0;
  size_t atoms = 0;
  if (seams_cages_signature(sys, 3.5, 0, 0, spec, &cages, &atoms) != SEAMS_OK) {
    die(spec);
  }
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  return (int)cages;
}

static int cmd_cages(void) {
  printf("cages sII 512 %d\n", cages_of("input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj", "512"));
  printf("cages sII 51264 %d\n", cages_of("input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj", "51264"));
  printf("cages sH 512 %d\n", cages_of("input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj", "512"));
  printf("cages sH sh %d\n", cages_of("input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj", "sh"));
  printf("cages sH 51268 %d\n", cages_of("input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj", "51268"));
  return 0;
}
```

![sII cages. 5^12 polyhedra are orange and 5^12 6^4 polyhedra are blue.](../_images/sii.png)

*sII. Orange is $5^{12}$ and blue is $5^{12}6^{4}$, the hexagonal and cubic colors. The legend is titled sII and the frame includes every cage.*

![sH cages. 5^12 is orange, the medium cage is yellow, and 5^12 6^8 is green.](../_images/sh.png)

*sH. Orange is $5^{12}$, yellow is $4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and green is $5^{12}6^{8}$. Each face is the ring placed on the images nearest the cage center. A face is omitted when an edge reaches 3.5 angstrom or the planarity residual exceeds 0.35 angstrom. The legend is titled sH and the frame includes every cage.*

## What this tells you {#what-this-tells-you}

One sII cell holds 16 pentagonal dodecahedra and 8 of $5^{12}6^{4}$.
Four sH formula units hold 12 of $5^{12}$, 8 of
$4^{3}5^{6}6^{3}$, and 4 of $5^{12}6^{8}$. Those are the
cage numbers that separate the two hydrates. A count that dropped the
sheared sH edges would miss the cages whose bonds cross the xy tilt.

# Performance and comparisons {#performance-and-comparisons}

What to time, how the literature codes were run, and where d-SEAMS sits next to them.

[Benchmarks](howto/benchmarks.md)[Literature head-to-head](howto/literature-h2h.md)[Reproduce the literature head-to-head](howto/literature-reproduce.md)[Head-to-head](comparisons.md)

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/benchmarks.md -->

# Benchmarks {#benchmarks}

Time a 2.14.0 build and write down the run. The guest-code medians are
on [Literature head-to-head](literature-h2h.md). The thread
width each guest receives is on
[Reproduce the literature head-to-head](literature-reproduce.md).
The pinned neighbour session is
[Cutoff neighbour lists](neighbour-lists.md).

## Build {#build}

`pixi run build` configures `bbdir` with `-Dwith_tests=true` and
compiles it. The same two steps by hand:

```bash
meson setup bbdir --prefix=$CONDA_PREFIX -Dwith_tests=true
ninja -C bbdir
```

The timers are `bbdir/tests/bench_*`. `pixi run test` runs the test
suite and does not run them.

A host-only build takes the host branch of the device code.
`SEAMS_OFFLOAD=0` forces that path. `SEAMS_OFFLOAD=1` selects the
offload path when the build has one. Record the host, the compiler,
the commit, the thread count, the cpu affinity, and `SEAMS_OFFLOAD`.

The comparisons below use the Python scripts under `scripts/`.

## Neighbour list {#neighbour-list}

`bench_cutoff_list` times `nneigh::orthoFullCsr` and `neighListO` on
ideal ice Ic. The lattice constant is 6.35 Å and the cutoff is 3.5 Å.
Molecules must be `8 n^3`. The arguments are molecules, threads, and
repetitions. The defaults are 110592, 1, and 8. Every repetition is a
sample. The printed median is the sample at index `n/2` after sorting.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_cutoff_list 110592 1 8
```

`scripts/bench_neighbours_threads.py` runs that binary and the same
list in vesin, freud, and matscipy, at 10648, 110592, and 884736
molecules and at 1, 2, 4, and 8 threads. Set `NEIGH_BENCH` to the
binary. The script’s own default is
`build-release/tests/bench_cutoff_list`. `--reps` defaults to 8.
`--out` writes the lines.

## Triclinic list, CHILL+, rings, and diamond {#triclinic-list-chill-rings-and-diamond}

`bench_v2` takes a mode, a molecule count, a thread count, and a
repetition count. Molecules must be `8 n^3`. `tilt` builds the
triclinic cell, with `xy = 0.25 L`, `xz = 0.05 L`, and `yz = 0.12 L`.
Any other mode uses the orthorhombic cell. The cutoff is 3.5 Å and
the neighbour build is inside the timer. The first call is the
warm-up and is dropped. The printed median is again the sample at
index `n/2` after sorting.

| mode | what the timer includes |
| --- | --- |
| tilt | the triclinic cutoff list |
| chill | that list, then CHILL+ |
| rings | that list, then primitive rings to depth 6 |
| symmetry | that list, then the diamond common-neighbour label |

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_v2 tilt 110592 1 8
```

`rings` is a full search of one frame. The carried update is
`bench_hop_stride`, below. `scripts/bench_neighbours_v2.py` drives
`bench_v2` and the matching vesin, freud, mdapy, and OVITO calls.
Set `NEIGH_BENCH`. The script’s default is
`bbdir-release/tests/bench_v2`. An output path, when given, is the
first argument. `NEIGH_ONLY` limits the matrix to
`mode:molecules:threads`.

## Local q4 and q6 {#local-q4-and-q6}

`bench_ql` reads a frame: a little-endian `uint32` count, a `float64`
box length, then `n` times three `float64` coordinates. The arguments
are the frame, the degree, and the number of timed calls. One warm-up
runs first. The neighbour build, at cutoff 3.5 Å, is inside every
sample. A last path writes the warm-up $q_l$ as raw `float64`.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_ql frame.bin 6 8
```

`scripts/bench_ql_threads.py` builds ideal ice Ic at bond 2.75 Å and
one shifted liquid, and times degrees 4 and 6 against OVITO and
freud. `--out` is required. The binary is `SEAMS_QL_BENCH`, or
`bbdir-release/tests/bench_ql`, or `bbdir/tests/bench_ql`. One
warm-up, then eight samples. The median of an even count is the mean
of the two central values, and the interquartile range is
Hyndman-Fan type 7.

## Primitive rings against OVITO {#primitive-rings-against-ovito}

`bench_rings_h2h` times the ring search on a cutoff graph built
before the timer. `--repl` reads commands: `go` repeats that search,
`in` times the neighbour list, the index, and the search together,
and `quit` stops.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_rings_h2h input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj 1 2 3.5 6 8 2
```

The arguments after the dump are frame, atom type, cutoff, maximum
ring, repetitions, and warm-up. The defaults for the last two are 8
and 2. Type 2 is the oxygen in `exampleTraj.lammpstrj`.

`scripts/rings_one_thread.py` runs the binary and OVITO
`CreateBondsModifier` plus `FindRingsModifier` at one thread and at
eight. `--bench` is the binary and `--json` is the output path.

## Cage stage {#cage-stage}

Run `bench_cages` from `input/`. The default dump is
`traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj`, frame 1, three repetitions, atom type 1.
The later arguments are the HC template, the DDC template, and the
atom type. The templates in the tree are `templates/hc.xyz` and
`templates/ddc.xyz`.

```bash
cd input && ../bbdir/tests/bench_cages
```

Each printed time is the fastest repetition. The lines are the ring
network to depth 7, `findHC`, `findDDC`, both of those, local $q_6$,
and, when the templates load, the shape match. A nauty certificate of
the six-rings is included when nauty is linked.

`bench_ddc_ladder` times `findDDC` alone. Neighbours, rings, and
`findHC` run before the timer. The arguments are the dump, the
warm-up count, and the repetition count.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_ddc_ladder input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj 1 8
```

## Incremental updates {#incremental-updates}

`bench_churn_sweep` moves a ball of molecules from frame A to frame B
and times `RingUpdater` and `AffiliationUpdater` against a full pass.
Each printed time is the median of the repetitions. Every incremental
result is checked against the batch result.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_churn_sweep input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj
```

The optional arguments are frame A, frame B, cutoff, atom type,
repetitions, a ring full-pass fraction, and an affiliation batch
fraction.

`bench_trajectory_incremental` walks a dump. `RingUpdater` is checked
against `ringNetwork`, and `AffiliationUpdater` against the batch
affiliation. The graph is `cutoff`, `knn`, or `knn-union`. The
default graph is `knn`.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_trajectory_incremental input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj
```

The optional arguments are the frame count, the atom type, the
maximum ring depth, the skin, and the graph.

`bench_hop_stride` times the carried primitive-ring update against a
full search of the same frame. The graphs are the 3.5 Å cutoff list
and the seeded pair used by `seams cages`: mutual and union
4-nearest, candidate cutoff 5 Å, rings through depth 6. The names in
the log are `cutoff`, `seeded-strict`, `seeded-union`, and `seeded`.
One warm-up, then eight repetitions, unless `--reps` and `--warmup`
say otherwise. The printed carry and rebuild times are type-7
medians. The printed speedup is the sum of the per-frame median
rebuild times divided by the sum of the per-frame median carry times.
A transition is inside the ball when the update enumerates fewer
sources than the molecule count.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_hop_stride time input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --graph both
```

`crossover` uses `--frame-a` and `--frame-b`. `--type` selects the
atom type. The carried-ring definition is on
[Linkcell neighbours and carried updates](linkcell-carried.md).

## Device batch {#device-batch}

`bench_gpu_batch` reads a dump and prints `resident yes` or
`resident no`. A host build that cannot keep the frames on the device
stops there. When they stay resident, the log has the cold
upload, compute, and download, then the warm repeat with the smallest
compute time.

```bash
bbdir/tests/bench_gpu_batch input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj
```

The optional arguments are the frame count, the atom type, and the
number of warm repeats. The defaults are 11, 1, and 5.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/literature-h2h.md -->

# Literature head-to-head {#literature-head-to-head}

Two recorded comparisons of d-SEAMS 2.14.0. The eight-call session is
`scripts/h2h_literature.py`. The six-call sitting is
`scripts/h2h_rc3_sitting.py`, and its medians are the long table at
the end of this page. How that sitting sets a thread width is on
[Reproduce the literature head-to-head](literature-reproduce.md).

## Eight-call session {#eight-call-session}

`scripts/h2h_literature.py` drops one warm-up and times eight calls in
one process. The median of that even sample is the mean of the two
central values. The quartiles are Hyndman-Fan type 7, from
`quantile_linear` in `scripts/h2h_protocol.py`. That module’s own
`REPEATS` is 6. This script passes 8.
One thread is pinned with `taskset -c 0`. Eight threads are pinned
with `taskset -c 0-7`. The run records `Cpus_allowed_list` and does
not record the host name. The cutoff is 3.5 Å.

| code | version on the neighbour and ring rows | what is timed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | neighbours, q_4, q_6, diamond, metal CNA, rings |
| pyscal3 | 4.1.0 | neighbours, q_4, q_6, diamond, metal CNA |
| vesin | 0.6.2 | neighbour lists |
| SQQ | 0.5.8 | chordless shortest-path rings of size 4, 5, and 6 |
| IRA | reported by ira_mod | the 17-atom ice shell |
| ClavisCage | reported by clavis_engine | TRACE cages 5^{12}, 5^{12}6^{2}, 5^{12}6^{4} |
| PLUMED | reported by the plumed package | q_4, q_6, coordination |

IRA is imported as `ira_mod` from the conda-forge package `ira`.
ClavisCage is imported as `clavis_engine`. PLUMED is loaded from
`PLUMED_KERNEL` when that variable is set. A kernel without the
symfunc module has no Q4, Q6, or COORDINATIONNUMBER.

Frames come from `scripts/gen_ideal_ice.py` and stay in memory unless
`--out` is passed. The oxygen bond is 2.75 Å. Ice Ic is the 8-atom
cubic cell. Ice Ih is the 8-atom orthorhombic cell made from two
hexagonal primitives, so the box has no tilt. The supercells are 128,
4096, and 110592 molecules. `input/traj/dump-l.lammpstrj` frame 1 is
512 atoms of type 1. The box edge is 11.808 Å, the number density is
0.311 Å^{-3}, and the median number of neighbours inside 3.5 Å is 56.
The script labels that frame `liquid-mw`.
`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` contributes its 250 type-2
oxygens, phase `tip4p-o`. `input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj` is 46
oxygens and `input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj` is 136.

Agreement is per atom. Neighbour rows match when the neighbour sets
match. $q_l$ matches when every atom is within $10^{-6}$. Diamond
labels are compared after mapping d-SEAMS cubic (1) and hexagonal (0)
onto the mdapy and pyscal3 codes 1 and 4. Metal CNA is a different
label set and is reported against the diamond label, so an ice atom
that CNA calls other stays visible. Rings match when the size census
matches. For IRA, the 16 nearest neighbours inside 5 Å plus the atom
itself are matched to the ice Ih and ice Ic templates. The template
with the smaller distance is the label, and a distance above 0.2 Å
is left unclassified. `seams_symmetry_backend` is `kabsch` when
libira is not linked and `ira` when it is.

```bash
python3 scripts/h2h_literature.py --lib bbdir/src/libyodaLib.so
```

With no `--lib`, the library is
`SEAMS_CORE_LIB` or `build/src/libyodaLib.so`. `--sizes` defaults to
128, 4096, and 110592. `--once CODE OP` times one operation on one
phase. It reads `H2H_PYTHON` and `SEAMS_CORE_LIB`.

The neighbour and ring medians below are the stored rows
at 4096 and 110592 molecules. `n` is 8. d-SEAMS on these rows is
2.14.0. On ideal ice the script requires four neighbours per molecule
before it times the frame.

| code | phase | molecules | threads | operation | median ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 1.371 |
| mdapy | Ic | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 2.053 |
| pyscal3 | Ic | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 7.690 |
| vesin | Ic | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 2.137 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 4096 | 1 | rings | 4.772 |
| mdapy | Ic | 4096 | 1 | rings | 104.216 |
| SQQ | Ic | 4096 | 1 | rings | 647.521 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 0.899 |
| mdapy | Ih | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 1.888 |
| pyscal3 | Ih | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 7.176 |
| vesin | Ih | 4096 | 1 | neighbours | 1.706 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 4096 | 1 | rings | 4.367 |
| mdapy | Ih | 4096 | 1 | rings | 110.485 |
| SQQ | Ih | 4096 | 1 | rings | 680.332 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 31.603 |
| mdapy | Ic | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 45.102 |
| pyscal3 | Ic | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 225.169 |
| vesin | Ic | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 51.939 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 110592 | 1 | rings | 116.834 |
| mdapy | Ic | 110592 | 1 | rings | 2651.418 |
| SQQ | Ic | 110592 | 1 | rings | 18672.033 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 25.773 |
| mdapy | Ih | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 41.722 |
| pyscal3 | Ih | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 216.279 |
| vesin | Ih | 110592 | 1 | neighbours | 47.958 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 110592 | 1 | rings | 110.414 |
| mdapy | Ih | 110592 | 1 | rings | 2964.323 |
| SQQ | Ih | 110592 | 1 | rings | 19688.702 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 0.430 |
| mdapy | Ic | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 21.425 |
| pyscal3 | Ic | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 8.430 |
| vesin | Ic | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 2.604 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 4096 | 8 | rings | 1.653 |
| mdapy | Ic | 4096 | 8 | rings | 128.797 |
| SQQ | Ic | 4096 | 8 | rings | 630.689 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 0.413 |
| mdapy | Ih | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 21.357 |
| pyscal3 | Ih | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 7.865 |
| vesin | Ih | 4096 | 8 | neighbours | 1.810 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 4096 | 8 | rings | 1.738 |
| mdapy | Ih | 4096 | 8 | rings | 133.650 |
| SQQ | Ih | 4096 | 8 | rings | 676.038 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 10.358 |
| mdapy | Ic | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 62.965 |
| pyscal3 | Ic | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 216.041 |
| vesin | Ic | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 52.525 |
| d-SEAMS | Ic | 110592 | 8 | rings | 34.116 |
| mdapy | Ic | 110592 | 8 | rings | 2670.661 |
| SQQ | Ic | 110592 | 8 | rings | 18326.846 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 9.663 |
| mdapy | Ih | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 61.494 |
| pyscal3 | Ih | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 216.341 |
| vesin | Ih | 110592 | 8 | neighbours | 50.518 |
| d-SEAMS | Ih | 110592 | 8 | rings | 33.709 |
| mdapy | Ih | 110592 | 8 | rings | 2981.948 |
| SQQ | Ih | 110592 | 8 | rings | 21085.739 |

`seams_diamond_cna` builds the cutoff list when the shell occupancy
$n/V \times 4\pi r^3/3$ is at most 12, and the four nearest
neighbours when the occupancy is higher. The 512-atom frame is in
the second case: its median coordination inside 3.5 Å is 56. A
crystal shell stays on the cutoff list. The ideal cells are the
first case.

The cage rows orient hydrogens 0.96 Å along an out-degree-2
placement of the four nearest oxygen-oxygen bonds. On a crystal the
TRACE call uses a 0.35 nm cutoff and a 35 degree angle. On a crowded
shell the TRACE cutoff is 1.05 times the fourth-neighbour distance,
and it is not taken past 0.35 nm. d-SEAMS counts on the GenIce cells
in the test suite are 2 of $5^{12}$ and 6 of $5^{12}6^{2}$ on the
sI unit cell (46 oxygens), 16 and 48 on the $2\times2\times2$
replicate (368 oxygens), and 16 of $5^{12}$ and 8 of $5^{12}6^{4}$
on sII (136 oxygens).

PLUMED Q4 and Q6 store the norm of the averaged spherical-harmonic
vector and omit $\sqrt{4\pi/(2l+1)}$. The script multiplies by
that factor. The neighbour weight is a rational switch with
`R_0=3.5`, `D_MAX=3.5`, `NN=100`, and `MM=200`. This script does not
set `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS`. The timed PLUMED columns are in the sitting
below.

## Six-call sitting {#six-call-sitting}

`scripts/h2h_rc3_sitting.py` drops one warm-up and times six calls.
The median is the mean of the two central values. The interquartile
range is type 7. Ideal ice Ic uses oxygen bond 2.75 Å and cutoff
3.5 Å. The C API test locks ideal-ice $q_4$ at 0.509175077 and
$q_6$ at 0.628539361. Six-rings on that crystal are two per
molecule, 221184 at 110592 molecules.

The worker opens `bbdir-release/bindings/libseams_lang.so`. There is
no flag for another path.

```bash
python3 scripts/h2h_rc3_sitting.py
```

The run needs numpy, vesin, mdapy, freud, OVITO, ASE,
`rings_statistics_matter`, `clavis_engine`, `fastatomstruct`, and a
symfunc PLUMED. `PLUMED_LIB` names `libplumed.so`. Otherwise the
script takes it from the `plumed` executable on `PATH`. The vesin
probe runs first and stops the run if vesin is missing.

One thread is `taskset -c 0`. Eight threads are `taskset -c 0-7`.
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` is that width and `OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE`. The `cores`
column is `Cpus_allowed_list` read in the worker.
`widenAffinity` returns without changing the mask when the OpenMP
width is one thread. In this file the one-thread neighbour, CHILL+,
ring, and cage rows list `0-7`, and the one-thread $q_4$, $q_6$,
and PTM rows list `0`.

vesin is `NeighborList` with `full_list=True`, `algorithm`”cell_list”`, =n_threads` set to the row width, and the copy inside the timer. At
110592 molecules that median is 51.194 ms on one thread and 22.269 ms
on eight. `n_threads=0` would follow `OMP_NUM_THREADS`. This worker
passes the row width. A half list is a different pair count. The full
ice Ic list at 110592 molecules is 442368 directed pairs.

The PLUMED worker writes the version `2.10.2+symfunc`, converts
positions to nanometres, and cuts the rational switch at 0.35 nm.
It sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS` and does not set `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS`. In
PLUMED 2.10 `getNumThreads` reads `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS`, so both
thread columns of these PLUMED rows are the one-thread measurement.
The sitting that sets `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS` to the row width is on
[the performance overview](../../explanation/performance-overview.md).

`rings_statistics_matter.ring_statistics` is called with
`backend`”rust”= and `num_threads` equal to the row width. The
worker writes version 0.3.0. The OVITO polyhedral template match
enables structure ids 6 and 7 and leaves the other templates off.
The d-SEAMS cell on that row is `seams_frame_symmetry` with tolerance
0.12. Both are labeled PTM in the table.
`OVITO_THREAD_COUNT` is set before `import ovito`.

King’s shortest paths are `fastatomstruct` `RingMethod.King` through
size 6. A call that does not return inside 10 minutes is not written,
and the larger sizes for that width are skipped. Every size through
110592 molecules in this file did return.

On the GenIce cages, hydrogens are an ice-rule orientation of the
four nearest oxygens and are built before the timer. TRACE reads
that graph at 0.35 nm and 35 degrees. The driver builds the
$2\times2\times2$ sI replicate because TRACE drops a ring that
crosses the periodic boundary, and that replicate is the frame on
which the two counts are compared. The d-SEAMS counts are the ones
in the test suite, listed above.

On every row that shares an operation, a molecule count, and a thread
count, the d-SEAMS median is the smaller one.

The table columns are code, version, molecules, operation, threads,
cores, `n`, median, and the type-7 interquartile range.

| code | version | molecules | operation | threads | cores | n | median ms | IQR ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | neighbours | 1 | 0-7 | 6 | 28.325 | 0.440 |
| vesin | 0.6.2 | 110592 | neighbours | 1 | 0 | 6 | 51.194 | 1.190 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | q4 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 23.747 | 0.471 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | q4 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 64.687 | 1.094 |
| freud | 3.6.1 | 110592 | q4 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 276.580 | 5.118 |
| PLUMED | 2.10.2+symfunc | 110592 | q4 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 1310.025 | 43.492 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | q6 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 25.832 | 1.264 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | q6 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 79.232 | 1.587 |
| freud | 3.6.1 | 110592 | q6 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 362.326 | 1.594 |
| PLUMED | 2.10.2+symfunc | 110592 | q6 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 1685.454 | 19.344 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | CHILL+ | 1 | 0-7 | 6 | 24.102 | 0.308 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | CHILL+ | 1 | 0 | 6 | 61.938 | 0.226 |
| OVITO | 3.17.2 | 110592 | CHILL+ | 1 | 0 | 6 | 622.424 | 3.316 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | rings | 1 | 0-7 | 6 | 86.531 | 1.036 |
| OVITO | 3.17.2 | 110592 | rings | 1 | 0 | 6 | 583.334 | 7.617 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | rings | 1 | 0 | 6 | 2276.747 | 13.477 |
| rings-statistics-matter | 0.3.0 | 110592 | rings | 1 | 0 | 6 | 1151.862 | 46.483 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | PTM | 1 | 0 | 6 | 30.475 | 1.072 |
| OVITO | 3.17.2 | 110592 | PTM | 1 | 0 | 6 | 2790.624 | 78.803 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | neighbours | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 6.453 | 1.508 |
| vesin | 0.6.2 | 110592 | neighbours | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 22.269 | 1.481 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | q4 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 6.094 | 1.114 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | q4 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 12.400 | 0.324 |
| freud | 3.6.1 | 110592 | q4 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 51.302 | 7.021 |
| PLUMED | 2.10.2+symfunc | 110592 | q4 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 1316.423 | 26.240 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | q6 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 5.820 | 0.314 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | q6 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 14.572 | 0.478 |
| freud | 3.6.1 | 110592 | q6 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 68.760 | 9.206 |
| PLUMED | 2.10.2+symfunc | 110592 | q6 | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 1680.281 | 29.897 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | CHILL+ | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 5.697 | 0.204 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | CHILL+ | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 12.379 | 0.422 |
| OVITO | 3.17.2 | 110592 | CHILL+ | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 88.685 | 1.045 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | rings | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 32.665 | 0.343 |
| OVITO | 3.17.2 | 110592 | rings | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 354.605 | 17.902 |
| mdapy | 2.0.0 | 110592 | rings | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 375.967 | 3.766 |
| rings-statistics-matter | 0.3.0 | 110592 | rings | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 264.953 | 10.643 |
| d-SEAMS | 2.14.0 | 110592 | PTM | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 6.976 | 0.433 |
| OVITO | 3.17.2 | 110592 | PTM | 8 | 0-7 | 6 | 370.341 | 1.536 |
