<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/literature-reproduce.md -->

# Reproduce the literature head-to-head {#reproduce-the-literature-head-to-head}

`scripts/h2h_rc3_sitting.py` writes the six-call sitting. One warm-up,
then six timed calls. The median of that even sample is the mean of
the two central values, and the interquartile range is Hyndman-Fan
type 7. The medians are the long table on
[Literature head-to-head](literature-h2h.md). This page is how
each guest code receives a thread width, and what that width did to
the median.

The driver starts every row under `taskset`. One thread is
`taskset -c 0`. Eight threads are `taskset -c 0-7`. It sets
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` to that width and `OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE`. d-SEAMS
follows that OpenMP width. Each guest then receives the same width
through its own control, except PLUMED and ClavisCage.

| code | what is timed | thread control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| freud | local q_4 and q_6 | freud.parallel.set_num_threads(n) |
| OVITO | CHILL+, primitive rings, polyhedral template matching | OVITO_THREAD_COUNT=n before import ovito |
| mdapy | CHILL+, q_4, q_6, rings | mdapy.set_num_threads(n) |
| vesin | full cell-list neighbour pairs, copy included | NeighborList(..., n_threads=n, algorithm”cell_list”)= |
| PLUMED | symfunc q_4 and q_6 | OMP_NUM_THREADS is set. PLUMED_NUM_THREADS is not |
| rings-statistics-matter | primitive rings | ring_statistics(..., num_threads=n, backend”rust”)= |
| fastatomstruct | King’s shortest paths through size 6 | fastatomstruct.set_num_threads(n) |
| ClavisCage | TRACE cages | the analyze_waters call takes no thread count |

Polyhedral template matching is the OVITO modifier. Structure ids 6
and 7 are enabled and the other templates are left off. The d-SEAMS
cell on that row is `seams_frame_symmetry` with tolerance 0.12. Both
are labeled PTM. rings-statistics-matter is imported as
`rings_statistics_matter`.

The worker opens `bbdir-release/bindings/libseams_lang.so`. `PLUMED_LIB`
names `libplumed.so`; otherwise the script takes that library from the
`plumed` executable on `PATH`.

```bash
python3 scripts/h2h_rc3_sitting.py
```

The vesin probe runs first.

## What the medians do {#what-the-medians-do}

On ideal ice Ic at 110592 and 884736 molecules, freud, OVITO, mdapy,
vesin, and rings-statistics-matter are faster at eight threads than
at one. OVITO’s template matching and its ring finder fall with the
same `OVITO_THREAD_COUNT` as its CHILL+. `t1` and `t8` are the
medians in the threads=1 and threads=8 columns. `ratio` is `t1 / t8`.

PLUMED is the exception in this file. The driver sets
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` and leaves `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS` unset. In PLUMED
2.10 `PLMD::OpenMP::getNumThreads` reads `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS`, and an
unset variable is one thread. The `threads=1` column and the
`threads=8` column are that same measurement, so the ratio stays
near 1. The sitting that sets `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS` to the row width
is on [the performance overview](../../explanation/performance-overview.md).
ClavisCage also has no thread argument. On the sI unit cell the
medians are 51.122 ms and 51.206 ms. On the 368-oxygen replicate they
are 301.514 ms and 302.471 ms. On sII they are 69.332 ms and 69.657 ms.
The first number of each pair is one thread and the second is eight.

| code | operation | molecules | t1 ms | t8 ms | ratio | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| freud | q4 | 110592 | 276.580 | 51.302 | 5.39 |  |
| freud | q4 | 884736 | 2358.091 | 431.376 | 5.47 |  |
| freud | q6 | 110592 | 362.326 | 68.760 | 5.27 |  |
| freud | q6 | 884736 | 2973.372 | 550.161 | 5.40 |  |
| OVITO | CHILL+ | 110592 | 622.424 | 88.685 | 7.02 |  |
| OVITO | CHILL+ | 884736 | 4890.789 | 666.288 | 7.34 |  |
| OVITO | PTM | 110592 | 2790.624 | 370.341 | 7.54 |  |
| OVITO | PTM | 884736 | 21304.364 | 2849.382 | 7.48 |  |
| OVITO | rings | 110592 | 583.334 | 354.605 | 1.65 |  |
| OVITO | rings | 884736 | 4883.899 | 2582.748 | 1.89 |  |
| mdapy | CHILL+ | 110592 | 61.938 | 12.379 | 5.00 |  |
| mdapy | CHILL+ | 884736 | 744.487 | 125.578 | 5.93 |  |
| mdapy | q4 | 110592 | 64.687 | 12.400 | 5.22 |  |
| mdapy | q4 | 884736 | 807.101 | 96.238 | 8.39 |  |
| mdapy | q6 | 110592 | 79.232 | 14.572 | 5.44 |  |
| mdapy | q6 | 884736 | 921.574 | 107.347 | 8.59 |  |
| mdapy | rings | 110592 | 2276.747 | 375.967 | 6.06 |  |
| mdapy | rings | 884736 | 19221.718 | 3361.913 | 5.72 |  |
| vesin | neighbours | 110592 | 51.194 | 22.269 | 2.30 |  |
| vesin | neighbours | 884736 | 1112.702 | 196.866 | 5.65 |  |
| rings-statistics-matter | rings | 110592 | 1151.862 | 264.953 | 4.35 |  |
| rings-statistics-matter | rings | 884736 | 11504.451 | 2665.750 | 4.32 |  |
| PLUMED | q4 | 110592 | 1310.025 | 1316.423 | 1.00 | one thread; PLUMED_NUM_THREADS unset |
| PLUMED | q4 | 884736 | 10053.680 | 10122.158 | 0.99 | one thread; PLUMED_NUM_THREADS unset |
| PLUMED | q6 | 110592 | 1685.454 | 1680.281 | 1.00 | one thread; PLUMED_NUM_THREADS unset |
| PLUMED | q6 | 884736 | 12947.767 | 12818.837 | 1.01 | one thread; PLUMED_NUM_THREADS unset |

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/user/comparisons.md -->

# Head-to-head {#head-to-head}

Measured comparisons of d-SEAMS 2.14.0 with other structure codes.
The cage census is read out of the agreement text of the cage
comparison.

A time in the summary and cage tables is the median of `n` repeats.
The ratio is the other median divided by
the d-SEAMS median. In those two tables every stored ratio is greater
than 1: the other median is the larger time. Where a table has an
agreement column, that column is the stored agreement text through
the first semicolon. The cage timing table’s last column is the
cage name. The census under it is the rest of the agreement text.
Notes about serial calls are in the section prose.

## The three comparisons {#the-three-comparisons}

In the summary and cage tables, the version
column is the `version` field. A slash, when present, separates the
d-SEAMS version from the other code. Every summary row records
`cores` 8. A one-thread summary row records `cpus` 0. An
eight-thread summary row records `cpus` 0-7.

In the SQQ comparison, each timing row
records d-SEAMS 2.14.0 and SQQ 0.5.8. Those rows store
means. The summary tables store medians. The SQQ ratio is
`ratio_sqq_over_dseams`.

The 884736-molecule comparison of ice and a TIP4P/ice liquid is on
[Performance](../explanation/performance-h2h.md). On the TIP4P/ice liquid the table states a freud $q_6$ gap
of 1.525e-04, called hard-cutoff rounding there, and a PLUMED
$q_6$ gap of 1.679e-01, also written 0.168, called the rational
switch there. CHILL+ agrees on 830736 of 884736 molecules. The
$q_6$ table on this page is the summary comparison. Its agreement
column is the maximum absolute gap stored for that size.

## Neighbour lists {#neighbour-lists}

vesin 0.6.2 and freud 3.6.1. The agreement text is the matching
pair count.

## Local q6 {#local-q6}

mdapy 2.0.0, pyscal3 4.1.0, and PLUMED 2.10.0. For a given code and
size the stored gap is the same at one thread and at eight. mdapy
and pyscal3 also store the Lechner-Dellago average, `q6bar_max_abs`,
equal to the local gap on these rows. PLUMED stores only
`q6_max_abs`. These gaps are $10^{-16}$ and $10^{-15}$. The
liquid comparison’s 1.679e-01 PLUMED gap is described above.

## CHILL+ {#chill}

mdapy 2.0.0 matches the label on every molecule and stores the same
`q6_max_abs` as its q6 rows. ClavisCage 0.3.18 matches the label on
every molecule. The agreement text on the ClavisCage rows states
that this CHILL+ path is a serial loop. The table is the measured
time: the eight-thread ClavisCage median stays with the one-thread
median at each size.

pyscal3 4.1.0 has no finished CHILL+ row. The agreement text says
that version exports no CHILL or CHILL+ name, that
`common_neighbor_analysis` is adaptive CNA and returns fcc, hcp,
bcc, ico, and other, and that `diamond_structure` is extended CNA.
The same text says neither function is the Nguyen and Molinero
CHILL+ rule, and that PyPI’s latest pyscal3 is this same 4.1.0.
The rows are
recorded at one thread and at eight, with an empty molecule count.

| comparator | version | operation | molecules | threads | cores | n | d-SEAMS ms | other ms | ratio | agreement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ClavisCage | 2.14.0/0.3.18 | chill_plus | 4096 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 0.7255 | 4.5952 | 6.3335 | labels 4096 equal |
| mdapy | 2.14.0/2.0.0 | chill_plus | 4096 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 0.7184 | 2.6670 | 3.7122 | labels 4096 equal q6_max_abs 4.441e-16 |
| ClavisCage | 2.14.0/0.3.18 | chill_plus | 4096 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 0.4711 | 4.5363 | 9.6285 | labels 4096 equal |
| mdapy | 2.14.0/2.0.0 | chill_plus | 4096 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 0.5076 | 0.5913 | 1.1649 | labels 4096 equal q6_max_abs 4.441e-16 |
| ClavisCage | 2.14.0/0.3.18 | chill_plus | 110592 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 18.4099 | 113.8680 | 6.1851 | labels 110592 equal |
| mdapy | 2.14.0/2.0.0 | chill_plus | 110592 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 18.5351 | 56.9564 | 3.0729 | labels 110592 equal q6_max_abs 1.776e-15 |

## FindRings and the primitive census {#findrings-and-the-primitive-census}

The hexagon counts above are one check. The subset result is
another.

On K2,3, d-SEAMS reports three primitive 4-rings and OVITO
FindRings reports two, with a 3.5 Å cutoff giving six edges.
[Primitive rings and OVITO FindRings](../explanation/ovito-findrings.md)
lists the three cycles.

On the 864-atom frame `input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj`, cutoff
3.5 Å, the graph has 1929 bonds and this primitive census:
142 of size 3, 188 of size 4, 377 of size 5, 1143 of size 6, 257 of
size 7, 54 of size 8, 52 of size 9, and 449 of size 10. Every one of
those rings passes the Franzblau test, and the sum of
those bins is 2662. On the same trajectory, the bond count matches on
both sides, every listed d-SEAMS ring is primitive, and each FindRings
bin from size 4 through 10 is at most the primitive bin.

## Adaptive common-neighbour analysis {#adaptive-common-neighbour-analysis}

Three OVITO rows,
operation `cna`, version field 2.14.0, 4096 molecules, one thread,
`cores` 8, `n` 1. The version field does not name an OVITO
release. There is no stored time. The agreement text says the
modifier’s structure types are Other, FCC, HCP, BCC, and ICO, and
that an FCC control is 256 of 256 FCC.

Ice Ih: 4096 of 4096 molecules labelled `hexagonal_ice` by CHILL+
are Other. Coordination 4, 3 staggered and 1 eclipsed, on all 4096.

Ice Ic: 4096 of 4096 molecules labelled `cubic_ice` are Other.
Coordination 4, 4 staggered and 0 eclipsed, on all 4096.

Liquid: 222 of 4096 disagree. One `hexagonal_ice` molecule is
Other at coordination 4, with 3 staggered and 1 eclipsed. Forty-nine
`hydrate` molecules are Other at coordination 4, with 4 eclipsed
and 0 staggered. One hundred sixty-eight `interfacial_hydrate`
molecules are Other at coordination 4, with 3 eclipsed. Four
`interfacial_ice` molecules are Other at coordination 4, with 2
staggered, or 3 staggered and 0 eclipsed.

The same liquid text names four shifted-ice waters with 12
neighbours inside 3.5 Å: 690 at (4.490, 15.864, 50.345), 1673 at
(16.865, 18.399, 11.795), 1675 at (15.210, 17.036, 12.464), and
2304 at (16.902, 34.179, 1.355). An independent minimum-image count
in that text gives the same 12 ids. The nearest pair is 0.183 Å,
from the Gaussian shift.

SQQ cage rows in the summary file did not run. The version field is

here are the 4096-molecule TIP4P/2005 frame. The other frames are

On tip4p2005-4096 the edge and ring counts match. The record’s
resolution on the chordless 6-ring row says every primitive 6-ring
is inside that count, and that the reference enumeration is 4045.

The primitive-rule row stores d-SEAMS 1075, SQQ 1129, both 4042,

## Per-atom q4 and q6 {#per-atom-q4-and-q6}

Per-atom $q_4$ and $q_6$,
the Lechner-Dellago averages, and the mean of each, are compared on three
frames. Ideal ice Ih is `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`. Ideal ice Ic
is a diamond cell with a 2.75 Å bond, four cells on a side. The
liquid is that cell plus Gaussian noise of 0.9 Å, seed 91001. The
neighbour rule is the same in d-SEAMS, freud, and
pyscal3: a pair counts when its minimum-image distance is strictly
below 3.5 Å. The comparison runs at one thread and at eight.

pyscal3 is float64. Local $q_l$, the Lechner-Dellago average, and
the mean of each over atoms that have a shell agree to
$10^{-10}$. freud stores $q_l$ as float32. On the two crystals
the gap stays within 8 units in the last place
of that float32 value. On the liquid the spherical-harmonic sum is
accumulated in float32, and the residual stays
under $2 \times 10^{-5}$.

An empty shell is 0 in d-SEAMS and NaN in freud and pyscal3.
0 is the empty accumulator.
[Local q4 and q6](howto/q4-q6.md) records why that 0 stays:
a NaN would enter every mean and every CHILL+ label.

OVITO 3.15.5 has no `SteinhardtParametersModifier`. OVITO 3.17.2 $q_4$
and $q_6$ are timed in the 884736-molecule comparison on
[Performance](../explanation/performance-h2h.md).

## PLUMED on the ice Ih dump {#plumed-on-the-ice-ih-dump}

On `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, the PLUMED engine reports hexagonal 128,
six-rings 256, and $q_6$ within $5 \times 10^{-7}$ of 0.625855.
[PLUMED](howto/engine-plumed.md) is the engine page. The standalone
PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in
[PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/).

That check is the ice Ih dump. The summary $q_6$ table is the
median comparison with PLUMED 2.10.0, with maximum absolute gaps
from $2.220 \times 10^{-16}$ to $6.661 \times 10^{-16}$. The
liquid comparison is the 1.679e-01 rational-switch gap.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/architecture.md -->

# Architecture {#architecture}

d-SEAMS 2.14.0 is one C++ engine, `libyodaLib`. Callers link
`libseams`, `libseams_lang`, or both. `libseams` (`include/seams.h`) is
the C API. `libseams_lang` (`bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h`) is the C ABI.
Each library links `libyodaLib`. `libseams_lang` is a separate library
from `libseams`. The `seams` command is the command-line front on the
same engine.

The engine reads the trajectory. XYZ and LAMMPS dumps are built in.
`.pdb`, `.gro`, and `.dcd` need chemfiles, and `.con` needs readcon.
Without chemfiles the command refuses `.pdb`, `.gro`, and `.dcd`.
Without readcon it refuses `.con`. Every other suffix is read as a
LAMMPS dump.

Optional drivers for LAMMPS, GROMACS, OpenMM, and PLUMED live in this
repository.

Building the engine and the `seams` command takes a C and C++
toolchain. Python, Lua, R, Julia, Rust, and Fortran are not required
for that build.

## Language packages {#language-packages}

Each language is its own package. The package calls this engine. It
does not carry a second copy of a classifier. A package release carries
the engine version it was built against, so `pydseamslib==2.14.0`
calls the 2.14.0 engine.

| language | repository | package | calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python | PydSEAMSlib | pydseamslib | libseams (import dseams) and libseams_lang (import pydseams) |
| Lua, Fennel | yodaStruct | Git source, require("dseams") | libseams |
| R | dseams-r | dseams | libseams_lang |
| Julia | Dseams.jl | Dseams, Seams | Dseams calls libseams_lang. Seams calls libseams. Both are distributed through libseams_jll |
| Rust | dseams-rs | dseams-sys, dseams | libseams |
| Fortran | dseams-fortran | fpm Git dependency dseams | libseams |

[Use a language binding](../user/howto/bindings.md) has the install
commands.

## Why the name is yoda {#why-the-name-is-yoda}

The 1.x executable was `yodaStruct`. This repository builds `seams`.
It does not build `yodaStruct`. The compiled Python module is
`pydseams.yoda`. `_core` and `cyoda` are aliases of `yoda`. Lua loads
`require("dseams")`. `require("yoda")` is that table.

## Cutoff list {#cutoff-list}

The cutoff list is every pair inside the distance cutoff. The full
list, which the `seams` command builds, picks a builder from the build
and from the OpenMP team.

With several OpenMP threads, an orthorhombic box and a box that carries
tilt terms are searched with the engine’s cell list. A search that
returns a list is the cutoff list. One thread does not run that search.
`linkcell::pairs_within` (`lc_pairs_within_rows`) is the builder when
the cell list did not supply the pairs, the build includes linkcell,
and the call succeeds. [linkcell](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/linkcell)
is that library. This repository asks for linkcell 0.4.2 or newer.
linkcell’s release number is its own, and the 2.14.0 tag does not
name it. `libyodaLib` links one copy and exports the `lc_` symbols.

Vesin fills the list when it is built and linkcell produced nothing:
linkcell is absent, or the linkcell call failed. When neither library
produced a list, the search continues with a cell list and then a
direct loop over pairs.

`seams --features` prints the compile-time backends. `linkcell pairs_within` and `vesin cutoff fallback` are two of those lines, each
`enabled` or `disabled`, among OpenMP, MPI, readers, and the other
optional libraries. The printout is the build. It does not name which
builder ran for a frame. A linkcell failure prints `trying the next cutoff list`. A vesin failure prints `falling back to brute force`.

The bond graph is a separate choice. For `seams cages`, `--graph` is
`cutoff`, `knn`, `knn-union`, or `seeded`, and `seeded` is the default
for that command. The cutoff-list builder does not select the graph.
Which graph the six-rings are found on, and why that is a different
question from CHILL+, is [CHILL+ versus cages](chill-plus-vs-cages.md).

## Device paths {#device-paths}

Two optional device builds do different work.

OpenMP target offload is the Meson option `with_openmp_offload`. The
default is disabled. The build covers Steinhardt $Y_{lm}$ and the
cage score, as hop-bound six-rings and cage affiliation, on the
neighbour list the host built. `SEAMS_OFFLOAD` requests that path.
The default is off, and `0` keeps the work on the host. `seams cages`
with `--graph seeded`, the default, stays on the host either way.
`seams chill` and `seams chill-plus` run on the host.

gpulite is the Meson option `with_gpulite`. When that library is
linked, the engine provides `gpu::analyzeResident`, a CUDA batch of
frames that stays on the device. The batch is the cage score: linkcell
device k-nearest, the mutual four-nearest graph, primitive six-rings,
and HC/DDC labels. It needs that device k-nearest. Without it, the
call reports that the path is not built. The batch returns cage
labels. It does not compute CHILL, CHILL+, or $q_{lm}$. The `seams`
subcommands do not call `gpu::analyzeResident`.

## Runtime settings {#runtime-settings}

Defaults are compiled into the binary. A dotenv file (`SEAMS_CONFIG`,
or `./seams.env` when that file is present) fills keys that are still
unset. The process environment overrides the file. A flag on the
`seams` command overrides the value for the setting that flag names.
`seams --print-config` prints the resolved values.

The keys choose frames, workers, the default graph, and whether
offload was requested. The subcommand (`chill`, `cages`, `rings`, and
the others) is not one of the keys. Compile-time Meson options are not
in the file. [The command reference](../reference/cli.md) lists
the keys and the defaults.

## Two classifiers {#two-classifiers}

`libyodaLib` holds both ice classifiers. CHILL and CHILL+ label a
molecule from its four nearest neighbours. The cage score labels
hexagonal-cage and double-diamond-cage membership. The two results do
not imply each other. The argument, and the counts on the mixed TIP4P
dump, are on [CHILL+ versus cages](chill-plus-vs-cages.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/binding-overhead.md -->

# Binding overhead {#binding-overhead}

Ice Ih at 4096, 32768, and 110592 molecules. GenIce writes a cell
that is not already on disk. The oxygen sites are kept and scaled
from nanometers to angstroms.

The record is an 8-core Intel Xeon. It does not name the host. Each
seams binding is one process for both thread widths. The process sets
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` and `PLUMED_NUM_THREADS` to 1, then to 8, and calls
`seams_set_num_threads` at each width. freud runs inside the Python
process and uses the same widths. The 1-thread and 8-thread OVITO
rows are two processes, started with `OVITO_THREAD_COUNT` set to 1
and to 8. Each cell is the median of 8 repeats after one warmup, in
milliseconds. The median of an even sample is the mean of the two
central values. The number in parentheses is the interquartile range,
quartile 3 minus quartile 1, Hyndman-Fan type 7.

## Handles {#handles}

Read, the mutual 4-neighbour list, and the primitive-ring search
return a handle. The parser and the search run inside libseams. The
C, Fortran, Lua, and ctypes drivers destroy a neighbour or ring
handle inside the timed section. The C++ wrapper destroys that handle
when the owning object leaves scope. On the 110592-molecule cell at 1
thread, Python read is the slowest measured wrapper of read and the
neighbour list: 47.209 ms against the C read median of 43.195 ms, a
ratio of 1.09.

`seams_rings_find` stores the primitive rings through size 6 on the
3.5 angstrom cutoff graph. A 5-ring is marked as a pentagon and a
6-ring as a hexagon. Prism, cage, and stacking labels are written
when `seams_rings_labels` reads the symmetry. The timed calls leave
that symmetry unread, so the prism pass stays out of the measurement.
At 4096 molecules the C median is 991.813 ms at 1 thread and
1561.161 ms at 8 threads. Every binding is repeated at that size. The
C search is also recorded at 32768 molecules, 65237.213 ms at 1
thread and 62041.600 ms at 8 threads. The 110592-molecule ring cells
are empty. A probe of that search had not returned after several
minutes.

At 4096 molecules the Python ctypes ring call is 1344.104 ms at 1
thread, 1.36 times C, and 1909.255 ms at 8 threads, 1.22 times C. The
other languages stay with the C time. Julia and R copy the ring
vertices out of the handle. Fortran also fills a size histogram and
the fraction of atoms on six-membered rings. Those extras sit inside
the C time.

## Per-molecule results {#per-molecule-results}

CHILL writes one label per molecule. The call is original CHILL,
published edges, on the cutoff graph. The timed q6 call writes q6 and
the Lechner-Dellago average q6bar, one double each per molecule, on
the 3.5 angstrom cutoff graph. A null q6bar pointer passed to
`seams_steinhardt` skips that average. The C, C++, and Fortran
drivers, and the ctypes worker, pass both caller-owned buffers. The
C++ wrapper allocates the averaged vector only when the caller asks
for it, and this call asks for it. On the 110592-molecule cell at 1
thread, Lua q6 is 33.288 ms, 1.05 times the C median of 31.822 ms.
The ctypes worker is 33.806 ms on that cell, 1.06 times C.

R times each call with `proc.time` elapsed time. On the calls that
finish in a few milliseconds the R medians fall on whole
milliseconds.

## freud and OVITO {#freud-and-ovito}

freud and OVITO are timed in the same session, on the same oxygen
coordinates. The freud rows are the neighbour query and q6. The OVITO
rows are read, a 4-neighbour finder, q6, and rings.

The seams neighbour list is the mutual 4-nearest graph. Candidates
lie inside 5 angstroms, the 3.5 angstrom cutoff plus 1.5. freud’s
query is the one-way 4-nearest list inside that same shell. OVITO’s
finder is `NearestNeighborFinder` with 4 neighbours. freud’s q6 call
is Steinhardt with l = 6, the averaged parameter, and a neighbour
shell of 3.5 angstroms. OVITO’s Steinhardt modifier uses that cutoff,
maximum degree 6, and the averaged parameters. OVITO’s ring row
creates bonds at 3.5 angstroms and then runs FindRings with a maximum
ring size of 6. That search is a different census from
`seams_rings_find`.

## Eight threads {#eight-threads}

Neighbour lists and CHILL take longer at 8 threads than at 1 thread,
at every size, in every language. q6 on the 4096-molecule cell is
faster at 8 threads: C falls from 0.950 ms to 0.550 ms, and the
languages with a finer clock follow it. R stays at 1 ms on that cell.
On the 32768-molecule cell C q6 rises from 9.065 ms to 278.258 ms,
and on the 110592-molecule cell from 31.822 ms to 294.849 ms.
Primitive rings at 4096 molecules are slower at 8 threads as well.
freud and OVITO neighbour and q6 calls are faster at 8 threads at
every size. The language bindings follow libseams.

![Median time of each binding divided by the direct C call](../_images/binding-overhead.png)

*Median time divided by the direct C call. The vertical axis is logarithmic, so a wrapper near 1 and a separate analysis sit on the same axes.*

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/c-api.md -->

# The C API {#the-c-api}

`include/seams.h` is ABI 1 of `libseams`. Language bindings and engine
plugins include that header and link `libseams`. `seams.h` includes
`seams_version.h`. The headers under `src/include/internal` belong to
the engine.

## Handles {#handles}

The public types are opaque. `seams_system` is one frame.
`seams_neighbours` is one neighbour list. `seams_rings` is one set of
primitive rings. `seams_cage_set` is hexagonal and double-diamond
membership. `seams_brine` is one planar ice front. `seams_topo` is the
topological fingerprint of one bonded frame. No public struct has
fields.

Each handle comes from a create, build, find, or analyse call and is
released by the matching destroy function. `seams_system_create`
starts an empty frame. A null pointer passed to a destroy function is
ignored. A second destroy of the same pointer records “double
destroy” and frees nothing.

The library copies every array a caller passes in. A handle built
from a frame holds its own copy, so the frame may be destroyed
first. Results are written into caller buffers. Strings the library
returns are static, or they stay owned by the library.

`seams_neighbours_csr` is the ABI 1 exception. It is marked
`SEAMS_DEPRECATED` and returns offset and column pointers owned by
the neighbour handle. Those pointers remain valid until
`seams_neighbours_destroy`. The columns omit the self index.
`seams_neighbours_copy` writes the same CSR into caller buffers. A
null buffer queries the length.

## Status and errors {#status-and-errors}

A call that can fail returns `seams_status`. Zero is `SEAMS_OK`. The
other codes are `SEAMS_ERR_NULL`, `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE`, `SEAMS_ERR_BOX`,
`SEAMS_ERR_ARG`, `SEAMS_ERR_STATE`, `SEAMS_ERR_NOMEM`, and
`SEAMS_ERR_INTERNAL`.

A failing call stores a detail string. `seams_last_error` and
`seams_last_error_message` return that thread-local string. When the
call had a handle, `seams_handle_error` returns the copy stored on
the handle. A null handle argument returns the thread-local string.
The handle string survives a later call on a different handle. The
next call that takes the same handle non-const clears the handle
string on entry. A successful call on this thread leaves the
thread-local string empty. A const call writes the handle string
only when it fails, so a successful const call leaves the previous
failure in place.

No C++ exception crosses this boundary. Each one is caught and
returned as a status. The version and name queries, the destroy
functions, and the ABI 1 counts `seams_system_count`,
`seams_neighbours_count`, and `seams_rings_count` return no status.
A null handle gives those counts the value 0.

## Lengths {#lengths}

Caller buffers take a `size_t` length. A null output buffer with a
length pointer queries the required count and returns `SEAMS_OK`. A
short buffer returns `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE`, leaves that buffer
untouched, and still writes the required count.

ABI 1 kept an `int` atom count on `seams_system_set_frame` and
`seams_system_set_ortho`. It also kept `seams_chill_plus`,
`seams_q4q6`, `seams_rings_labels`, and `seams_rings_histogram`
without a caller-supplied length. The length-checked spellings are
`seams_system_set_atoms`, `seams_system_natoms`,
`seams_neighbours_nrows`, `seams_rings_nrings`,
`seams_chill_plus_n`, `seams_q4q6_n`, `seams_rings_labels_n`, and
`seams_rings_histogram_n`. A count that does not fit in the frame’s
integer width is `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` on the `size_t` entry as well.

## ABI {#abi}

`SEAMS_ABI` is 1, and `seams_abi` returns it. The number stays 1
while every shipped function keeps its signature and every shipped
enumerator keeps its numeric value. New functions and new
enumerators are appended. `SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF` is 0,
`SEAMS_GRAPH_MUTUAL` is 1, and `SEAMS_GRAPH_SEEDED` is 2. A later
struct, if one is added, starts with a `uint32_t` size set by the
caller to the size of the struct that caller compiled. The library
reads only the prefix that size covers.

`SEAMS_API` marks every exported symbol. The rest of the library is
hidden. `SEAMS_VERSION_MAJOR`, `SEAMS_VERSION_MINOR`,
`SEAMS_VERSION_PATCH`, `SEAMS_VERSION_STRING`, and
`SEAMS_VERSION_NUMBER` are the version of the header.
`seams_version` returns the `SEAMS_VERSION_NUMBER` the library was
built with, packed as `(major << 16) | (minor << 8) | patch`. This
release is 2.14.0. The header and the library disagree when
`seams_version` and `SEAMS_VERSION_NUMBER` differ.

## Threads {#threads}

Distinct handles may run on distinct threads at the same time. One
non-const call owns its handle until it returns. Const calls on one
handle may run together while that handle has no non-const call in
progress. When threads share a handle, read the failure with
`seams_last_error_message`. The handle slot holds whichever failure
landed last.

`seams_ql`, `seams_q4q6`, `seams_q4q6_n`, `seams_q6bar`, and
`seams_steinhardt` keep their `q_lm` work arrays on the calling
thread, so those calls may run at the same time on different
handles. `seams_set_num_threads` is process-global. Call it while
no analysis is running. The stored width is the OpenMP team every
later analysis requests. A positive argument sets that width. Zero
restores the width captured at first use. A negative width is
`SEAMS_ERR_RANGE`.

`seams_chill`, `seams_chill_plus`, and `seams_chill_plus_n` write
each atom’s label into the stored frame. Coordinates, the cell,
types, and ids stay as they were. A load replaces the stored frame,
and on failure the previous frame stays. Every other analysis
clears the error slot and leaves coordinates, the cell, types, and
ids unchanged.

## Coordinates {#coordinates}

Coordinates and cutoffs are Angstrom. The cell is nine doubles:
origin `ox, oy, oz`, edge lengths `lx, ly, lz`, then the tilts
`xy, xz, yz`. A zero tilt is orthorhombic.

A cutoff neighbour is kept when the squared minimum-image distance
is strictly below the cutoff squared. `seams_neighbours_build` with
`SEAMS_GRAPH_MUTUAL` keeps the four nearest neighbours inside
cutoff + 1.5. That call rejects `SEAMS_GRAPH_SEEDED`. Cage searches
accept the seeded graph: mutual seeds, then union completions. A
zero neighbour count on a seeded search selects 4.

A non-positive `shell_rmsd` passed to `seams_system_symmetry`
selects the library ceiling, the scale-free second-shell residual
0.15. The label is 0 for ice Ih, 1 for ice Ic, 2 for stacking
disorder, and -1 when the shell does not match.

`seams_q6bar` counts finite values strictly above `ice_cut`. The
nucleation census uses 0.36. The mean and the median ignore
non-finite values, and an empty finite set stores 0.

A trajectory loop calls `seams_system_set_atoms` for the first
frame and `seams_system_set_positions` for each later frame of the
same length. The later call writes coordinates.

## What a caller can run {#what-a-caller-can-run}

| call | analysis |
| --- | --- |
| seams_system_set_atoms / seams_system_set_frame | coordinates and a nine-number cell |
| seams_system_read / seams_path_nframes | one trajectory frame; the index starts at 1 |
| seams_neighbours_build | cutoff list, or the mutual four nearest inside cutoff + 1.5 |
| seams_neighbours_knn | k nearest inside cutoff + 1.5, mutual or one-way |
| seams_rings_find | Franzblau rings; the largest size runs from 3 to 12 |
| seams_ql / seams_steinhardt | q_l for l of 3, 4, 6, 8, or 12, and the Lechner-Dellago average |
| seams_q4q6 | local q4 and q6 on the cutoff shell |
| seams_q6bar | q6-bar, its mean and median, and the count above ice_cut |
| seams_chill | original CHILL, inclusive edges or the OVITO open edges |
| seams_chill_plus | CHILL+, the 2015 four-neighbour rule or the OVITO shell |
| seams_cages | hexagonal and double-diamond membership |
| seams_signature_cages | closed cages of one ring census |
| seams_rdf / seams_running_cn / seams_coordination | partial g(r) and the coordination number |
| seams_hbonds | hydrogen-bond count |
| seams_density_axis | number density along one cell axis |
| seams_fingerprint | topological key of the bonded graph |
| seams_prisms | perfect and deformed prism counts |
| seams_monolayer | primitive-ring histogram of a monolayer |
| seams_site_table | per-atom site kind from a site spec |
| seams_contact_pairs | mutual nearest unlike contacts |
| seams_domains | largest polar or apolar domain |
| seams_system_symmetry | ice Ih, ice Ic, stacking disorder, or no match |
| seams_brine_analyse | planar front, rejection coefficient, profile, and pockets |

`seams_cages` is the same search as `seams_cages_find`.
`seams_signature_cages` is the same search as `seams_cages_signature`.
`seams_steinhardt` is `seams_ql` on the cutoff graph. The mutual
graph of `seams_ql` reads the four nearest neighbours inside
cutoff + 1.5. `seams_signature_cages_edge` takes the same census
with an explicit face-edge window. A null or empty window keeps
2.65 to 3.15 in the coordinate units of the file. The text `none`
leaves the cage bound to the face census.

`seams_system_read` reads CON when readcon is linked. Every other
file goes through chemfiles when that library is linked. XYZ and
LAMMPS dump also have a native reader, and a tilted dump is stored
as the nine-number cell above. A negative type filter keeps every
atom. Zero guesses the oxygen species. A positive value keeps that
species number.

The bond rows of the 2015 CHILL+ rule and of the OVITO modifier are
on [CHILL+: the published rule and the
OVITO rule](chill-plus-rules.md).

## OVITO and freud {#ovito-and-freud}

d-SEAMS keeps a cutoff neighbour when the minimum-image distance is
strictly below the cutoff. Freud uses the same open ball. OVITO’s
uniform bond modifier also keeps a pair that sits on the cutoff.
Two particles 3.5 Å apart are a bond in OVITO, and d-SEAMS and freud
leave that pair out. A separation of 3.5 Å minus 1e-4 Å is a
neighbour in all three.

`seams_neighbours_knn` writes an undirected row. With the mutual
flag clear, an edge is kept when either atom lists the other among
its k nearest. With the flag set, both atoms must list each other.
Freud and OVITO return the directed k nearest. Closing those
directed lists the same way reproduces the C rows. Four points on a
line at 0, 1, 3, and 6 Å, with k = 1, put both adjacent indices in
the one-way row of the point at 1 Å. The mutual row of that point
holds only the point at 0 Å.

Local `q_l` is the norm of the spherical harmonic of the cutoff
shell. q6-bar is the Lechner-Dellago norm of the mean `q_6m`, and
the atom itself is in that mean. Three oxygens at (0, 0, 0),
(2, 0, 0), and (0, 2, 0), with a cutoff of 2.5 Å, follow that mean.
The value differs from the mean of the scalar q6 numbers. Two
oxygens 2 Å apart give q6 = 1. An empty shell is stored as 0.
Freud 3.6 stores `q_l` in float32. Rounding the same `q_6m` to
float32 before the norm is the residual against a float64 sum.

`seams_chill_plus` with `SEAMS_CHILL_OVITO` averages `q_lm` over
every neighbour inside the cutoff and uses the modifier’s open
edges. `SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED` is Nguyen and Molinero, J. Phys.
Chem. B 2015, equation 1: the four closest neighbours, with
inclusive edges. `seams_chill` is Moore’s four-neighbour rule.
`SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED` uses the inclusive `c_ij` edges, and
`SEAMS_CHILL_OVITO` uses the open edges.

`seams_system_symmetry` and OVITO polyhedral template matching, with
the cubic and hexagonal diamond structures enabled and an RMSD
cutoff of 0.1, name the same atoms on ice Ih and on the generated
ice Ic lattice. That lattice sits on the cubic-diamond template,
with RMSD below 1e-6. The ice Ih file stays under 0.1. Where the
two labels differ, a kernel crystal that the template matcher calls
other has RMSD above 0.1, and a template-matcher diamond that the
kernel leaves unlabeled has RMSD below 0.1. The kernel ceiling on
that comparison is the second-shell residual 0.15.

`seams_rdf` counts each unordered like-species pair once and
normalises by `N(N-1)/2`. OVITO, and freud in its exact mode,
normalise the directed histogram by `N^2`. The histograms differ by
`N/(N-1)`. Multiplying the d-SEAMS values by `(N-1)/N` recovers the
directed normalisation, including the bin centers. The coordination
number from `seams_coordination` carries the same factor, so the
neighbour degree is that integral times `(N-1)/N`. On the 64-atom
ice Ic cell the factor is 64/63. A degree of 4 is an unscaled
coordination of 256/63.

Freud refuses an `r_max` past half the shortest edge. d-SEAMS still
bins minimum-image distances on a 10 Å cell out to 6 Å. A float32
distance can move a pair across one bin edge.

A pair placed 0.1 Å inside opposite faces of a 10 Å cell whose
origin is (2, 2, 2) Å has a minimum-image distance of 0.2 Å. That
pair is a cutoff neighbour in d-SEAMS, freud, and OVITO.

## Install {#install}

The install provides `seams.h`, `seams_version.h`, and the C++
wrapper `seams.hpp`. The shared library is `libseams.so` on Linux,
`libseams.dylib` on macOS, and `seams.dll` on Windows. `seams.pc`
is the pkg-config file. `seams-config.cmake` and
`seams-config-version.cmake` are installed under `cmake/seams/` in
the library directory.

```sh
pkg-config --cflags --libs seams
```

`examples/c/quickstart.c` builds against that install. The Meson
file in `examples/c` uses `dependency('seams')`. The CMake file uses
`find_package(seams)` and the imported target `seams::seams`.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/chill-plus-rules.md -->

# CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule {#chill-the-published-rule-and-the-ovito-rule}

Nguyen and Molinero, *J. Phys. Chem. B* 2015, 119, 9369
([10.1021/jp510289t](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp510289t)), equation 1
averages $q_3$ over the four nearest neighbours of a shell that
already holds four neighbours inside the cutoff. Table 1 gives the
bond rows. A staggered bond is $c(i,j) \le -0.8$. An eclipsed bond
lies on $-0.35 \le c(i,j) \le 0.25$. Those edges are closed.
Footnote a of Table 1 is the neighbour test: two staggered bonds need
a neighbour with more than two staggered bonds, and three staggered
bonds with no eclipsed bond need a neighbour with more than one.

The OVITO 3.17.2 Chill+ modifier
([Chill+](https://docs.ovito.org/reference/pipelines/modifiers/chill_plus.md))
averages $q_3$ over the whole cutoff shell. Its staggered edge is
the open cut $c(i,j) < -0.8$, and the eclipsed band is open at both
ends. The modifier skips the neighbour test in footnote a.
`seams ovito-chill+` and `seams chill-plus --rule ovito-chill+`
implement that rule. `seams chill-plus` with no `--rule` is the 2015
rule.

## One oxygen from the liquid {#one-oxygen-from-the-liquid}

`input/chill-def/liquid-four-nearest.txt` is an 18-atom piece of the
TIP4P/ice liquid. The focus is atom 1, the second oxygen in the file.
Its cutoff shell holds four neighbours. One of those neighbours has a
fifth oxygen inside 3.5 Å, so the whole-shell average of $q_3$
moves off the four-nearest average. None of the four correlations sits on
`-0.8`, `-0.35` or `0.25`.

The published rule counts two eclipsed bonds and labels atom 1 water.
`ovito-chill+` counts three eclipsed bonds and labels atom 1
interClathrate. That is the one atom the fixture is built to move.

```text
fixture focus 1 published water ovito interClathrate
```

## The 4096-molecule liquid {#the-4096-molecule-liquid}

On the 4096-molecule TIP4P/ice liquid
(`tests/data/tip4pice-liquid-4096.txt`), 250 of 4096 oxygens differ
between the published rule and OVITO 3.17.2. Every one of the 250 has
four neighbours inside 3.5 Å. 235 of them change an eclipsed or
staggered count because a neighbour has a fifth oxygen in the shell:
that is the $q_3$ average. The other 15 keep those bond counts and
differ on the neighbour test alone. `ovito-chill+` matches the OVITO
modifier on all 4096 atoms.

Ideal cubic ice stays cubic under both rules. The bundled cell
`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj` is 4096 cubic molecules under each
rule. Ideal ice Ih (`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`) stays hexagonal
under both rules, 128 of 128.

## Names of the two rules {#names-of-the-two-rules}

`seams chill-plus` takes `--rule chill+` or `--rule ovito-chill+`.
The command `seams ovito-chill+` is the second of those. On the ice
Ih frame each of these prints `nop 128 hexagonal 128`.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1 --rule chill+
seams chill-plus input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1 --rule ovito-chill+
seams ovito-chill+ input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 1
```

The C call `seams_chill_plus` takes `SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED` or
`SEAMS_CHILL_OVITO`. A type argument of 0 keeps every atom.
`seams_frame_chill_plus_rule` takes the strings `chill+` and
`ovito-chill+`. A positive type keeps that LAMMPS species. On ice Ih
the atoms are type 1, and both calls label 128 hexagonal molecules.

```c
seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels, counts);
seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_OVITO, labels, counts);
seams_frame_chill_plus_rule(frame, 3.5, 1, "cutoff", "chill+", labels, counts);
seams_frame_chill_plus_rule(frame, 3.5, 1, "cutoff", "ovito-chill+", labels, counts);
```

Python, in pydseamslib, is `dseams.chill_plus`. `dseams.PUBLISHED` is
the 2015 rule. `dseams.OVITO` is the OVITO rule. The eight-molecule
conventional ice Ic cell below (oxygen spacing 2.75 Å) is cubic under
both rules. The first population count is cubic.

```python
import math
import numpy as np
import dseams

a = 2.75 * 4.0 / math.sqrt(3.0)
fcc = np.array([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [0.5, 0.5, 0.0], [0.5, 0.0, 0.5], [0.0, 0.5, 0.5]])
basis = np.array([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [0.25, 0.25, 0.25]])
positions = ((fcc[:, None, :] + basis[None, :, :]) * a).reshape(-1, 3)
box = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, a, a, a, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
labels, counts = dseams.chill_plus(positions, box, rule=dseams.PUBLISHED)
assert len(labels) == 8 and int(counts[0]) == 8 and int(counts.sum()) == 8
labels, counts = dseams.chill_plus(positions, box, rule=dseams.OVITO)
assert len(labels) == 8 and int(counts[0]) == 8 and int(counts.sum()) == 8
```

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md -->

# CHILL+ versus cages {#chill-versus-cages}

Two classifiers in the engine library `libyodaLib` answer different
questions. A CHILL+ label does not imply a cage, and a cage label
does not imply a CHILL+ label.

## Four-neighbour star {#four-neighbour-star}

CHILL (`seams chill`, `chill::getCorrel` / `getIceTypeNoPrint`) and
the published CHILL+ call (`seams chill-plus`, `chill::getCorrelPlus`
/ `getIceTypePlusNoPrint`) read the bond star of an oxygen.

CHILL is Moore et al., *Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.* 2010, 12, 4124
(DOI 10.1039/b919724a). It averages
$q_3$ over the four nearest neighbours. A staggered bond is
$c(i,j) \le -0.8$. An eclipsed bond lies on
$-0.2 \le c(i,j) \le -0.05$. The label is read from those four
bonds, so a cutoff shell of five or more neighbours can still be ice
when the four nearest bonds match. The labels are cubic, hexagonal,
interfacial, and water.

CHILL+ is Nguyen and Molinero, *J. Phys. Chem. B* 2015, 119, 9369
([10.1021/jp510289t](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp510289t)). The
eclipsed window is $-0.35 \le c(i,j) \le 0.25$. A crystal,
clathrate, or interfacial label needs exactly four neighbours inside
the cutoff. That count is the cutoff shell, taken before the bond
list is reduced to the four nearest. $q_3$ is the average over
those four neighbours. The labels are cubic, hexagonal, interfacial,
clathrate, interfacial clathrate, and water.

A molecule is cubic or hexagonal when its four bonds look like ice,
even when those neighbours do not close a cage.

The OVITO form of CHILL+ averages $q_3$ over the whole cutoff
shell. That comparison is
[the published rule and the OVITO rule](chill-plus-rules.md).

## Cage membership {#cage-membership}

The ice score (`seams cages`, `ring::seededCageAffiliation` by
default) is cage membership. A molecule in a hexagonal cage (HC) is
ice Ih. A molecule in a double-diamond cage (DDC) is ice Ic. A
molecule in both is counted as both. A molecule in neither is water.
The cages are assembled from six-membered primitive rings on a chosen
bond graph.

This is topological unit matching (TUM). The methods paper is the
2020 JCIM article (see [Citation](citation.md)).

The GPU path (`gpu::analyzeResident`) is that TUM ice score only:
`linkcell::gpu` k-nearest, the mutual four-nearest graph, primitive
six-rings, and HC/DDC affiliation. CHILL, CHILL+, and $q_{lm}$ stay
on the host. Only cage labels come back.

## Why they disagree {#why-they-disagree}

A configuration can share the closed star of a vertex (the same
induced graph and the same coordinates on those five atoms) and still
carry a different cage label, because the cage predicates read a
larger neighbourhood of six-rings. Cage membership is not a function
of the four-neighbour star.

On the mixed TIP4P dump (`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj`, oxygen
type 2), `seams chill-plus` uses the cutoff list by default and
prints `interClathrate 9 water 241`. `--graph mutual` prints
`clathrate 1 interClathrate 7 water 242`. `seams cages` prints
`hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 250`. A three-eclipsed star is not
cage membership. The commands are in
[the mixed TIP4P tutorial](../user/tutorials/bulk-ice.md).

## Bond graph {#bond-graph}

`seams cages --graph` chooses the bond graph those rings are found on:

| value | graph |
| --- | --- |
| cutoff | pairs inside the distance cutoff |
| knn | mutual k-nearest (default k=4). mutual is the same graph |
| knn-union | union k-nearest, the completion graph of the seeded rule |
| seeded | mutual seeds and union completions (the CLI default) |

On the 4096-molecule cubic cell (`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj`,
type 1) each of the four graphs labels every molecule cubic. On the
mixed TIP4P dump each of the four graphs labels every oxygen water.
The split with CHILL+ on that dump is the star.

## Ring-adjacent completion {#ring-adjacent-completion}

`ring::seededCageAffiliation` takes `ringAdjacentCompletion` as its
fifth argument, default `false`. When the flag is `true`, the
accepted labels pass through `ring::ringAdjacentCompletion`: a
permissive six-ring with all but one vertex labeled fills that last
vertex, and the walk repeats to a fixed point. Hexagonal-cage flags
and double-diamond-cage flags run as two walks.

`seams cages --complete` sets the flag. The rule and its least fixed
point are on [Ring-adjacent completion](ring-completion.md).

# ClavisCage TRACE {#claviscage-trace}

ClavisCage 0.3.18 runs TRACE (Hsu and Lin, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025,
[10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459))
on the same hydrate cells as d-SEAMS 2.14.0. d-SEAMS counts closed cages
of census $5^{12}$, $5^{12}6^{2}$ and $5^{12}6^{4}$ on the oxygen
neighbour graph. TRACE counts cages on the hydrogen-bond graph. The two
constructions are [TRACE and signature cages](trace-assembly.md).
The commands are the how-to
[Cages and TRACE](../user/howto/cages-trace.md).

`analyze_waters` takes no thread count, so an eight-thread row times the
same serial TRACE call as the one-thread row. d-SEAMS uses the width the
row names. A row also names the version pair, the molecule count, the
repeat count `n` and the core count. The agreement text is the cage
census: cages found by both codes, cages found only by d-SEAMS, and
cages found only by TRACE.

## ClavisCage TRACE {#id1}

The tables compare d-SEAMS with the named analysis packages on the same inputs.

One row per cell. The agreement column is the cage census. The signature-by-signature rows are in the block below.

On the 46-molecule sI cell the census drops 7 cages that only d-SEAMS counts, and TRACE counts none that d-SEAMS does not.
512-0 has 18 of 30 bonds across the periodic cell; the six 51262 cages have 10 to 15. The 5^12 TRACE returns has none. The 2x2x2 tile matches, so d-SEAMS is right.
On 110160 molecules, one thread, d-SEAMS takes 955.8314 ms and TRACE takes 61962.4841 ms. At eight threads d-SEAMS takes 303.0753 ms and TRACE takes 61956.9697 ms. TRACE is serial: analyze_waters has no thread argument and Cargo.toml leaves rayon commented out.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/hop-ball.md -->

# Carried rings and the hop ball {#carried-rings-and-the-hop-ball}

`primitive::RingUpdater` returns the primitive rings of one neighbour
graph. The list equals `primitive::ringNetwork` on that frame, in the
same canonical order, so the two compare equal element by element.
The measured speedups are the how-to
[Linkcell neighbours and carried updates](../user/howto/linkcell-carried.md).
The primitive test is
[Primitive rings and the full graph](primitive-rings.md).

## What can change {#what-can-change}

Let $G$ and $G'$ be the neighbour graphs of two consecutive frames
with the same vertex count, and let $C$ be the vertices whose
adjacency row differs. Those vertices are the endpoints of every added
or removed edge. Write $D$ for the deepest ring the search keeps, and

$$
L = \lfloor D/2 \rfloor, \qquad
r = \max(0,\ \lfloor (L - 2)/2 \rfloor).
$$

A cycle of at most $D$ members is a primitive ring of one graph and
not of the other only if it contains a changed edge, or a changed edge
lies on a shortcut between two of its members. The shortcut is a path
of $l < d$ edges between two members that are $d$ apart around the
ring, with $d \le L$. One endpoint of that changed edge then lies
within $r$ edges of a ring member, measured along the shortcut.
Every ring that differs therefore meets $T$, the vertices within
distance $r$ of $C$ in the union of $G$ and $G'$.

For $D \le 7$, $r = 0$, so $T = C$. The update drops the stored
rings that meet $T$ and adds the rings of $G'$ that meet $T$. Each
new ring is enumerated once, from its lowest-indexed member in $T$.
When $T$ is every vertex, the search starts at every source.

The first frame, and any frame whose vertex count differs, searches
every source. A frame with no changed row returns the stored list.
For $D \ge 8$ a carried update keeps a ball of radius $L - 1$ at
each vertex and refreshes a ball when an edge within that radius of
the vertex changes. A full search at that depth fills every ball.
For $D \le 7$ the search does not keep those balls.

## When a frame walk carries {#when-a-frame-walk-carries}

A `seams` range keeps one updater when the frames arrive in order on
one worker, `--rebuild` is absent, and `SEAMS_CARRY` is left on. On a
LAMMPS dump the worker count is `--jobs 1`, and the dump is not split
across MPI ranks. On a `.xyz`, `.con`, `.pdb`, `.gro`, or `.dcd` path
the count may be any `--jobs`, because those suffixes are walked by
one worker. A single frame (`--last` omitted or equal to `--frame`),
`--rebuild`, `SEAMS_CARRY=0`, an MPI split of a LAMMPS dump, and a
LAMMPS dump read with `--jobs` above 1 call `ringNetwork` on every
frame. The rings match the carried walk. The flags are in the
[seams CLI](../reference/cli.md) reference.

## How the changed sources run {#how-the-changed-sources-run}

The search over $T$ uses `sourceTeam`. Inside an OpenMP region the
width is one. Outside it, the width stays one while the source count
is below 80 times the OpenMP width. Past that threshold the width is
the source count divided by 80, and at most the OpenMP width.
`teamFor` returns the OpenMP width for any count it is passed.

When `sourceTeam` is one, the new rings are copied and sorted on the
calling thread. When it is wider, the ring indices are sorted with a
stable parallel sort. Outside an OpenMP region the merge of the rings
that miss $T$ uses `teamFor`. Inside a region the merge stays on the
calling thread. Width one walks the stored list and inserts the new
rings in order. A wider width marks the rings that meet $T$ and
merges the rings that stay.

`seams_frame_chill_rings` can keep a cutoff neighbour list across
calls. A positive skin on the cutoff graph builds that list at cutoff
plus skin, and the next call reuses it while the box, cutoff, skin,
type, and graph are unchanged and every atom’s minimum-image
displacement is at most half the skin. The rings of that call are
`ringNetwork`. The ring carry is the updater above, on a sequential
`seams` frame walk.

The ring calls are on [C](../stable/c.md) and [C++](../stable/cpp.md).


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/interface-order.md -->

# Interface and confined ice {#interface-and-confined-ice}

Two published CHILL+ rules, on the same coordinates, with the
thresholds left alone.
The neighbour test and the $q_3$ shell are what move the labels.
The open edges do not, on these frames.
Prism blocks and sheet rings name confined ice that CHILL+, the
diamond test, adaptive common-neighbour analysis and a tetrahedron
template do not.
The rule itself is
[CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule](chill-plus-rules.md).
The counts below are `seams chill-plus` on the shipped frames.

Ideal ice Ih (`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, 128 molecules) is
hexagonal under both rules, with no disagreements.

## The two rules {#the-two-rules}

Nguyen and Molinero, J. Phys. Chem. B 119 (2015) 9369, equation 1
averages $q_3$ over the four nearest neighbours.
A staggered bond is `c(i,j) <= -0.8`.
An eclipsed bond is `-0.35 <= c(i,j) <= 0.25`.
Table 1 gives a crystal or clathrate label only when four neighbours
lie inside the cutoff.
Footnote a of that table keeps the interfacial neighbour test.
Two staggered bonds need a neighbour with more than two staggered
bonds.
Three staggered bonds and no eclipsed bond need a neighbour with
more than one staggered bond.

The OVITO 3.17.2 manual
([Chill+](https://docs.ovito.org/reference/pipelines/modifiers/chill_plus.md))
states the same cutoff and the same four-bond rows, and then differs
in three places.
A staggered bond is a correlation less than `-0.8`.
An eclipsed bond lies between `-0.35` and `0.25`.
Interfacial ice is “4 bonds of which 2 or 3 staggered”, with
hexagonal ice preferred when the fourth bond is eclipsed.
The neighbour test is not stated.

mdapy’s Chill+ kernel (cross-checked there against OVITO’s
`ChillPlusModifier`) is the same statement in code.
$q_3$ is summed over every neighbour inside the cutoff, not over the
four nearest.
The inequalities are strict.
A row is classified only when the coordination is 4.
Two staggered bonds, or three staggered and no eclipsed bond, are
interfacial, with no look at the neighbour.

`chill+` in the supplied examples is the 2015 rule.
`ovito-chill+` is the OVITO/mdapy rule.
Neither threshold is changed.
The comparison turns one lever at a time: the neighbour test, then
the $q_3$ shell, then the open edges.
An atom is counted under the lever that first produces the OVITO
label.
If more than one lever moves the label, the atom is mixed.

On both frames below, every atom that changes label has exactly four
neighbours inside 3.5 Å.
The shell condition in Table 1 is not the split.
Widening $q_3$ changes the label of a four-coordinated molecule when
one of its neighbours has a further neighbour inside the cutoff.
The open edges move no atom on either frame.
No correlation in these two frames sits on `-0.8`, `-0.35` or `0.25`.

## Nucleus {#nucleus}

Frame 1 of `input/traj/nucleation_f1.lammpstrj` (timestep 15677000,
4096 mW molecules).
The two rules disagree on 397 molecules.

| label | 2015 | OVITO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cubic | 47 | 48 |
| hexagonal | 62 | 54 |
| water | 3589 | 3360 |
| interfacial | 240 | 478 |
| clathrate | 20 | 21 |
| interfacial clathrate | 138 | 135 |

All 397 molecules are in the four-neighbour shell.
Of the molecules that do not change label, 1927 also have four
neighbours, 1428 have five, 289 have six and 38 have seven or more.
17 have three.
The extra neighbours sit on the agreeing population.
They change a neighbour’s $q_3$, and that is the shell lever.

Ring membership does not separate the 397.
395 of them lie on a primitive 6-ring, 381 on a 5-ring and 111 on a
4-ring, on the 3.5 Å graph.
The agreeing population is 3656, 3583 and 1957 on those same rings.
The primitive-ring search finds 40 prismatic faces.

The crystal radius, read outward from the shell of highest crystal
fraction to the 0.5 crossing, is 4.75 Å.
The 10-90 width of that crystal front is 7.69 Å.
The solid radius is 2.25 Å (2015) and 2.25 Å (OVITO).
The 10-90 width of the solid front, measured from the center of mass,
is 10.26 Å under the 2015 rule and 14.56 Å under OVITO.

The same frame has an instantaneous surface in the sense of Willard
and Chandler, J. Phys. Chem. B 114, 1954 (2010).
The coarse-graining Gaussian has their width, ξ = 2.40 Å.
Rays leave the center of mass of the 2015 crystal.
The surface on a ray is where the coarse density crosses the midpoint
of the core and the outer liquid.
288 of 288 rays cross.
The mean radius is 9.19 Å and the root-mean-square deviation of the
surface about that mean is 7.59 Å.
The 10-90 width of the coarse density, measured along the local
normal of that surface, is 1.34 Å.
On the same coordinate the 2015 solid fraction has a 10-90 width of
1.75 Å and the OVITO solid fraction has 1.79 Å.
The 10.26 Å and 14.56 Å widths are the center-of-mass profiles.
Adaptive common-neighbour analysis calls 4096 of 4096 molecules other.
The diamond test calls 13 cubic and 14 hexagonal.
A tetrahedron template with RMSD below 0.1, the OVITO polyhedral
template matching cutoff, passes 12 molecules, of which 1 is in
the disagreeing set.
Mean `q6` is 0.540 on the disagreeing set and 0.489 on the rest.
Bulk ice Ih in the test set has mean `q6` 0.626.

## Slab {#slab}

`input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj` is 864 mW molecules in a box of
22.99 × 21.61 × 52.51 Å.
The long axis is the surface normal.
The two rules disagree on 46 molecules.

| lever | molecules |
| --- | --- |
| neighbour test | 5 |
| q_3 shell | 41 |
| open edge | 0 |
| both levers | 0 |

| label | 2015 | OVITO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cubic | 1 | 1 |
| hexagonal | 352 | 346 |
| interfacial | 49 | 57 |
| clathrate | 3 | 3 |
| interfacial clathrate | 25 | 20 |
| water | 434 | 437 |

The net interfacial count rises by 8, from 5.67% to 6.60%.
Forty-six labels move, in both directions.
Hexagonal to interfacial is 10.
Interfacial to water is 5 and interfacial to hexagonal is 4.
Interfacial clathrate to water is 10.
The solid fraction is 0.465 and 0.468.
The crystal fraction is 0.409 and 0.402.

The 2015 solid slab is 24.82 Å thick, between Gibbs surfaces at
0.30 Å and 25.11 Å.
The 10-90 widths are 3.04 Å and 5.29 Å.
The OVITO solid slab is 22.98 Å thick, between 2.05 Å and 25.04 Å.
The widths are 1.10 Å and 5.29 Å.
One surface stays put.
The other moves by 1.76 Å, and that is the whole of the thickness
change.
The crystal slab, cubic plus hexagonal only, is 21.61 Å (2015) and
21.23 Å (OVITO).

The 46 molecules sit on average 5.33 Å from the nearest 2015 solid
surface.
The other 818 sit 6.67 Å away.
The shift is real and small.
Bins on the two surfaces hold part of the 46, and the rest are
scattered through the liquid, one or two molecules in a 1 Å bin.
All 46 have four neighbours inside 3.5 Å.
Forty-five lie on a 6-ring.
There is no prism and no bilayer.

Adaptive common-neighbour analysis calls every molecule other.
The diamond test calls 143 hexagonal and none cubic.
The tetrahedron template passes 346 molecules, 8 of them in the
disagreeing set.
Mean `q6` is 0.527 and 0.511.

## Confined ice {#confined-ice}

The frameworks are ideal oxygen sites at a nearest-neighbour
distance of 2.75 Å.
A nanotube is a stack of 8 rings in a box whose long axis is the
tube.
A sheet is a rectangular honeycomb, one layer or two.
The second layer is shifted by one bond in the plane, which is the
graphite AB stacking, and separated by 2.75 Å.
Half the bilayer molecules then have three neighbours and half have
four.
The library builds the oxygen sites. No trajectory is stored.
The `seams` command does not print the prism or sheet census.

| framework | N | 2015 | OVITO | rings | diamond | CNA | PTM | q6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| square tube | 32 | water 32 | water 32 | prism 32, 8 blocks | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.424 |
| pentagon tube | 40 | water 40 | water 40 | prism 40, 8 blocks | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.487 |
| hexagon tube | 48 | water 48 | interfacial 48 | prism 48, 8 blocks | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.509 |
| monolayer | 48 | water 48 | water 48 | polygon 48 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.741 |
| AB bilayer | 96 | cubic 48, water 48 | cubic 48, water 48 | bilayer 96 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.622 |

The hexagon tube is the neighbour test on its own.
Every molecule has four neighbours and an interfacial bond count.
Footnote a fails for all 48, so the 2015 rule leaves them as water.
OVITO labels all 48 interfacial.
The prism blocks are the same eight basal pairs either way.
Square and pentagon tubes are water under both rules.
Their bond angles are not the staggered ice pattern.
The prism blocks still name the tube.
The monolayer has three neighbours, so both CHILL+ rules say water
before any bond test.
Every molecule is on a planar 6-ring.
Its mean `q6` is 0.741, above the 0.626 of bulk ice Ih, so a `q6`
threshold taken from bulk ice does not reject the sheet.
The AB bilayer is split by coordination.
The four-coordinated sublattice is cubic under both CHILL+ rules.
The diamond test, adaptive common-neighbour analysis and the
tetrahedron template call none of the 96 a crystal.
The bilayer rings cover all 96, and there is no prism.

Adaptive common-neighbour analysis is the Stukowski test: 12
neighbours for FCC, HCP and icosahedral, 14 for BCC, with the
adaptive cutoff `(1+sqrt(2))/2` times the mean neighbour distance.
The diamond test is the second-shell common-neighbour test used for
cubic and hexagonal diamond.
The template is the four unit vectors of a tetrahedron, accepted
when the best rigid match has RMSD below 0.1.
`q6` is the Steinhardt invariant on the 3.5 Å shell, the quantity
`freud.order.Steinhardt(l=6)` returns for that neighbour list.

## Growth {#growth}

The campaign is `input/interface/campaign.py`.
It starts from `interface_f0.lammpstrj`, the mW Stillinger-Weber
potential, a 10 fs step, and NVT at the volume of that frame.
Four velocity seeds, numbered 1 to 4, run at 240, 250, 260 and 270 K.
The velocity seed is ten times the temperature plus the replica, so
the sixteen streams differ.
Frames are kept every 10 ps for 800 ps.
The slope on a seed is ordinary least squares of the solid thickness
while the 2015 solid fraction lies between 0.15 and 0.90 and both
thicknesses are still defined.
The mean of the four seeds is a percentile bootstrap, 10000 draws,
Hyndman-Fan type 7, generator seed 270.
The interval is the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles.
The difference is the 2015 rate minus the OVITO rate on the same
seed, resampled by the shared seed index.
It excludes zero when those two percentiles lie on the same side of
zero.

The thickness below is the ice slab on that fixed-volume cell.
It is the sum of the two fronts.
It is not a speed that can be set beside a direct-coexistence table.

| T (K) | 2015 slab (Å/ps) | OVITO slab (Å/ps) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 240 | 0.269 [0.224, 0.312] | 0.287 [0.237, 0.334] |
| 250 | 0.174 [0.148, 0.200] | 0.183 [0.151, 0.213] |
| 260 | 0.143 [0.128, 0.159] | 0.148 [0.132, 0.164] |
| 270 | 0.0292 [0.0137, 0.0569] | 0.0299 [0.0139, 0.0584] |

## Rule-sensitivity bound {#rule-sensitivity-bound}

The paired difference on that slab, 2015 minus OVITO, excludes zero
at 240, 250, 260 and 270 K.
Four further seeds at 272 K and at 273 K put the interval across zero.

| T (K) | difference (Å/ps) | excludes zero |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 240 | −0.0179 [−0.0217, −0.0140] | yes |
| 250 | −0.00854 [−0.0130, −0.00395] | yes |
| 260 | −0.00466 [−0.00733, −0.00245] | yes |
| 270 | −0.00067 [−0.00154, −0.00015] | yes |
| 272 | −0.00015 [−0.00058, 0.00032] | no |
| 273 | −0.00028 [−0.00054, 0.00001] | no |

272 K is the rule-sensitivity bound for this thickness.
Below it the two published CHILL+ rules are distinguishable as
growth rates.
At 272 K they are not.
The crystal thickness, cubic plus hexagonal and not the interfacial
label, already includes zero at 240, 260 and 270 K, so the bound is
carried by the interfacial label.
The 2015 thresholds are unchanged.

## Direct coexistence {#direct-coexistence}

`input/interface/npt_growth.py` builds the comparison cell.
The oxygen sites are the GenIce ice Ih cell.
Its basal normal is y, where the planes come in pairs 0.92 Å apart
separated by 2.76 Å.
Its secondary-prism normal is z, where the planes are 2.25 Å apart.
Each face is 8064 molecules, ice in the middle half and liquid in
the two caps, so the periodic cell has two interfaces.
The ensemble is anisotropic NpT at 1 bar (0.986923 atm in the real-unit
pressure of LAMMPS).
Four velocity seeds run at 240, 250, 260 and 270 K.
The speed of one front is L / (2 τ), the definition in equation 2 of
Espinosa, Navarro, Sanz, Valeriani and Vega, J. Chem. Phys. 145,
211922 (2016), page 211922-4.
L is the liquid length in the first production frame.
τ is the first frame whose solid fraction is at least 0.95.
The mean of the seeds that freeze is the same percentile bootstrap.

| face | T (K) | 2015 (Å/ns) | OVITO (Å/ns) | seeds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| secondary prism | 240 | 139.5 [133.0, 145.9] | 139.5 [133.0, 145.9] | 4 |
| secondary prism | 250 | 108.3 [100.0, 115.5] | 108.3 [100.0, 115.5] | 4 |
| secondary prism | 260 | 74.2 [72.6, 77.1] | 74.2 [72.6, 77.1] | 4 |
| secondary prism | 270 | 18.8 [15.5, 20.4] | 18.8 [15.5, 20.4] | 3 |
| basal | 240 | 62.5 [60.7, 64.0] | 62.9 [61.1, 64.4] | 4 |
| basal | 250 | 53.7 [45.2, 62.1] | 53.7 [45.2, 62.1] | 4 |
| basal | 260 | 37.7 [34.0, 40.6] | 37.8 [34.3, 40.6] | 4 |
| basal | 270 | not frozen in 2 ns | not frozen in 2 ns | 0 |

The paired difference includes zero on every row that freezes.
On this cell the front speed is not sensitive to the choice of rule.
The 272 K bound belongs to the fixed-volume thickness, not to this speed.

Table I on page 211922-4 lists the mW secondary-prism rate, and no
basal rate.
The printed values are 490 Å/ns at 240 K, 375 Å/ns at 250 K and
266 Å/ns at 260 K.
The table has no 270 K row.
Table II on the same page gives the mW melting point as 274.6 K.
The secondary-prism speeds here are 0.28 times those printed numbers.
Montero de Hijes, Romano, Gorfer and Dellago, J. Chem. Phys. 158,
204706 (2023), say in the caption of their Figure 4 that the mW
points taken from that table were divided by ten, because the authors
of the 2016 paper acknowledged a units erratum.
Dividing the printed table by ten gives 49, 37.5 and 26.6 Å/ns.
The speeds here are 2.8 times those corrected values.
The basal face is slower than the secondary prism at each temperature,
which is the direction Espinosa, Navarro, Sanz, Valeriani and Vega
report for TIP4P/ICE on the same page: the basal rate is within five
per cent of 0.6 times the secondary prism at 245, 255 and 260 K.
They do not print an mW basal number.

## Which definition meets Table I {#which-definition-meets-table-i}

The gap is not the 0.95 cutoff, the box length, the barostat period,
or the number of molecules.

Equation 2 is u = L / (2 τ), with L the liquid length and the 2
standing for two interfaces. On a linear freeze that is the same
number as the slope of the solid count,

u = (dN/dt) Lz / (2 N),

and the same number as half the slope of the solid thickness.
Lengths here are angstroms and times are picoseconds, so the speed
in Å/ns is 1000 times the speed in Å/ps. 490 Å/ns is 49 m/s.

`input/interface/espinosa_protocol.py` repeats the secondary prism
at the size on page 211922-2: 4000 molecules, ice in the middle
half, box 39.11 × 36.77 × 90.37 Å. The barostat is anisotropic
Nose-Hoover at 1 bar, with the 2 ps period stated for their
thermostat and barostat. LAMMPS has no velocity-rescaling fix of
the Gromacs kind; Nose-Hoover is the NpT fix. The mW parameters are
the Molinero and Moore set: ε = 6.189 kcal/mol, σ = 2.3925 Å,
a = 1.80, λ = 23.15, γ = 1.20, cos θ0 = −1/3. The temperature is
the Kelvin target of that fix. A 20 ps melt at 400 K with a 2 ps
period left the liquid on the crystal sites, mean move 0.3 Å, so
the liquid was melted for 100 ps at 500 K before the growth run.
Four seeds at 240 K and four at 260 K.

| definition | 240 K (Å/ns) | 260 K (Å/ns) | over printed | over printed/10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L/(2τ) at 0.95 | 151.6 [143.6, 160.8] | 82.8 [80.5, 85.6] | 0.31 | 3.1 |
| solid-count slope | 116.2 [112.3, 122.0] | 64.1 [61.0, 67.5] | 0.24 | 2.4 |
| thickness slope / 2 | 116.5 [109.9, 123.2] | 58.5 [53.2, 61.7] | 0.23 | 2.3 |
| Table I as printed | 490 | 266 | 1 | 10 |
| Table I divided by 10 | 49 | 26.6 | 0.1 | 1 |

The same three definitions on the earlier 8064-molecule runs, with
a 0.2 ps Nose-Hoover period, give a count slope of 115.3 at 240 K
and 57.1 at 260 K. Changing the molecule count and the barostat
period does not move the speed onto either published column.
Using the whole box instead of the liquid length, and dropping the
factor of two, gives about 600 Å/ns at 240 K and about 325 Å/ns at
260 K. That is the nearest misreading of equation 2, and it still
sits about 20% above the printed table.

The factor of ten in Montero de Hijes, Romano, Gorfer and Dellago,
Figure 4, is what they were told to apply to the 2016 points. It
does not turn Table I into this front displacement. The contour of
the solid fraction moves about 34 Å in 145 ps on the 4000-molecule
cell at 240 K, which is a one-front speed near 120 Å/ns whether or
not the count of solid molecules is used. That is the speed this
model produces with equation 2. It is 0.24 times the printed table
and 2.4 times the table divided by ten, at both 240 K and 260 K.

## Where the factor of four sits {#where-the-factor-of-four-sits}

The protocol keeps equation 2. A second campaign,
`input/interface/espinosa_faces.py`, repeats the 4000-molecule
secondary prism and adds the basal face, the primary prism, and one
secondary-prism seed at a 5 fs step. The melt, the 2 ps Nose-Hoover
periods, and the 10 fs step are the ones above. Production is 600 ps
at 240 K and 1000 ps at 260 K, with frames every 5 ps.

The one-front speed is the slope of the solid count,
u = (dN/dt) L / (2 N), on solid fraction 0.55 to 0.90.
On the secondary prism that slope is
116.9 \[107.9, 125.9\] Å/ns at 240 K and
64.1 \[62.0, 67.4\] Å/ns at 260 K.
Four times those intervals is \[432, 504\] and \[248, 270\].
Table I, 490 and 266, lies inside both.
The ratio of the slope to the printed table is 0.239 at 240 K and
0.241 at 260 K.
The ratio to the table divided by ten is 2.39 and 2.41.

| reading, secondary prism | 240 K (Å/ns) | 260 K (Å/ns) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L_liquid/(2τ) at 0.95 | 142.6 [133.5, 151.6] | 84.8 [77.9, 93.9] |
| L_liquid/(2τ) at 0.99 | 131.4 | 72.9 |
| L_liquid/(2τ) at 0.70 | 277.0 | 167.4 |
| solid-count slope | 116.9 [107.9, 125.9] | 64.1 [62.0, 67.4] |
| thickness slope / 2 | 117.7 [100.0, 147.4] | 56.1 [36.9, 71.0] |
| Lechner-Dellago q6bar slope | 118.3 [107.3, 129.4] | 64.8 [62.2, 67.4] |
| q6bar slope at 0.358 | 117.5 [108.1, 126.8] | 64.1 [61.9, 67.2] |
| potential-energy clock | 135.4 [127.3, 143.5] | 80.6 [74.5, 88.6] |
| L_box/(2τ) at 0.95 | 283.1 | 165.8 |
| L_box/τ at 0.95 | 566 [540, 593] | 332 [304, 368] |
| initial slab length / (2τ) | 140.5 | 81.0 |
| one interface’s travel, divided by 2 again | 71.3 | 42.4 |
| Table I | 490 | 266 |
| Table I / 4 | 122.5 | 66.5 |
| Table I / 10 | 49 | 26.6 |

L_liquid is the liquid length in the first production frame, about
half the long edge.
The 0.70 clock uses that whole liquid length for a shorter time, so
the speed rises to 277 Å/ns at 240 K and 167 Å/ns at 260 K, about
half the printed table.
The time at which the solid fraction first reaches 0.995 is noisier,
105.6 \[71.8, 128.0\] at 240 K and 58.8 \[44.5, 71.5\] at 260 K,
because the last percent flickers.
The potential energy falls by about 2100 kcal on the 4000-molecule
cell, about 1.05 kcal/mol for the 2000 molecules that freeze.
The energy clock uses that drop in place of an order parameter and
lands on the same side of both published columns.

Page 211922-3 identifies solid molecules with the Lechner-Dellago
q6 on a 3.5 Å shell. The threshold is the point where the fraction
of bulk ice labeled liquid equals the fraction of bulk liquid
labeled ice, about half a percent.
On these trajectories that cut is 0.38 to 0.40.
The slope of that count is the CHILL+ count slope.
The constant 0.358 quoted for the earlier seeding work gives the
same slope.
The local, unaveraged q6 at 0.5 is lower, 76.5 Å/ns at 240 K and
43.6 Å/ns at 260 K on the secondary prism, and it is still a quarter
of the printed table or less.
The 2015 CHILL+ thresholds are unchanged.

The primary prism, two seeds, has a count slope of
101.3 \[87.5, 115.0\] at 240 K and 51.3 \[49.4, 53.2\] at 260 K.
The basal face has 61.1 \[60.0, 62.3\] and 36.4 \[34.1, 38.8\].
Basal over secondary prism is 0.52 at 240 K and 0.57 at 260 K.
Page 211922-4 says the basal rate of TIP4P/ICE is within five
percent of 0.6 times the secondary prism, and that the two prismatic
planes are similar.
The mW cell here has that same ordering.
A wrong face does not supply the missing factor of four.

One secondary-prism seed at 240 K with a 5 fs step, frames still
5 ps apart, has a count slope of 96.0 Å/ns and an equation-2 speed
of 132.6 Å/ns.
The four 10 fs seeds at that temperature span 106 to 127 Å/ns on
the count slope and 131 to 154 Å/ns on equation 2.
The shorter step does not move the speed by a factor of four.

116.9 Å/ns is 11.7 m/s and 1169 cm/s.
Dividing by σ = 2.3925 Å gives 48.9 σ/ns at 240 K and 26.8 σ/ns at
260 K, which is the table divided by ten (49 and 26.6).
The long edge of the cell is 90.37 Å.
Page 211922-2 describes that cell as about 9 nm, so the length used
here is already in angstroms.
Table II fits ln(u/(Å/ns)) for mW with C1 = 4.1711, C2 = 0.096266 K^−1
and C3 = −0.001148 K^−2.
At 240 K, ΔT = 34.6 K, the fit returns 458 Å/ns, next to the printed

The fit is the printed column, in the unit the table names.

Shi, Fulford, Salvalaglio and Molteni, J. Chem. Phys. 162, 054714
(2025), Figure 3, plots mW growth on the primary prism and the basal
face.
The markers, read from the figure coordinates, are
98.3 Å/ns at 240 K and 62.1 Å/ns at 260 K on the primary prism,
with the error bars running 85.2 to 111.4 and 51.6 to 72.7.
The basal markers are 88.1 and 39.5.
The primary-prism equation-2 speeds here are 115.2 at 240 K and
63.2 at 260 K, and the energy clocks are 108.7 and 62.1.
The basal equation-2 speeds are 84.0 and 44.1.
Those sit with Figure 3.
Rozmanov and Kusalik, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 13, 15501 (2011),
report basal speeds of 0.7, 0.9 and 1.1 Å/ns at 10 K of supercooling
for their large, medium and small cells, as quoted by Shi et al.
Table I for TIP4P/ICE at 260 K is 0.933 Å/ns, on that atomistic scale.
Moore and Molinero’s minimum crystallization time is about ten
nanoseconds, as cited on page 211922-7.
Avrami time scales as u to the power −3/4, so a factor of four in u
moves that time by 4^0.75 = 2.8, inside the order of magnitude the
2016 paper claims for the comparison.
The ten-nanosecond minimum does not separate Table I from a quarter
of Table I.

The steady one-front speed, times four, is the printed mW column.
That factor is what you get by taking L as the whole box and dropping
the two in equation 2, since the liquid is half the box:
L_box / τ = 4 L_liquid / (2 τ).
On the 0.95 clock this reading is 566 and 332 Å/ns, above the table.
On the count slope it is 468 and 256 Å/ns, and the printed 490 and
266 fall inside the seed intervals.
The private correction of ten, applied to a column that already
carries this factor of four, leaves a residual 10/4 = 2.5, which is
the stable 2.4 measured here.
Equation 2 is the speed the trajectories produce, and it is the
speed in Figure 3 of Shi et al.

## Growth-speed curve {#growth-speed-curve}

The curve uses the same 4000-molecule deck as
`input/interface/espinosa_faces.py`.
The melt, the 2 ps Nose-Hoover periods and the 10 fs step are
unchanged.
240 K keeps the 600 ps production of that file and 260 K keeps the
1000 ps production.
220 K and 230 K run for 800 ps, 250 K for 1200 ps and 265 K for
2000 ps, so the basal face still crosses the fitting window.
Basal, primary prism and secondary prism, four velocity seeds each,
six temperatures, seventy-two trajectories.
Every seed reached a solid fraction of at least 0.90.

The speed is the count slope already used for the factor of four,

u = (dN/dt) Lz / (2 N),

on the 2015 CHILL+ solid fraction between 0.55 and 0.90.
The thresholds are not changed.
The same window is scored with Lechner-Dellago q6bar on the 3.5 Å
shell, once at the mislabel cut and once at the constant 0.358.
Neither cut is fitted to these rates.
The mean of the four seeds is a percentile bootstrap, 10000 draws,
Hyndman-Fan type 7, generator seed 270.
The interval is the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles.
Speeds are angstroms per nanosecond.
