```python
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> atoms = frame.to_ase()
>>> len(atoms)
128
```

## to_solvis {#to-solvis}

`to_solvis` needs solvis-tools. It returns `solvis.system.System`.

```python
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> type(frame.to_solvis()).__name__
'System'
```

## `dseams.Frame` {#dseams-frame}

`import dseams` is the array module in the same pydseamslib wheel.
This repository does not build it. `dseams.Frame` stores a coordinate
array and calls `include/seams.h`. `dseams.from_ase` returns positions
and a LAMMPS cell, which `set_frame` accepts. `q4q6` returns the local
`q4` and `q6` arrays. `chill_plus()` returns labels and nine counts;
index 1 is hexagonal. `neighbours` returns a CSR, and the last offset
is the pair count. On this ice Ih cell that is 128 waters, 512
neighbour entries, 256 six-rings, mean q6 0.625855, and 128 hexagonal
labels.

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import dseams
>>> def ice():
...     xyz, edges, reading = [], [], False
...     handle = open("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj")
...     try:
...         while True:
...             line = handle.readline()
...             if line == "":
...                 break
...             if line.startswith("ITEM: BOX BOUNDS"):
...                 edges = []
...                 for _ in range(3):
...                     lo, hi = handle.readline().split()[:2]
...                     edges.append(float(hi) - float(lo))
...             elif line.startswith("ITEM: ATOMS"):
...                 reading = True
...             elif reading:
...                 parts = line.split()
...                 if len(parts) < 5:
...                     break
...                 xyz.append([float(v) for v in parts[2:5]])
...     finally:
...         handle.close()
...     return xyz, edges
>>> xyz, edges = ice()
>>> frame = dseams.Frame()
>>> frame.set_frame(np.asarray(xyz), np.asarray(edges))
>>> frame.count()
128
>>> offsets, cols = frame.neighbours(3.5)
>>> int(offsets[-1])
512
>>> sizes, sym, hist, frac = frame.rings(3.5, 6)
>>> int(hist[6])
256
>>> q4, q6 = frame.q4q6(3.5)
>>> round(float(q6.mean()), 6)
0.625855
>>> labels, counts = frame.chill_plus()
>>> int(counts[1])
128
>>> from ase import Atoms
>>> atoms = Atoms(symbols=["O"] * len(xyz), positions=xyz, cell=edges, pbc=True)
>>> pos, box = dseams.from_ase(atoms)
>>> pos.shape
(128, 3)
>>> frame.set_frame(pos, box)
>>> int(frame.chill_plus()[1][1])
128
```


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/reference/cli.md -->

# seams CLI {#seams-cli}

The engine command is `seams`. The parser is Argum. Help, errors,
ice-type counts, and `--features` are colorized through Argum’s
`environmentColorStatus`. `NO_COLOR` turns the colors off.

```text
seams --help
seams --version
seams --features
seams read FILE
seams chill FILE
seams chill-plus FILE
seams cages FILE
seams rdf FILE
seams cn FILE
seams hbonds FILE
seams pairs FILE
seams density-z FILE
seams domains FILE
```

The same commands on the bundled multi-type frame. `pairs` and `domains`
need `--site`, so the runnable lines include it:

```bash
seams read input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams chill input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams hbonds input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams pairs input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams density-z input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams domains input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion,3=tail' --subset polar
```

A positional `command` and a positional `file` are required. Missing
either, an unknown command, or a parse error exits 2.

Every command accepts `--format text|json`. Text is the human-readable
format documented below. JSON writes one object per line, one object
per output frame, with the fields `schema` (`dseams.cli/v1`), `command`,
`frame`, `status`, and `text`. The `text` field is the command’s text
output, with JSON escapes for characters that need them.
`--strict-input` returns 2 when a requested
frame has no atoms; without it, empty input retains the legacy text output.
An MPI build appends a sentence to the `--last` help: under `mpiexec` the
ranks share a dump’s frames, each with `--jobs` workers, and `SEAMS_MPI=0`
keeps MPI off.

## Commands {#commands}

The `command` positional help string is `read | chill | chill-plus | ovito-chill+ | cages | symmetry | rings | prisms | cluster | fingerprint | ions | f4 | steinhardt | rdf | cn | hbonds | pairs | density-z | domains`. `chill_plus` is an accepted alias of
`chill-plus`, and `ovito_chill_plus` is an accepted alias of
`ovito-chill+` (neither alias is listed in that help string).

| command | action | stdout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read | print the loaded cloud | nop N frame F box Lx Ly Lz and, when box.size() >= 6, xy xz yz |
| chill | CHILL labels | nop N then name count for each ice type present |
| chill-plus | published CHILL+ (shell of 4, four-nearest q3, neighbour test) | same as chill. --rule selects the rule. --layers adds phi-c P stack S. --tum-layers adds tum-phi-c P tum-stack S |
| ovito-chill+ | OVITO 3.17.2 CHILL+ (shell of 4, full-shell q3, no neighbour test) | same as chill-plus |
| symmetry | space group, one shell overlay, and the ice-label tally | symmetry backend NAME, then space-group NUMBER SYMBOL, space-group off, or space-group none. A matching whole cell adds the overlay and point-group SYMBOL N. One shell overlay, then shells LABEL N ... unmatched U. IRA, SOFI, and spglib run only when that build linked them. No atoms or no box prints symmetry needs a frame and a box and exits 2 |
| rings | primitive rings on the cutoff list. --max-ring N is the largest size (default 6). A value below 3 is read as 6 | nop N rings R then one SIZE COUNT line for each size that occurs |
| prisms | perfect and imperfect prisms of size 3 to 6 on the mutual four-nearest graph | nop N, then size S perfect P imperfect I for each size, then perfect P imperfect I |
| cluster | largest connected component of the loaded atoms | nop N largest L subset S percolation P |
| cages | ice score on six-membered rings. The four counts are disjoint and sum to the water atoms: hexagonal only, cubic only, both, water | nop N graph KIND hexagonal IH cubic IC both B water W |
| cages --signature SPEC | closed polyhedra whose ring-size census matches SPEC; each vertex lies on at least three faces that close around it, V - E + F = 2, and rings that wind the periodic cell are left out | one line per signature, nop N graph KIND signature S cages C atoms A. --incomplete adds incomplete K. --guest-types adds guests G occupied O multiple M free F, inside 1 with --inside, and occ K:N when the histogram is not empty. --shape adds shape N:GROUP |
| fingerprint | topology keys of the bonded graph | nop N graph KIND hops H method M key K classes C rings 3:a 4:b ... top key=count ... |
| fingerprint --by-atom | the summary, then one row per atom | atom I species S coord C homopolar H rings SIZE:COUNT ... |
| fingerprint --emit-library LABEL | the frame’s distinct keys as library lines | # method M hops H colors C then key LABEL rows |
| fingerprint --library FILE[,FILE...] | atoms named by key libraries | nop N graph KIND hops H method M matched X label=count ... unmatched=U and, with several libraries, depth H1=n1 H2=n2 |
| ions | ions classed by their first water shell against the seeded cages. An empty cloud prints nop 0 | nop N ice A ions I in-ice X front Y liquid Z shell S shell-ice F clusters C ions-in-ice J capped K broken B |
| f4 | Rodger F4 on H-O…O-H pairs | nop N f4 MEAN n M |
| steinhardt | cutoff-shell Steinhardt parameters for the degrees named by --l (default 4,6) and their Lechner-Dellago averages. Degrees 4 and 6 use the solid-harmonic kernel. --l 3,4,6,12 is the former four-degree line | nop N then qL A qLbar B for each requested degree, in the order given |
| rdf | partial site-site g_{IJ}(r) | # r g count then # types I J rmax R bins N volume V then one r g count row per bin |
| cn | site-site coordination number | # site-site then # types I J cutoff R cn X nI N nJ M volume V |
| cn --ions --site | cage degree on ionCloud | cage ionCloud types 1 2 cutoff R degree D nCation N nAnion M |
| hbonds | geometric hydrogen-bond count | nop N hbonds E |
| pairs --site | mutual-nearest contact pairs | contact-pair count N nCation C nAnion A |
| density-z | type-resolved \rho along one axis | # z rho then one z rho row per bin |
| domains --site | polar/apolar Stoddard component. --subset defaults to polar; tail is apolar | subset polar n N largest L P P_inf |

`chill` / `chill-plus` default to `--graph cutoff`: `nneigh::neighListO`,
every pair closer than `--cutoff`. `--graph mutual` (alias `knn`) calls
`nneigh::kNearestNeighbourList` with `k = 4`, mutual; there `--cutoff`
is only the cell-size hint (`cutoff + 1.5`). Other graphs exit 2.
Published cutoff `chill-plus` classifies in `chill::chillPlusPublishedCutoff`
(one cutoff CSR and the fused $q_3$). Every other published call goes
through `chill::applyChillPlus`, which builds that same CSR from the
neighbour rows and calls `chill::chillPlusFromCsr`. `ovito-chill+` stays
on `chill::getCorrelPlus` / `chill::getIceTypePlusNoPrint` with open
edges. `chill` calls `chill::getCorrel` / `chill::getIceTypeNoPrint`.
`--water-types T,U` is the neighbour mask (OW only); `--type` is the
load filter and is not that mask. Ice names are the
`molSys::atom_state_type` enumerators: `cubic`, `hexagonal`,
`water`, `interfacial`, `clathrate`, `interClathrate`, `reCubic`,
`reHex`, `unclassified`.

`cages` reports cage membership, not CHILL labels. Hexagonal is
HC only (Ih), cubic is DDC only (Ic), both is an atom on both,
and water is neither. The bond graph is `--graph`.

`rdf` and `cn` call `rdf::partialRdf` on LAMMPS type IDs from
`--pair-types I,J` (default `I = J = --type`). `--cutoff` is rmax. `--bins`
is optional. The volume is `nneigh::dumpVolume` (det of dump `H`).
`cn` integrates the site-site RDF to that cutoff
(`rdf::coordinationNumber`). Help text and the `cn` header say
`site-site`. `cn --ions --site` is the cage degree, documented in the
next paragraph.

`cn --ions --site SPEC` builds `site::ionCloud` and prints the mean
unlike degree of type-1 (cation) vertices from
`nneigh::neighList(cutoff, ions, 1, 2)`. The line contains `cage`.
`pairs --site SPEC` prints the size of
`nneigh::mutualNearestUnlike(ions, 1, 2)`. That line contains
`contact-pair`, not ionicity. Both need `--site`.

`density-z` calls `site::densityZ`. `--type 0` (default) keeps
every atom; `--type I` keeps that LAMMPS type. `--axis` is `x`,
`y`, or `z` (default `z`). `--bins` defaults to the bound span
over $0.1$. Each slab volume is $A_\perp \times dz$, with
$A_\perp$ from dump H (recovered `lx, ly, lz`, not bound
spans). This is not an ice score.

`chill`, `chill-plus`, and `cages` call `site::iceScoreAllowed`.
When `--family` is not `waterIce` they print `site::refuseIceScore`
(the message names the family) and exit 2. They do not fall through
to `atom_state_type::water`. Unflagged `seams chill` stays
`waterIce`. If `--family` is absent and the frame has more than two
LAMMPS types, one stderr line names `--family` and the command
still exits 0.

An empty cloud (`nop 0`) still prints. `chill` / `chill-plus` print
`nop 0`. `cages` prints `nop 0 graph KIND hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 0`. A signature on an empty cloud prints
`nop 0 graph KIND signature S cages 0 atoms 0` for each signature.
`rdf` / `cn` still emit their headers. `hbonds` prints
`nop 0 hbonds 0`. `f4` prints `nop 0 f4 nan`. `density-z` prints
`# z rho` and zero-density bins. `ions` prints `nop 0`.

`hbonds` loads the heavy-atom cloud with `--type` and the hydrogen
cloud with `--htype`, then builds a cutoff neighbour list. Without
`--donors` it uses the water two-hydrogen-per-molecule set
(`hAtomMolList`). `--donors` passes every hydrogen index to
`populateHbondsFromDonors`. `--hdist` and `--hangle` are the acceptor-H
distance and the acceptor-centered O-O-H angle cutoffs (angle
between OO and OH). The defaults are 2.42 Å and 30 degrees, the
water values in `bond::populateHbonds`. They are not an
ionic-liquid criterion.

## Options {#options}

Names and help text are the Argum `Option` / `Positional`
definitions in `src/seams_cli.cpp`. Defaults are the C++
initializers (Argum does not write defaults into the help).

| flag | default | Argum help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -h, --help |  | show this help message and exit |
| -v, --version |  | Print version information |
| --features |  | Print compile-time backends |
| -f, --frame N | 1 | First frame (1-based) |
| --last N | omitted (0) | Last frame (inclusive). Omit for a single --frame |
| -j, --jobs N | 1 | Parallel frame workers (OpenMP). 1 is serial |
| --rebuild | off | Recompute rings and cages on every frame. A one-worker frame range otherwise updates them from the previous frame; the output is the same |
| --format KIND | text | Output format: text (default) or json |
| --strict-input | off | Fail when a requested frame produces no atoms |
| -t, --type I | 0 | Atom type (0 guesses oxygen then type 1; density-z: 0 is every atom) |
| --water-types T,U | unset | Neighbour graph on these LAMMPS types only (OW). Substrate and ions never enter the 4-NN list. A type that is not in the frame is an error |
| --mol SPEC | unset | Water oxygens by molecule: water, or ids such as 1,5-12. Neighbours, CHILL, CHILL+, rings and cages then ignore ions. A missing id is an error |
| --rule NAME | published chill+ | chill-plus rule: chill+ (published default) or ovito-chill+. A path to a readable file is scanned for a rule or chill-plus key. Comments are skipped. The file is not executed as Lua or YAML. CHILL_PLUS_RULE fills an unset flag |
| --layers | off | chill-plus: literature I_sd reference from CHILL+ molecule bins (Phi_c and H/C string) |
| --tum-layers | off | chill-plus: TUM stacking from HC-basal and DDC-equatorial rings, not CHILL+ molecules |
| --shape | off | cages --signature: point group of each found cage, from those vertices only |
| --inside | off | cages --guest-types: assign by ray-parity inside the fan-triangulated faces, not nearest centroid |
| --per-atom FILE |  | chill\vert{}chill-plus\vert{}cages\vert{}fingerprint\vert{}ions: append a LAMMPS dump frame with one extra per-atom column (label, cage, class or state) for OVITO or VMD |
| --subset KIND | polar | domains subset: polar \vert{} apolar. tail is accepted as apolar |
| --by-atom | off | fingerprint: one row per atom with coordination, same-species bonds, and primitive rings through that atom |
| --max-ring N | 6 | Largest primitive ring kept by rings (default 6) |
| --pair-types I,J | I = J = --type | Pair types for site-site rdf/cn (default I=J=--type) |
| --types I,J |  | Deprecated exact alias of --pair-types. The handler prints --types is deprecated; use --pair-types on stderr |
| --family NAME | waterIce | Material family (default waterIce): waterIce, ionicLiquid, moltenSalt, des, electrolyte, confinedIL, confinedWater, networkFormer |
| --site SPEC |  | Type-to-kind map for ionCloud (1=cationHead,2=anion) |
| --ions |  | cn on ionCloud cage degree (needs --site) |
| -c, --cutoff ANGSTROM | 3.5 | Neighbour cutoff (rdf/cn rmax; hbonds heavy-atom nList) |
| --l LIST | 4,6 | Steinhardt degrees, comma-separated. Default 4,6, the solid-harmonic pair. 3, 8 and 12 are computed only when named |
| --cage-edge SPEC | 2.65,3.15 | cages --signature: keep a face only when every edge lies in LO,HI (coordinate units of the file; default 2.65,3.15). none uses the face census alone (SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE) |
| --bins N | rmax / 0.1 or box[axis] / 0.1 | Histogram bins (rdf: rmax/0.1; density-z: L/0.1) |
| --axis XYZ | z | Histogram axis for density-z (x\vert{}y\vert{}z, default z). 0, 1, and 2 are accepted |
| -k N | 4 | k for knn / seeded cages |
| --graph KIND | seeded | Bond graph. cages: cutoff \vert{} knn \vert{} knn-union \vert{} seeded. chill and chill-plus: cutoff \vert{} mutual. Help then appends the stored name, seeded unless the runtime table changed it |
| --complete | off | Seeded cages: fill the last vertex of six-rings whose other vertices carry a label (ring completion) |
| --signature SPEC |  | cages: ring-size census (4:6,6:8) or a named table entry (sodalite\vert{}alpha\vert{}512\vert{}51262\vert{}51264\vert{}51268\vert{}sh\vert{}hc\vert{}ddc); join several with + for one line each. Joined signatures share one ring network and one cage search |
| --incomplete | off | cages --signature: also report cups and incomplete cages on the ring graph |
| --guest-types T,U |  | cages --signature: LAMMPS types of guests (methane, THF, ions) placed in the found cages by their periodic centroids |
| --guest-radius R | 4.0 | cages --signature: a guest belongs to the nearest cage center within R (default 4.0) |
| --hops N | 2 | fingerprint: bonds from the center in each local key (default 2) |
| --color-types | off | fingerprint: color vertices by LAMMPS type, so species never match across types. --colour-types is the same option and is left out of help |
| --library FILE |  | fingerprint: key library (from --emit-library) to name atoms by; several, comma separated, at different hop counts name each atom by the deepest that knows it |
| --emit-library LABEL |  | fingerprint: print the frame's distinct keys as library lines under LABEL instead of the summary |
| --ion-types I,J |  | ions: LAMMPS types read against the cage assignment |
| --ion-cutoff ANGSTROM | --cutoff | ions: first water shell radius (default --cutoff) |
| --htype I | 1 | Hydrogen atom type for hbonds and f4 |
| --hdist ANGSTROM | 2.42 | Acceptor-H distance cutoff for hbonds |
| --hangle DEG | 30 | O-O-H angle cutoff for hbonds (acceptor-centered) |
| --donors | off | Use every hydrogen as a donor candidate |
| --config FILE | SEAMS_CONFIG or ./seams.env | Dotenv of SEAMS_* / LINKCELL_* knobs. Env wins over the file |
| --print-config |  | Print the resolved runtime knobs and exit |
| --tpp N | 0 (occupancy picker) | Threads per particle for the device k-NN (LINKCELL_TPP) |
| --block N | 0 | CUDA block size (LINKCELL_BLOCK / SEAMS_BLOCK) |
| --resident FRAC | 0.80 | Fraction of free device memory for a resident batch (SEAMS_RESIDENT) |
| --cell ANGSTROM | 3 | Link-cell hint so NPT frames share a grid (SEAMS_CELL) |

`--help`, `--version`, `--features`, and `--print-config` print and
exit 0 before any file is opened.

`--tpp`, `--block`, `--resident`, and `--cell` apply to the device
TUM ice score (`seams cages`) only. CHILL and $q_{lm}$ stay on
the host.

`--cutoff` is in Angstrom. `-k` also applies to `knn-union` (the
same `k` feeds `nneigh::kNearestNeighbourList`). `--graph` is used
by `cages` and `fingerprint`; a fingerprint wants one graph, so
`seeded` (two graphs) falls back to `cutoff` there. `--complete` is used by `cages` and `ions`: it
passes `true` as the fifth argument of `seededCageAffiliation`.

## `--type` {#type}

| value | single frame (load) | --last range (forEachLammpsFrame) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | LAMMPS: type 2, then type 1 if that cloud is empty. chemfiles: keep every atom. XYZ: every atom is type 1 | LAMMPS: every atom (sinp::readLammpsTrj). Classification uses cloud.pts[0].type |
| I > 0 | LAMMPS readLammpsTrjO / chemfiles filter I | LAMMPS readLammpsTrjO with that type. The CLI does not pass a coordinate slice. |

XYZ always stores type 1. Classification still uses `--type` after
the read (type 0 then becomes 1).

A mixed-type dump that is not the water guess needs `--type I`.
`density-z` treats `0` as every atom, not the oxygen guess.
See [Ionic-liquid dumps](../user/howto/ionic-liquid.md).

## `--water-types` {#water-types}

`--type` is a load filter (one LAMMPS type, or the oxygen guess).
It is not the neighbour mask. `--water-types T,U` loads the mixed
dump (`loadType = -1`) and builds `nneigh::kNearestNeighbourList`
/ `kNearestNeighbourPair` on that type set. Ag, I, protein and
ions stay in the cloud for guests and `ions`, but they never
enter the four neighbours of OW. `chill`, `chill-plus`, `cages`
and `ions` honour the flag. Ice and cage counts are the water
types only.

```bash
seams chill-plus FILE --water-types 1
seams cages FILE --graph seeded --water-types 1
seams ions FILE --ion-types 3,4 --water-types 1
```

The same flags on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --water-types 1
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph seeded --water-types 1
seams ions input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --ion-types 3,4 --water-types 1
```

## `--pair-types` {#pair-types}

Used by `rdf` and `cn`. The Argum form is `I,J` (one comma). A bad
string exits 2 (`bad --pair-types (want I,J)`). Omit the flag to set both
sides to `--type`. These are LAMMPS type IDs on the original cloud
(site-site). `cn --ions` is a different path (ionCloud cage degree).

`--types` is a deprecated exact alias of `--pair-types`. It accepts
the same `I,J` text and prints one warning on stderr. `--type` and
`--types` both bind, because an exact name is taken before a longer
name that starts with the same characters. `--ty` matches both and
is ambiguous.

| --pair-types | single-frame load | --last range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omitted | same as --type (one species) | same as --type |
| I,I (like) | keep type I | keep type I |
| I,J with I != J | every atom (readLammpsTrj / chemfiles unfiltered) | every atom (typeFilter 0) |

`cmdRdf` / `cmdCn` then call `rdf::partialRdf` on those two integers.
`typeOf` still resolves a zero to the first atom (or 1).

## `seams read` and the box {#seams-read-and-the-box}

`seams read` prints `gen::formatDumpBox`: the three bound spans,
then `xy xz yz` when `box.size() >= 6`. There is no separate tilt
flag. `seams rdf` uses the same dump H (`gen::periodicDist` and
`nneigh::dumpVolume`). `seams density-z` uses recovered `lx, ly, lz` for $A_\perp$, not bound spans. The in-plane sampler remains
`rdf2::sampleRDF_AA`; see
[Sheared cells](../user/howto/sheared-cells.md).

## `--graph` {#graph}

`chill` and `chill-plus` take `cutoff` or `mutual`.
The default is `cutoff`: every pair closer than `--cutoff`.
The stored configuration name of that default is `seeded`, and those two commands map `seeded` onto the cutoff list.
`--graph mutual` keeps the mutual four nearest neighbours, with candidates inside `--cutoff + 1.5`.

`cages` does not make that mapping.

| value | graph |
| --- | --- |
| seeded | mutual k-nearest seeds, union completions (ring::seededCageAffiliation; --complete sets the fifth argument) |
| cutoff | pairs inside --cutoff (nneigh::neighListO) |
| knn | mutual k-nearest (nneigh::BondGraph::KnnMutual) |
| knn-union | union k-nearest (nneigh::BondGraph::KnnUnion) |

`nneigh::bondGraphFromName` also accepts `knn-mutual` and `mutual`
as `knn`, and `union` as `knn-union`. `seeded` is handled in the CLI
and is not a `BondGraph` enumerator. Any other name throws
`std::invalid_argument` (`unknown bond graph 'NAME' (use cutoff, knn, knn-union)`) and `cages` exits 2.

Candidate cutoff for the knn graphs is `--cutoff + 1.5`.

## `--cage-edge` {#cage-edge}

Used by `cages --signature`.
Each face is kept when every minimum-image edge lies in the window.
The default is `2.65,3.15`.
`none` (also `off` or `false`) leaves that test out, and the cage bound is the face census alone, which is the search from before the window existed.
`hc` and `ddc` keep their geometric finders. The window applies to the ring-census search.

The numbers are in the coordinate units of the file.
The LAMMPS dumps in this tree are angstroms, and the default covers the oxygen-oxygen contacts of the reference cells (about 2.74 to 2.81).
Set the window to the heavy-atom contact range of the model.
Widen it for a compressed cell or a guest that stretches a cage.
A file in nanometers uses `0.265,0.315`, or `none` when the contact range is unknown.
Use a comma, a colon, or a slash. `2.65-3.15` is rejected.

```bash
seams cages FILE --graph cutoff --signature 512
seams cages FILE --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge none
seams cages FILE --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge 2.4,3.4
```

The same flags on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff --signature 512
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge none
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge 2.4,3.4
```

The same string is `SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE`.
`dseams.userframe.Frame.cages_by_signature("512", edge="none")` passes it through.
`pydseams.Frame.cages_by_signature` does not take `edge`.
Lua `dseams.cages_by_signature` calls `findBySignature` and does not read a window.
The C entry is `seams_frame_signature_edge`; a null edge string is the default window.

## Runtime knobs {#runtime-knobs}

Defaults live in the binary. An optional dotenv (`SEAMS_CONFIG` or
`./seams.env`) fills unset keys. The process environment wins the
file; CLI flags win the environment. `seams --print-config` dumps
the table.

| variable | default |
| --- | --- |
| SEAMS_FRAME / SEAMS_LAST | 1 / 0 |
| SEAMS_JOBS | 1 |
| SEAMS_CARRY | 1 (0 is --rebuild) |
| SEAMS_TYPE | 0 |
| SEAMS_CUTOFF | 3.5 |
| SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE | 2.65,3.15 (none turns the window off) |
| SEAMS_K | 4 |
| SEAMS_GRAPH | seeded |
| SEAMS_FAMILY | waterIce |
| SEAMS_RESIDENT | 0.80 |
| SEAMS_CELL | 3.0 |
| SEAMS_TPP / LINKCELL_TPP | occupancy picker (0) |
| SEAMS_BLOCK / LINKCELL_BLOCK | occupancy picker (0) |
| SEAMS_OFFLOAD | false (Steinhardt Ylm and TUM cages; 0 forces host) |
| YODA_FENNEL_PATH / YODA_LUA_PATH | empty |

Analysis choice (which command) is not this table.

## File suffix {#file-suffix}

`seams` picks a reader from the path suffix
(`path.find_last_of('.')`):

| suffix | reader | included when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| xyz | sinp::readXYZ | always |
| con | sinp::readCon | SEAMS_HAS_READCON. Otherwise the command fails: readcon-core is not in this build |
| pdb, gro, dcd | sinp::readChemfiles | SEAMS_HAS_CHEMFILES. Otherwise the command fails: chemfiles is not in this build |
| anything else | LAMMPS dump (readLammpsTrjO / readLammpsTrj) | always |

A missing reader does not parse those suffixes as LAMMPS dumps.
`seams --features` reports chemfiles, readcon-core, and readcon-db.

## Frame ranges {#frame-ranges}

Omit `--last`, or set it equal to `--frame`, for one frame. That
path calls `load` and works for every linked suffix.

A range (`--last` > `--frame`) dispatches by suffix. LAMMPS dumps use
`sinp::forEachLammpsFrame`, with one handle per OpenMP worker and
deterministic output order. XYZ is a single-frame input and emits frame 1
at most. Chemfiles and readcon inputs are read serially until the requested
range or the first missing frame. `--jobs 1` is serial; non-LAMMPS readers
do not use OpenMP workers.

A serial range carries rings and cage affiliation from one frame to the
next: `primitive::RingUpdater` and `ring::AffiliationUpdater` recompute only
the atoms whose bounded ball changed. LAMMPS ranges with `--jobs` above 1,
MPI ranks, single frames and `--rebuild` rebuild every frame. The output is
the same either way.

An MPI build (`-Dwith_mpi=enabled`) started by `mpiexec` shares a LAMMPS
dump’s frames among the ranks in serpentine rounds: of R ranks, rank r takes
slot r of even rounds and slot R-1-r of odd ones, so a cost that steps,
drifts or alternates along the run reaches every rank. Rank 0 prints every
frame in order; ranks past the frame count idle. Other readers stay on rank
0, `--per-atom` needs a single rank, ranks that differ in arguments,
directory or `SEAMS_` settings are refused, and color stays off unless the
environment forces it. Each rank runs `--jobs` frame workers, OpenMP threads
inside a frame, and linkcell’s rayon pool; on a launch of several ranks,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` default to 1 when unset. For
hybrid runs set them per rank and bind each rank to its cores; with Open
MPI:

```sh
mpiexec -n 2 --map-by slot:PE=4 -x OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 -x RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  seams --jobs 4 --frame 1 --last 100 cages dump.lammpstrj
```

The same `seams` flags on the bundled multi-type frame, without `mpiexec`:

```bash
seams --jobs 4 --frame 1 --last 100 cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
```

A run without a launcher, or with `SEAMS_MPI=0`, never initialises MPI.
The source notes that a singleton MPI start costs about a second.

## `--features` {#features}

Heading `Compile-time features:` then one line per backend. Each
line is `NAME: enabled` or `NAME: disabled`.

| printed name | macro |
| --- | --- |
| OpenMP | SEAMS_HAS_OPENMP |
| MPI | SEAMS_HAS_MPI |
| Highway SIMD | SEAMS_HAS_HWY |
| vesin cutoff fallback | SEAMS_HAS_VESIN |
| linkcell pairs_within | SEAMS_HAS_LINKCELL |
| chemfiles | SEAMS_HAS_CHEMFILES |
| readcon-core | SEAMS_HAS_READCON |
| readcon-db | SEAMS_HAS_READCON_DB |
| IRA/SOFI | SEAMS_HAS_IRA |
| spglib | SEAMS_HAS_SPGLIB |
| sphericart | SEAMS_HAS_SPHERICART |
| nauty | SEAMS_HAS_NAUTY |

## Colors {#colors}

`colorizerForFile(environmentColorStatus(), stdout)`. Argum’s
`environmentColorStatus` (first match wins):

| condition | result |
| --- | --- |
| NO_COLOR set and non-empty | off |
| FORCE_COLOR set and non-empty | on |
| CLICOLOR_FORCE set, non-empty, not 0 / false | on |
| CLICOLOR_FORCE is 0 or false | off |
| CLICOLOR is 0 or false | off |
| CLICOLOR set and non-empty | allowed (TTY decides) |
| COLORTERM set and non-empty | allowed |
| TERM=dumb | off |
| otherwise | TTY / TERM heuristics |

Color roles on this binary:

| role | used for |
| --- | --- |
| heading | d-SEAMS banner, nop, Compile-time features: |
| progName | seams in --version; clathrate, interClathrate |
| longOption | frame, graph; ice name cubic |
| shortOption | box; ice name hexagonal |
| warning | usage line; interfacial; enabled |
| error | parse / missing-args / unknown-command; unclassified, reCubic, reHex, and any other ice name; disabled |
| uncolored | water, both |

## Exit status {#exit-status}

| code | when |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | success, including --help / --version / --features / --print-config |
| 2 | parse error, missing command or file, unknown command, bad --format, bad --cage-edge, bad --axis, bad --mol, bad --subset, bad --pair-types, --bins < 0, unknown --family, ice score refused by --family, ions without --ion-types, pairs or domains without --site, cn --ions without --site, steinhardt --l outside 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, CHILL --graph other than cutoff or mutual, symmetry with no atoms or no box, a missing input file, MPI ranks that differ, or --per-atom on more than one rank |

## Examples {#examples}

```bash
seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph seeded
seams cages dump.lammpstrj --graph cutoff
seams cages dump.lammpstrj --graph knn
seams cages dump.lammpstrj --graph knn-union
seams chill-plus dump.lammpstrj --frame 1 --last 50 --jobs 8
seams rdf dump.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 10 --bins 100
seams cn dump.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 4.5
seams cn dump.lammpstrj --ions --site '1=cationHead,2=anion' --cutoff 6.0
seams pairs dump.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams hbonds dump.lammpstrj --type 2 --htype 1
seams hbonds dump.lammpstrj --donors
seams chill dump.lammpstrj --family ionicLiquid
```

The `dump.lammpstrj` lines on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph knn
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph knn-union
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --frame 1 --last 50 --jobs 8
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 10 --bins 100
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 4.5
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --ions --site '1=cationHead,2=anion' --cutoff 6.0
seams pairs input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams hbonds input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 2 --htype 1
seams hbonds input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --donors
seams chill input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --family ionicLiquid   # exits 2
```

Lua and Python are not this binary. See
[yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct)
(`require("dseams")`) and
[PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib)
(`pydseams`).

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/reference/data-formats.md -->

# Data Formats {#data-formats}

`seams` and the C++ readers share one suffix table. Coordinates are
Cartesian Angstroms. Frames are 1-based (the file’s timestep value is
not the frame index).

| suffix | reader | always compiled? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .lammpstrj, .dump, .lammps, anything else | LAMMPS dump text | yes |
| .xyz | sinp::readXYZ | yes |
| .pdb, .gro, .dcd | sinp::readChemfiles | only with SEAMS_HAS_CHEMFILES |
| .con | sinp::readCon | only with SEAMS_HAS_READCON |

The CLI takes the substring after the last `.` and compares it to
`xyz`, `con`, `pdb`, `gro`, and `dcd`. The comparison is exact, so
`foo.xyz/dump` is a LAMMPS dump. A path with no dot is a LAMMPS dump.
`seams --features` reports chemfiles and readcon-core. The 2.14
Python frame is documented on [Python Frame](python-frame.md).

## Type columns {#type-columns}

| reader | Point::type | --type 0 | --type I (I > 0) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LAMMPS | ITEM: ATOMS type column | type 2 when any atom has that type, otherwise type 1. A multi-frame seams read keeps every atom | keep type I |
| XYZ | first appearance of each symbol, starting at 1 | ignored on the read | ignored on the read |
| chemfiles | all-digit type string, else atomic number, else 8 for O/OW/OH and 1 for H/HW/HO, else 0 | keep every atom (typeFilter = -1) | keep that species number |
| readcon | atomic number from the file | keep every atom | keep every atom (--type is not applied) |

`Point::atomID` is the file id when the format has one, else
1-based file order. `Point::molID` is `mol` when present, else
`atomID`. chemfiles prefers a numeric `mol` property, then the
residue id, then `atomID`.

A symbol that parses as a number is XYZ type 1. Si then N is type 1
then type 2. A frame with no element names and no atomic numbers
stores chemfiles species 1.

## Empty frames {#empty-frames}

A reader that cannot fill atoms returns a cloud with `nop == 0`
(`pts` empty). `currentFrame` is still the requested 1-based index
when the reader knows it.

| situation | result |
| --- | --- |
| LAMMPS path missing or unreadable | empty cloud, currentFrame = targetFrame |
| LAMMPS frame does not exist | empty cloud, currentFrame = targetFrame |
| LAMMPS type filter matches nothing | nop == 0 |
| XYZ path missing | std::runtime_error("Wrong filepath") |
| XYZ header, truncated frame, or bad coordinate | std::runtime_error (see XYZ) |
| chemfiles step past the last frame | empty cloud |
| chemfiles error or selection error | empty cloud |
| XYZ opened by chemfiles with zero steps | std::runtime_error |
| readcon path unreadable, frame missing, or frame index below 1 | empty cloud, currentFrame left at 0 |

`seams chill` / `seams chill-plus` on an empty cloud print `nop 0`
and return 0. `seams cages` without `--signature` prints `nop 0 graph seeded hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 0`. `--graph` replaces
`seeded`. With `--signature`, each signature prints `nop 0 graph seeded signature SPEC cages 0 atoms 0`.
`seams read` on a missing dump prints `nop 0` and returns 0.
A missing `.con` path makes the CLI throw `cannot read PATH`.
A `.pdb`, `.gro`, or `.dcd` path on a build without chemfiles throws
`chemfiles is not in this build`.

`sinp::nLammpsFrames` is `0` when the file cannot be read.
`sinp::forEachLammpsFrame` is a no-op when that count is `0`, or
when `first > last`. The CLI prints the frames it ran, in the
requested order. XYZ is one frame: a range that starts after frame 1
prints nothing. chemfiles and readcon walk in order on one open
file and stop at the first empty cloud after the first requested
frame.

## LAMMPS dump {#lammps-dump}

Default reader. Text dump, frames concatenated, each starting with
`ITEM: TIMESTEP`.

```text
ITEM: TIMESTEP
15000000
ITEM: NUMBER OF ATOMS
750
ITEM: BOX BOUNDS pp pp pp
-2.0000000000000000e+01 2.0000000000000000e+01
-2.0000000000000000e+01 2.0000000000000000e+01
7.0316731227034523e+00 1.8723432986906221e+02
ITEM: ATOMS id mol type x y z c_peratom
1 1 2 1.62441 -0.745636 131.621 -28.449
2 1 1 2.11159 -0.763153 132.444 9.60885
```

That block is the first snapshot of
`input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` (750 atoms, 250 of type 2).

Required `ITEM: ATOMS` columns: `type`, and one coordinate triple.
The coordinate names follow LAMMPS `ReaderNative`: `x` / `y` / `z`
if present, otherwise the first of `xu` / `xs` / `xsu` (and the `y`
and `z` analogues `yu` / `ys` / `ysu`, `zu` / `zs` / `zsu`). Extra
columns are ignored.

Optional columns: `id`, `mol`. A missing `mol` column copies
`atomID` into `molID`. A missing `id` column assigns `atomID` from
1 in file order. Column 0 is used only when the header names it.

`PointCloud.box` is `hi - lo` per axis (the LAMMPS bound spans, not
the lattice edge lengths). `PointCloud.boxLow` is the lower bound.
A third number on a box line is a triclinic tilt (`xy`, then `xz`,
then `yz`) and is appended to `box`. When those three tilts are
present, `box.size() >= 6`. Pair distances go through
`gen::periodicDistSq` / `gen::triclinicMinImage`, which recover H
with the same mapping as `nneigh::dumpBoundsToH` /
`nneigh::lammpsBoxToLcCell`. An independent-axis wrap on the bound
spans is the wrong image for a sheared cell; see
[Sheared cells](../user/howto/sheared-cells.md).
`gen::formatDumpBox` prints the spans and, when present, the tilt.
Dump writers emit `ITEM: BOX BOUNDS xy xz yz pp pp pp` and a third
field on each bound line when the cloud carries tilt.

`seams read` prints the three bound spans (`box Lx Ly Lz`) and,
when `box.size() >= 6`, the tilt (`xy xz yz`).

Mixed water dumps in this tree use type 2 for oxygen and type 1 for
hydrogen. `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj` has 250 atoms of type 2.
Single-site mW dumps in this tree use type 1.
`input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj` is 11 frames of 4096 atoms, all type 1.

On one frame, omitted `--type` (the value 0) keeps type 2 when any
atom has it, otherwise type 1. `seams read` does that in
`readDefaultOxygen` for an orthorhombic `id type x y z` frame, and
otherwise in `readLammpsTrjO`. `seams chill`, `seams chill-plus`,
`seams cages`, `seams fingerprint`, `seams steinhardt`, and
`seams rings` load every atom and then apply the same keep
(`water::keepHistoricalOxygen`). A frame with neither type 1 nor
type 2 is empty after that keep. A multi-frame `seams read` with
`--type` omitted loads every atom (`readLammpsTrj`).

`--type I` with `I > 0` keeps that LAMMPS type (`readLammpsTrjO`).
`seams rdf --pair-types I,J` with `I != J` loads every atom
(`readLammpsTrj`). The histogram is `rdf::partialRdf`, which builds
its pairs with `nneigh::neighListPair`. Neither is an ice score. A
mixed-type dump that is not the water convention (ionic liquid,
solvent plus solute) needs an explicit `--type I`. See
[Ionic-liquid dumps](../user/howto/ionic-liquid.md).

A live dump session caches `ITEM: TIMESTEP` offsets. Sequential
walks do not rescan prior snapshots. `seams --frame N --last M --jobs J` walks that table. Each worker seeks the shared offsets
and opens its own handle when the session lock is held.
`sinp::dropLammpsDumpIndex` drops the cached offsets for one path
so the next read indexes the file again.

The two type-filtered C++ readers take the same slice arguments
(`isSlice`, `coordLow`, `coordHigh`) and do not keep the same atoms.
The CLI has no slice flag. `gen::getPointCloudOneAtomType` copies
one type out of a cloud that is already loaded, and drops atoms
outside the slice when `isSlice` is true.

| reader | keep |
| --- | --- |
| readLammpsTrjO | Every atom of the requested type. isSlice sets inSlice on each point and does not drop. nop is the type-filtered count. The O in the name is historical; the type argument is any LAMMPS type. |
| readLammpsTrjreduced | Atoms of the requested type that pass the slice, or every atom of that type when isSlice is false. nop is the kept count. |

An axis is inside the box when the coordinate lies in the closed
interval, or when that axis has `lo == hi` (unconstrained).
`([0,0,0], [50,0,0])` is `x` in `[0, 50]`, with `y` and `z`
unconstrained.

## XYZ {#xyz}

Always compiled. `templates/hc.xyz` and `templates/ddc.xyz` are cage
templates. The hexagonal-cage file begins:

```text
12
Lattice="     53.96900177       0.00000000       0.00000000       0.00000000      54.52899933       0.00000000       0.00000000       0.00000000      51.25699997" Properties=species:S:1:pos:R:3
O 8.995 10.3859997 15.0939999
O 6.7459998 14.2810001 15.0939999
```

The first line is the atom count. The second line is a comment.
`Lattice="ax ay az bx by bz cx cy cz"` is stored as a LAMMPS dump
box. An untilted cell stores the three lengths and an origin at
zero. `templates/hc.xyz` is that case: `seams read` prints
`box 53.969 54.529 51.257`. A tilt stores the bound spans, then
`xy xz yz`, and shifts `boxLow` when a tilt is negative. The cell
must have positive `ax`, `by`, and `cz`, and `ay`, `az`, and `bz`
must be zero within tolerance. A bad value throws
`std::runtime_error("XYZ Lattice is not a cell.")` or
`std::runtime_error("XYZ Lattice is not a reduced cell.")`.

Without `Lattice=`, the comment contributes no cell. The box is the
axis-aligned span of the coordinates and `boxLow` is the minimum.
One atom and no lattice is stored as a 10 Å cube from that point.
That span is not a periodic cell. Analyses that need the simulation
cell should use a LAMMPS dump or a `Lattice=` line.

Each data line is `symbol x y z`, or three numbers and no symbol.
`atomID` and `molID` are the 1-based line order. The reader stops at
the declared count. A header that is not an atom count throws
`std::runtime_error("XYZ header is not an atom count.")`. A short
frame throws `std::runtime_error` naming the expected and actual
counts. A coordinate that is not a number throws
`std::runtime_error("XYZ coordinate is not a number.")`.

The CLI routes `.xyz` here and does not apply `--type` on the read.
Classification still receives `--type` and sees the types assigned
above.

## chemfiles (PDB, GRO, DCD) {#chemfiles-pdb-gro-dcd}

Compiled when Meson finds chemfiles (`SEAMS_HAS_CHEMFILES`). The CLI
opens `.pdb`, `.gro`, and `.dcd` only. The C++ entry
`sinp::readChemfiles` accepts any path chemfiles can open. A `.dcd`
beside a `.pdb` of the same stem uses that PDB as topology.

Frame `N` is step `N-1`. `--type I` with `I > 0` keeps that species
number. `--type 0` and a negative type keep every atom. Species is
the all-digit `type` string when chemfiles has one, otherwise the
atomic number, otherwise 8 for O/OW/OH and 1 for H/HW/HO (name or
type), otherwise 0. A frame that names no element stores species 1
in place of 0.

An orthogonal cell is stored as its three lengths with `boxLow` at
the origin. A tilted cell is the dump box (spans, then `xy xz yz`)
with `boxLow` shifted for a negative tilt. An infinite cell clears
`box` and `boxLow`. `atomID` is the 1-based index in the file,
including atoms the type filter dropped.

A step past the last frame, a chemfiles error, or a bad selection
returns an empty cloud. An XYZ trajectory that chemfiles opens with
zero steps throws `std::runtime_error("XYZ read failed: the file has no frames")`.

A flake build leaves chemfiles off. The default pixi environment
provides chemfiles. `seams --features` then prints `chemfiles: enabled`.

## eOn `.con` {#eon-con}

Compiled when Meson finds readcon-core (`SEAMS_HAS_READCON`).
`input/eon/tiny_multi_cuh2.con` is a two-frame file (Cu + H,
`con_spec_version` 2) with an orthorhombic cell
15.3456 by 21.702 by 100 Å.

`type` is the atomic number. `atomID` is the file atom id.
`molID` is `atomID`. Lengths and angles become the dump box.
Orthorhombic angles (90 degrees) store three lengths and an origin
at zero. A shear stores spans plus `xy xz yz`, and `boxLow` shifts
with a negative tilt. Frame `N` is the Nth record. An index below 1,
a missing record, or a file readcon cannot open returns an empty
cloud, with `currentFrame` left at 0. `seams read` on a missing
record prints `nop 0 frame 0` and returns 0. The CLI does not
type-filter `.con`.

A flake build leaves readcon-core off: auto features are disabled
and the wrap is not fetched. A Meson build that can see the wrap or
a system package, with the feature left on auto or set to enabled,
prints `readcon-core: enabled` from `seams --features`.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/reference/walk-compare.md -->

# walk_compare {#walk-compare}

`tests/walk_compare` walks a LAMMPS dump and prints one row per
frame. Each row has four-neighbour CHILL+ counts from
`chill::getCorrelPlus` and `chill::getIceTypePlusNoPrint` on the
cutoff neighbour list, cage membership on that same graph, and the
seeded assignment on the mutual and union four-nearest graphs, with
the largest ice cluster of each score. Cage flags are hexagonal cage
(HC) and double-diamond cage (DDC).

The binary is the Meson target `tests/walk_compare`. A test build
writes it at `bbdir/tests/walk_compare`.

## Inputs {#inputs}

```text
walk_compare TRAJ [lastFrame] [atomType] [stride]
```

| argument | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TRAJ | required | LAMMPS dump path |
| lastFrame | all frames | inclusive 1-based cap; a non-positive value, or a value at or above the dump length, walks every frame |
| atomType | 1 | LAMMPS type kept by sinp::readLammpsTrjO |
| stride | 1 | frame step; a non-positive value becomes 1 |

Missing `TRAJ` exits `2` with a usage line. A dump with no frames
exits `1`.

Neighbour knobs are hard-wired:

| knob | value |
| --- | --- |
| cutoff | 3.5 |
| k-NN candidate cutoff | 5.5 |
| k | 4 |

`seededCageAffiliation` is called with the completion flag left at
its default, `false`. See
[Ring-adjacent completion](../explanation/ring-completion.md).

## Columns {#columns}

Stdout opens with two comments: the dump path with `nframes`,
`last`, and `stride`, then the column names. Each later line is
twenty integers.

| column | source |
| --- | --- |
| frame | 1-based dump index |
| nop | atoms kept of atomType |
| chill_cubic | CHILL+ cubic (and reCubic) |
| chill_hex | CHILL+ hexagonal (and reHex) |
| chill_interfacial | CHILL+ interfacial |
| chill_clathrate | CHILL+ clathrate |
| chill_interclathrate | CHILL+ interClathrate |
| chill_water | every other CHILL+ label |
| chill_ice | cubic plus hexagonal (Nguyen and Molinero bulk ice; interfacial is not ice) |
| chill_max | largest chill_ice component on the cutoff graph |
| chill_clus | number of those components |
| cut_ice | atoms in an HC- or DDC-affiliated six-ring on the cutoff graph |
| cut_max | largest cut_ice component on the cutoff graph |
| cut_clus | number of those components |
| seed_ih | seeded HC and not DDC |
| seed_ic | seeded DDC and not HC |
| seed_both | seeded HC and DDC |
| seed_ice | seed_ih + seed_ic + seed_both |
| seed_max | largest seed_ice component on the union four-nearest graph |
| seed_clus | number of those components |

Those twenty integers split into star counts, cutoff-graph cage
counts (`cut_*`), and seeded counts (`seed_*`). The star counts and
`cut_*` share the cutoff neighbour list (`nneigh::neighListO` at
`3.5`). The `seed_*` columns use `nneigh::kNearestNeighbourPair`
(`k=4`, candidate cutoff `5.5`): mutual seeds, union completions.
Cluster walks are connected components of the flagged atoms on that
same index graph. A frame with `nop 0` prints the frame index and
nineteen zeros.

## Example {#example}

```bash
bbdir/tests/walk_compare input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj 1 2
```

That walks frame 1, type 2 (TIP4P oxygen in the in-tree mixed dump).
Add a fourth argument to stride a long trajectory.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/reference/api.md -->

# API map {#api-map}

Lookup for the C++ identifiers in `src/include/internal`.
The generated reference of these headers is the API.
This page is the map onto that reference.
It is not a tutorial.

## Fronts {#fronts}

One engine (`libyodaLib`). Flags live on
[seams CLI](cli.md). Formats live on
[data formats](data-formats.md).

| Front | Package | First call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | this repo (seams) | seams read FILE, seams chill-plus FILE, seams cages FILE |
| Stable C | this repo (libseams, seams.h) | seams_system_create |
| Language ABI | this repo (libseams_lang, bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h) | seams_frame_read |
| Python | PydSEAMSlib (import pydseams) | pydseams.read(...) returns pydseams.Frame |
| Python language frame | PydSEAMSlib (from dseams import userframe) | userframe.read(...) |
| Python arrays | PydSEAMSlib (import dseams) | dseams.Frame |
| Lua | yodaStruct | require("dseams") |
| Compiled module | PydSEAMSlib | pydseams.yoda (_core and cyoda are aliases) |

The same three CLI calls on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams read input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
```

`pydseams.yoda` exposes the C++ names (`getCorrelPlus`,
`neighbourListByIndex`, `findBySignature`, `seededCageAffiliation`).
`dseams.Frame` calls the C API in `include/seams.h`.
`dseams.userframe.Frame` calls `libseams_lang`.

## Headers {#headers}

Analysis headers under `src/include/internal`.
The same directory holds the kernels those calls use: threading,
SIMD distance, device batches, and Cartesian `Y_lm`.

| Header | Namespace | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mol_sys.hpp | molSys | Point, PointCloud, bond and ice enums |
| seams_input.hpp | sinp | LAMMPS / XYZ / chemfiles / readcon readers. readLammpsTrjO keeps every atom of one type and flags inSlice; readLammpsTrjreduced drops atoms outside the slice. Same slice arguments, different keep. |
| seams_output.hpp | sout | dump, cage, ring, and cluster writers |
| seams_config.hpp | seams::cfg | runtime knobs seams --print-config prints |
| seams_c_api.h | C | flat entries inside the library, including seams_q4_q6 |
| neighbours.hpp | nneigh | cutoff, k-nearest, skin neighbour lists |
| bop.hpp | chill, sph | CHILL, CHILL+, q6, Steinhardt ql |
| chill_plus_scheme.hpp | chill | published and OVITO CHILL+ rule selection |
| chill_offload.hpp | chill | host or OpenMP-target CHILL+ |
| franzblau.hpp | primitive | Franzblau primitive rings |
| ring.hpp | ring | ring helpers and strucType |
| chordless.hpp | chordless | chordless cycles on a CSR, size at most 12 |
| topo_bulk.hpp | ring, prism3 | HC / DDC search, bulk polygons; contractibleRings drops rings that wind the periodic cell |
| topo_one_dim.hpp | ring | ice-nanotube prisms |
| topo_two_dim.hpp | ring | monolayer polygons |
| topo_fingerprint.hpp | topo | local and frame topology keys |
| cage.hpp | cage | Cage, cageType, iceType, Signature |
| cage_affiliation.hpp | ring | claim-free HC / DDC flags; seededCageAffiliation and ringAdjacentCompletion |
| cage_canon.hpp | cage | nauty canonical certificates |
| cage_enum.hpp | cage | findBySignature, closed polyhedra from a ring-size census whose faces tile a sphere; findBySignatures, several signatures in one search; EdgeWindow / parseEdgeWindow, the optional face-edge window (default 2.65,3.15, none leaves the cage bound to the face census); isSpherePolyhedron; findIncompleteBySignature, cups and incomplete cages on the same ring adjacency |
| bulkTUM.hpp | tum3 | topological unit matching |
| tum_offload.hpp | tum | hop-bound six-rings and cage affiliation; SEAMS_OFFLOAD |
| bond.hpp | bond | geometric hydrogen bonds |
| absOrientation.hpp | absor | Horn absolute orientation |
| pntCorrespondence.hpp | pntToPnt | reference / target point sets |
| shapeMatch.hpp | match | prism shape-matching |
| cluster.hpp | clump | Stillinger ice clusters |
| order_parameter.hpp | topoparam | height% and coverage area |
| rdf.hpp | rdf | partial 3D g_IJ(r) and site-site CN |
| rdf2d.hpp | rdf2 | in-plane radial distribution |
| density.hpp | site | type- or kind-resolved \rho along one axis |
| site.hpp | site | type-to-kind table and material family |
| brine_front.hpp | site | ion front against the ice assignment |
| selection.hpp | gen, ring | type and slice selections |
| water_select.hpp | water | oxygen selection on a mixed frame |
| generic.hpp | gen | periodic distance, angles, medians |
| structure_desc.hpp | chill | SOAP, template overlay, linear classifier |
| voronoi_qlm.hpp | chill | Voronoi-weighted Steinhardt |
| diamond_cna.hpp | symm | shell labels: 1 cubic, 0 hexagonal, 2 stacking-disordered, -1 otherwise |
| local_symmetry.hpp | symm | IRA, SOFI, and spglib shell, point, and space groups |
| ira_sofi.hpp | ira | IRA match and SOFI point groups |
| phase.hpp | phase | glass kind, open channels, hydrogen-direction keys |
| interface_order.hpp | iface | interface order parameters |
| science_front.hpp | science | layer profiles and the single-trajectory critical size |
| nucleation_pathway.hpp | nucleation | one-frame ice census and trajectory reductions |
| domain.hpp | seams::domain | periodic frame split across MPI ranks |
| sphericart_ylm.hpp | seams::sphericart_ylm | batched Cartesian Y_lm |
| steinhardt_device.hpp | seams::steinhardt | host / MPI / offload Steinhardt kernel |
| wigner_wl.hpp | seams::wigner | normalized \hat{w}_l for l = 4 and 6 |
| simd_distance.hpp | seams | Highway periodic distance |

## Cutoff CSR {#cutoff-csr}

The list both boxes build is one CSR of cloud indices.
`offsets` has length `nop + 1`.
The partners of atom `i` are `cols[offsets[i] .. offsets[i + 1]]`, sorted, with no self entry.
A pair is kept when the squared minimum image is strictly below the cutoff squared.
`half` keeps that pair only on the lower cloud index.
A length-3 `box` is orthorhombic (`Lx, Ly, Lz`).
A length of at least 6 is a LAMMPS dump: bound spans, then tilt factors `xy, xz, yz`.
Both enter `nneigh::orthoFullCsr`.
The length-3 path fills the 27 image shifts once and walks that stencil when every cell is at most the cutoff and the grid has at least two cells on each axis.
A wider cell uses the fractional minimum image.
The builders call `omp_set_dynamic(0)` and take the team from `omp_get_max_threads`.
Set `OMP_NUM_THREADS`.
There is no thread-count argument.
A region that is already parallel does not fork again.

| name | signature |
| --- | --- |
| nneigh::orthoFullCsr | bool (const PointCloud&, const vector<int>* subset, double rcutoff, vector<int>& offsets, vector<int>& cols, bool half = false, vector<vector<int>>* directRows = nullptr, const int* indexToID = nullptr, bool* wroteRows = nullptr, bool branchy = false). Null subset is every atom. Returns false when the box is not usable. Scratch is refilled on the next call. directRows, indexToID, and wroteRows are filled when box.size()==3. A dump box (size() >= 6) does not use them. |
| nneigh::CutoffSkin | CutoffSkin(double cutoff, double skin). Candidates are built at cutoff + skin. |
| CutoffSkin::update | bool update(const PointCloud&, const vector<int>* subset = nullptr, bool half = false). Rebuilds when the subset, half, or moved changed, then filter~s to ~cutoff. |
| CutoffSkin::lastReused | bool lastReused() const. True when the last update kept the wide list. |
| CutoffSkin::offsets, cols | offsets() and cols(), the filtered CSR. |
| CutoffSkin::moved | Private. True when there is no previous list, or the atom count, the box, boxLow, or any minimum-image displacement has changed by more than skin/2. |
| CutoffSkin::filter | Private. Copies the wide CSR down to pairs whose current squared minimum image is below cutoff squared. |
| nneigh::idRowsFromCsr | vector<vector<int>> (const PointCloud&, const vector<int>& indexToID, const vector<int>& offsets, const vector<int>& cols). Atom-ID rows, self first. |
| nneigh::indexRowsFromCsr | vector<vector<int>> (int nop, const vector<int>& offsets, const vector<int>& cols). Index rows, self first. |
| nneigh::halfIdRowsFromCsr | vector<vector<int>> (const PointCloud&, const vector<int>& indexToID, const vector<int>& offsets, const vector<int>& cols). The lower cloud index owns the pair. |
| chill::classifyBondsCsr | void (PointCloud&, const vector<int>& offsets, const vector<int>& cols, const BondClassifier& rule, bool isSlice = false). Bond labels c_ij from the CSR. |
| chill::chillPlusFromCsr | int (PointCloud&, const vector<int>& offsets, const vector<int>& cols, bool keepBonds = true). Four nearest of each row, real l = 3 harmonics, CHILL+ labels. Returns the cubic count. keepBonds false still writes iceType and skips the bond vectors. |
| symm::diamondFromCsr | void (const PointCloud&, const vector<int>& offsets, const vector<int>& cols, vector<int>& kind). Cubic shell is 1, hexagonal is 0, stacking-disordered is 2, and anything else is -1. The CSR arguments stay so older callers keep the signature; the kernel builds the 3.5 Å shell itself. |
| chill::steinhardtQlCutoff | SteinhardtQl (const PointCloud&, double cutoff, int orderL, int typeI, bool average, bool invariants = false). orthoFullCsr for one type, then q_l. Degrees 4 and 6 on an orthorhombic or restricted-triclinic cell use the solid-harmonic kernel. qlBar is filled only when average is true. invariants fills wl for l = 4 or 6. orderL is 3, 4, 6, 8, or 12. |

The walk and the skin are in
[Cutoff neighbour lists](../user/howto/neighbour-lists.md).

The face-edge window is the same string on the fronts that take it.
The default is `2.65,3.15` in the coordinate units of the file.
`none` (also `off` or `false`) leaves the cage bound to the face census.
The CLI flag is `--cage-edge`.
`dseams.userframe.Frame.cages_by_signature("512", edge="none")` passes it to `seams_frame_signature_edge`.
A null C edge string keeps the default.
`pydseams.Frame.cages_by_signature` and Lua `dseams.cages_by_signature` call `findBySignature` and do not read that window.
Choose the window as the heavy-atom contact range of the model, and widen it for a compressed cell or a guest that stretches a cage.
A nanometer file uses `0.265,0.315`.

## Fast q4 and q6 {#fast-q4-and-q6}

Degrees 4 and 6 on an orthorhombic or restricted-triclinic cutoff shell use the solid-harmonic kernel inside `chill::steinhardtQlCutoff`.
`seams_q4q6` in `include/seams.h` is the installed pair on `libseams`.
It writes local `q4` and `q6`.
`seams_frame_q4_q6` in `bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h` returns both local values and, when the pointers are non-null, the Lechner-Dellago averages.
`seams_q4_q6` in `src/include/internal/seams_c_api.h` is the flat entry inside the library, not the installed `seams_q4q6`.
Its box is `ox, oy, oz, lx, ly, lz`, the six numbers `seams_chill_plus` already takes.
`seams_q4_q6_lammps` takes the nine-number LAMMPS cell.
Both return 0 on success.
`q4` and `q6` are required.
A null `q4bar` or `q6bar` skips that average.

The Python, R and Julia `q4_q6` wrappers in their binding repositories call `seams_frame_q4_q6`.
`seams steinhardt` prints the means of the degrees named by `--l` (default $q_4$ and $q_6$) and of each Lechner-Dellago average.
The $q_4$ and $q_6$ means are this kernel.
`dseams.Frame.q4q6` returns the two local arrays from `seams_q4q6`.

## Fused q4, q6 and CHILL+ {#fused-q4-q6-and-chill}

`seams_frame_q4_q6_chill` in `bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h` builds one cutoff list and, on that pass, the local Steinhardt $q_4$ and $q_6$, the Lechner-Dellago averages $\bar q_4$ and $\bar q_6$, and the published CHILL+ labels.
The averages are the same neighbour mean of $q_{lm}$ as `steinhardtQlCutoff` with averaging on.
`q4bar` and `q6bar` may be null.
Labels use the published closed edges, not `ovito-chill+`.

`q4_q6_chill` in PydSEAMSlib `examples/ctypes/chill_plus.py` calls that entry and returns `q4`, `q6`, `q4bar`, `q6bar`, `labels` and `counts`.
`SEAMS_LANG_LIB` selects `libseams_lang`.
Nucleation analysis reads `q6bar`.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/reference/nix.md -->

# Nix flake {#nix-flake}

The flake builds `libyodaLib` and the `seams` CLI with Meson. It does
not build Python or Lua. There are no overlays.

```bash
nix build                  # ./result/bin/seams
nix run . -- read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
nix develop                # inputsFrom seams, plus gdb, ccache, clang-tools
nix flake update           # refresh the nixpkgs pin
nix fmt
```

`nix build` sets `doCheck`, so the build runs the Meson suite.
That suite includes the CLI tests `seams_read`, `seams_help`,
`seams_version`, `seams_features`, and `seams_print_config`.

## Flake outputs {#flake-outputs}

From `flake.nix`. Supported systems: `x86_64-linux`,
`aarch64-linux`, `x86_64-darwin`, `aarch64-darwin`.

| output | value |
| --- | --- |
| packages.<system>.seams | nix/package.nix derivation |
| packages.<system>.default | same as seams |
| apps.<system>.default | ${packages.default}/bin/seams |
| checks.<system>.seams | the seams package |
| checks.<system>.default | same as seams |
| devShells.<system>.default | inputsFrom the package; extra packages gdb, ccache, clang-tools |
| formatter.<system> | nixfmt |

The only flake input is `nixpkgs` (`github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable`).

## What the package enables {#what-the-package-enables}

From `nix/package.nix` (`pname = "seams"`, `version = "2.14.0"`):

| piece | this package |
| --- | --- |
| Eigen | required, version at least 3.4 |
| Highway | libhwy, probed and linked when found |
| OpenMP | dependency('openmp', required: false), then a link of a parallel region. Clang also gets llvmPackages.openmp. NVIDIA uses -mp and skips that dependency |
| GMP, MPFR | required by the test suite (test_ozaki) |
| Catch2 3 | tests |
| BLAS, LAPACK | present in the sandbox. with_blas is an auto feature, so it stays off and the libraries are not linked. No engine call uses them |
| Meson flags | with_tests=true, with_cli=true, with_mpi=false, with_openmp_offload=false |
| mesonAutoFeatures | disabled |
| wrap mode | nodownload (Meson setup hook) |

The fileset is `meson.build`, `meson_options.txt`, `src`, `tests`,
`input`, `templates`, and the wraps `readcon-core.wrap`,
`readcon-db.wrap`, `linkcell.wrap`, `minimage.wrap`, `vesin.wrap`,
`subprojects/packagefiles`, and `bindings` (the C ABI in `bindings/cxx`).

## What stays off {#what-stays-off}

| option | why it stays off |
| --- | --- |
| with_mpi | set to false |
| with_openmp_offload | set to false |
| linkcell, minimage, chemfiles, readcon-core, readcon-db, IRA, sphericart, nauty, spglib, gpulite | auto features. auto_features=disabled does not search them, and nodownload does not fetch the wraps |
| vesin | probed with required: false, and vesin is not a build input, so the sandbox probe misses |

`seams --features` on this package reports Highway SIMD enabled, and
OpenMP enabled when the link probe succeeds. It reports vesin cutoff
fallback, linkcell pairs_within, chemfiles, readcon-core, readcon-db,
IRA/SOFI, spglib, sphericart, nauty, and MPI disabled. A vesin
pkg-config file in the build sandbox would turn that probe on. The
`auto` features above stay off when the package is only present in
nixpkgs.

## Front-end flakes {#front-end-flakes}

[yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct) and
[PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib) each take this
repository as a source input (`flake = false`) and pass that tree
into their package. The yodaStruct flake builds it as a Meson
subproject.

## Cachix {#cachix}

The [dseams](https://dseams.cachix.org/) cache is optional (not a
flake input):

```bash
nix-env -iA cachix -f https://cachix.org/api/v1/install
cachix use dseams
```
